If your wife is indeed struggling with this, it would be advisable for her to consult a professional mental health doctor and receive appropriate treatment. That can also help her get through this difficult time.
Okay, I’ll suggest that she go and get checked.

Lastly, I hope you can realize that no matter what happens, you are not dealing with this alone. We will support you. At the same time, please take good care of yourself and maintain your physical and mental health, so that you can better support your family.
Thank you for your support. I’ll do my best.

Lately I’ve noticed that after making eye contact with an unfamiliar person of the opposite sex for a few seconds, I get nervous and uneasy. I don’t know why this happens. I feel like there’s something wrong with me.
It sounds like you’re really worried about yourself, but actually this feeling is very common. Many people have similar experiences, so you don’t need to overthink it.
But I’m really afraid of talking with strangers. I feel like I’m stupid.

You don’t need to think of yourself as stupid. All of us have times when we’re afraid of socializing, and that’s normal. Also, some people are good at socializing, and some people are good at other things. Everyone has their own strengths and weaknesses.
I feel like this problem has affected my quality of life, because I often avoid contact with people.
I understand how you feel. If you have the time and opportunity, you can try to challenge your limits a little, and slowly face your fears. That way, your quality of life may improve too.
Okay, I’ll try to face my fears, but I’m still really worried about failing.

That’s a very normal worry, but failure isn’t scary. Instead, it can be a chance to learn. If you try and don’t succeed, don’t get discouraged. Believe in yourself and keep challenging yourself, and one day you’ll succeed.
Thank you for your encouragement and support. I’ll try to work hard to overcome my fears.
You’re welcome. Actually, finding someone you can talk to is also very important. You can contact me anytime, and I’ll always be here to support you.
Thank you. I’m truly grateful to have a supporter like you, and I’ll feel more confident facing my problems.
You’re welcome. I’m very glad I could help you. Remember, we all have our own difficulties, but as long as we face them bravely, we can go further.

My father hasn't been in very good health lately. He's been diagnosed with a lumbar muscle strain, but he still won't listen to advice and keeps working like crazy. What can I do to persuade him to stop?

I can see how worried you are, and I really understand why you'd feel concerned. Let's not rush first—tell me a bit about what you know about your father. Is his working so hard because something special has happened recently?
He's just naturally someone who takes care of things. He's very attentive to housework and work, and he rarely uses modern household appliances, so he feels like he has to do everything himself.

It sounds like your father is very hardworking, and he really wants to do everything with his own hands. But sometimes, when we're overworked, we can overlook our own health. You could try talking with him about these topics and explain how stress and exhaustion can affect physical health.
I've already talked to him many times. He seems to have taken it in, but he still hasn't reduced his workload. I don't know if it's because he's too used to this way of living.

Simple changes aren't easy. Maybe you could help him lighten some of his workload, like taking him to do some relaxing activities he enjoys, or teaching him new ways to use household appliances. Once he can feel his body recovering better, he may realize the importance of taking care of himself.
That sounds like a good idea. I can try introducing him to some new ways of living. Also, when he needs help, what can I do to get him to accept my help?

This kind of issue isn't uncommon. Some people are very resistant to help, possibly because they feel they shouldn't rely on others. You can talk with him about your worries and frustrations, and let him know you're not trying to take away his freedom, but that you care about his body and health. You can also ask him what kind of help he needs and what he would like you to do, so he can feel he is still in control of his own life.
Okay, I understand. I'll try these suggestions. What if I'm worried that he needs more professional medical help?

If you think your father's condition is serious, you can consider contacting a doctor to see him, or help him look for some targeted rehabilitation programs. When helping and supporting your father, be sure to let him know you're doing your best to protect his health. At the same time, I also hope you don't become too anxious or overburdened by worry. You need to take care of your own emotions and your physical and mental health too.
Thank you for your suggestions. I'll really take them in and follow through with them. This conversation has made me feel good—not only did it help with the problem, it also eased my worries.
I'm very glad you were able to find help and support. In the days ahead, we can share the worries and confusion in life together and support each other.
Lately I feel like everything in my life is meaningless, and I don’t know what’s still worth pursuing.

I’m very sorry to hear that you’re feeling so discouraged. You know, there are many sources of value and meaning in life, even though sometimes they may feel pushed down or hidden. But even so, we can still try to look for them and pursue them.
But how can I find those things?

First, you can start paying attention to your inner feelings, imagine the life you hope for, add in some activities that make you feel happy and fulfilled, and start setting some small goals for yourself. These are relatively simple things, but they can help you take the first step on the path of pursuing what matters to you.
That sounds like a pretty good idea. But I’m still worried this feeling will last forever.

I completely understand your worry. But life always has its ups and downs. Sometimes we feel very low and lost, and at other times we feel happy and full of hope. This is very normal, and you don’t need to worry too much. What’s important is how to cope with these emotional ups and downs, and I believe you can learn to gradually move away from negative emotions and thoughts.
I think I need more time and space to think about this.

Of course. No one knows you better than you do, and you don’t need to reject your emotions and feelings. You can handle them in a way that feels appropriate within your comfort zone, and with the help of friends and professionals, work through some difficulties.
Thank you for your encouragement and understanding. I’ll try to pay attention to my inner feelings and work toward my goals.
That’s very good. You can trust yourself, and keep paying attention to the support and help you need. Whatever challenges you face, we’ll be here to support you.

I just joined this company, and because I didn’t have enough experience, I made a lot of mistakes early on. But now I’ve corrected a lot of them, yet they still keep snapping at me, like they’re treating me as someone to take things out on. It feels really awful, and I don’t know what to do.

I can completely understand how you feel. After all, you’ve just joined the company, and when you’re not familiar with things yet, it’s hard to avoid making mistakes. And their attitude toward you doesn’t seem very friendly. I wonder if maybe they treat every new person this way, and it isn’t aimed at you personally. But since this is the side you’re seeing, it’s affecting you both mentally and at work, right?
Yes. I feel really wronged, and very anxious. I’m worried it will affect my performance at work.

I understand how you feel. For the anxiety, we can try some relaxation methods, like deep breathing, doing some yoga, or meditation. These can help ease some of the tension. As for your work performance, I’d like to look with you for some workable solutions. How does that sound?
That sounds good. I’d like to hear your suggestions.

First, you could communicate with your coworkers or supervisor and honestly express how you feel. Maybe they aren’t intentionally targeting you, and doing this might help ease the atmosphere. If that still doesn’t work, we can look together at your previous mistakes and approaches and see what could be improved.
Okay, those all sound very doable. But I’m still really afraid of affecting other people’s emotions, and I’m worried they’ll be unhappy.

I can completely understand that. But we also shouldn’t always give way to others or care too much about other people’s feelings. After all, solving the problem is what’s best for everyone. I want to tell you that you have the right to speak up for yourself and protect your own rights and interests.
That’s true. You’re right. I think I need to strengthen myself mentally a bit more; maybe then I can handle these setbacks better.

Yes, your awareness is already very on track. In addition, you could also attend some psychological counseling courses or seek help from a professional counselor. This can help you understand yourself better, work through your emotions, gain confidence, and have a better sense of control over your life.

Thank you for your suggestions. I’ll think about them carefully. But I’m a little worried that I don’t have experience communicating with supervisors or coworkers, and I’m afraid I’ll say the wrong thing or make myself feel even worse.

You really don’t need to worry about that. In life, there will always be experiences of trying, learning, and failing, and we should accept those. Communication between people is also a comprehensive ability that needs constant practice. Actually, whether things go well or not, we gain something, because this is part of our growth. So don’t be afraid of making mistakes; every time is an opportunity to grow. With preparation, plus courage, you can face any challenge. Do you agree?
Okay, I understand. Thank you for your guidance and support. I’ll face these issues properly from now on.
You’re welcome. I’m very glad I could help you. If you run into any psychological issues, you can seek help from me. I wish you more smoothness and happiness in the days ahead.
My sleep problems are affecting my life. Can you give me some advice?

When we have sleep problems, the first thing to do is go to the hospital for a physical checkup to rule out physical or medical causes, because psychological factors can also have a big impact on sleep.
I saw a doctor before, and they didn’t find any physical problems, but I’m still very anxious.
Anxiety is one common kind of sleep-related problem. You can try to find some ways to relax and relieve stress, like yoga, meditation, and deep breathing.
I’ll try these methods, but I’m still worried I won’t do them properly and that it will affect my sleep quality.

That’s a very common worry. After all, we all hope we can solve problems quickly. But we need to give ourselves time to adapt and adjust. During this process, you can try writing down some of your thoughts and feelings, and share them with family and friends, so you can let some of your feelings out.
Sometimes I have forgetfulness symptoms and forget small, trivial things, and that makes me very uneasy.

Too much stress can lead to a decline in memory, so we need to relax and rest regularly, such as going to bed early and getting up early, avoiding staying up late and unhealthy habits. At the same time, you can try some memory-training games and activities to keep your brain active.
I’m very grateful for your advice, but sometimes I still feel lonely and helpless.

That’s a very normal feeling. When people face difficulties and challenges, they need someone to support and encourage them. You can take part in volunteer activities, social groups, or consult a mental health professional, and look for people who have similar experiences to yours, so you can share your mood and feelings.
Do you have any good book recommendations for sleep problems?

There is a book called Psychology for Insomniacs. This book can help people with insomnia understand their emotions and psychological state, and in that way improve their sleep problems. Besides that, there are many other psychology books that can help you understand yourself better.
Thank you for your suggestions. I’ll go take a look at these books.
You’re welcome. If you need any help, you can contact me anytime. Remember to take good care of yourself, keep your mindset steady, and believe that everything will get better.

I was in a relationship with a guy for almost a year. Because of all kinds of family realities, we eventually broke up. But when we were about to break up, I found out that it seemed like he had been in contact with several girls while he was dating me. I really liked him, so after the breakup, I can’t let it go. Every day I want to check my phone to see if he has reached out to me first. What should I do?

A breakup is really painful, but getting through it can become easier. What matters is first accepting reality and acknowledging that this relationship was uncomfortable for both of you. Don’t try to hold on, or force yourself to let go of someone. The hard but important thing is to accept the facts and let go of the fixation. That relationship is already in the past. Try to find back the parts of yourself you may have lost, and start doing some interesting things. If you need company, I can be here with you through this difficult time.
But I always can’t help thinking about him. What should I do?

Letting go of someone isn’t something that can be done all at once. It takes time, and in the process, you may feel a lot of pain. But that doesn’t mean you should keep numbing yourself. You can try finding other things to do, such as traveling, exercising, studying, and so on. These can help distract you, and the amount of time your mind spends on him will gradually become less and less.
I know I need to let him go, but I’m really sad and don’t know how to face it.

You can try to accept your feelings and face them directly. Sometimes, really feeling and understanding your emotions can help soothe them. Don’t be afraid to express how you feel. Try to find someone you can talk to, such as a close friend, family member, or a professional counselor. They can offer you help and support.
He seems to be really happy already, while I’m still stuck on this. I feel like I’m so pathetic.

You don’t need to compare where you are now with where he is. Everyone has their own path of growth, and everyone has their own difficulties and challenges. You need to focus on yourself and try to become stronger and more confident. Try to pay more attention to your own feelings and needs, do the things you want to do, and become someone more independent and self-aware.
I know I need to accept all of this, but I’m really sad. I really want to recover quickly.

Getting through a breakup takes time. Try to give yourself some time to breathe and rest. Don’t force yourself to feel better; this kind of emotion needs to be adjusted and soothed slowly. Do some things you enjoy, or go traveling with friends. These can help you relax and gradually regain your confidence and motivation.
Thank you. I’ll try to accept who I am right now.
You’re welcome. You are a brave and strong person. I believe you can come out of the shadow of this breakup and find your own happiness again.

Lately I’ve been really troubled. I often think about things in the past that I didn’t do well, and when I think of them I feel extremely embarrassed. Then I imagine going back to that time and, with the way I think now, doing that thing perfectly. I’ll think of the same thing many times, and each time I come up with a different new way to handle it. These thoughts keep me from sleeping well and affect my life and my mood.

From what you’re saying, your emotions have been very troubling for a while, and this is a very common situation. We’ve all had similar experiences, repeatedly thinking about bad things that happened. It’s like a kind of self-torture, bringing feelings of guilt and shame. When these emotions can’t be worked through, they can make you feel unusually weighed down inside, so constantly replaying those bad moments can also be a way of easing your feelings. But this is only a temporary measure. The most important thing is to recognize who you are now and what your real situation is, to bravely face your inner self, and to look for the things you truly want to put your energy and passion into. That’s how you’ll find meaning and a sense of belonging in life. So, try to let go of the past first, and bravely face the present and the future.
But every time I think of it, I lose control emotionally and can’t think rationally.

To confirm again, what you’re feeling now is anxiety and a sense of losing control. That’s understandable, and we can use some methods to help calm ourselves down. Running, yoga, deep breathing, and other approaches can help ease this uncomfortable feeling. The most important thing is to find a way you like and that suits you, to help you regulate your emotions.
I’ve always felt that I have no value, and I often feel like no one understands me.

This is a very common thought. We all experience self-doubt and self-denial at times. But you need to know that everyone is unique, with different values and accomplishments. We can’t compare ourselves with others; we need to learn to accept ourselves and value ourselves. At the same time, it’s also important to communicate more with the people around you and let them understand what you’re going through. That way, not only can you get support and help, but you can also build closer relationships with others.
I’ve always felt like I’m a failure and that there’s no way for me to succeed.

Success and failure are not black-and-white concepts. Everyone has their own understanding and standards, and different achievements and gains. What matters is seeing your strengths and potential, and continuing to try to improve yourself. This requires patience and perseverance. Every effort is meaningful; even if the result isn’t what you hoped for, it is still an experience and a lesson, and in another way, a foundation for success.
But I feel so lonely, like there’s no one I can rely on.

There will always be times of loneliness on the road of life, and that’s very normal. But you need to know that you’re not walking alone. If there are people around you who accompany you and understand what you’re going through, your life will feel more meaningful. So you need to actively look for like-minded friends and groups. For example, you could join some volunteer organizations, take part in social activities, and so on. By meeting more people and communicating more, you may come across someone who is just in need of a good friend.
Thank you for listening so patiently to what’s in my heart and for helping me.
There’s no need to thank me. I believe you will get through your current situation and have a bright future of your own. Remember, if you need any help, I’ll be here by your side to support you.
Lately I feel like I’m always very sad, and I don’t know what to do.
Can you tell me why you’re feeling sad?
Maybe it’s because I’ve had setbacks at work, and I feel like I didn’t do well enough.
Success and failure are both a normal part of life. Don’t push yourself too hard. Whether you do well or not doesn’t affect your worth or your abilities.
But I feel like I can’t do anything right.
That sounds like a self-critical thought. Try not to be too harsh on yourself, and don’t forget the achievements and experience you’ve had before. Believe in yourself—you can do things well.
Thank you for encouraging me, but I’m still really afraid of failing.

Fear is a very natural emotion, but don’t let it stop you from pursuing what you want. Try to let go of the fear, because you can do this. Failure isn’t the end; it’s just the starting point for becoming stronger next time.
I feel a little better after hearing what you said, but I’m still very nervous.

Feeling nervous is also common. Don’t feel discouraged or blame yourself for it. Trust in your abilities and your self-worth, and face challenges with your head held high. They’re just opportunities for you to grow.
Thank you for continuing to support me. I’ll try my best to work through my emotions and challenges.
You’re welcome. I believe you can get through this difficult time. Take it step by step, and we’ll get through each challenge together.
I feel awful. Life lately has made me feel so empty, and it feels like there isn’t anyone around me I can talk to. I really don’t know what to do anymore.

I can understand how you’re feeling right now. You don’t have to face all of life’s difficulties alone. I really appreciate you coming here and sharing this with me, and I’ll do my best to support you.
Thank you for comforting me. Can you tell me how I can get through this pain?

First, you need to recognize your feelings and accept them. Don’t suppress your emotions; you can express them by writing them down, drawing, watching movies, and so on. At the same time, you can also communicate more with the friends and family around you and share how you’re feeling about your life.
Mm, I’ll try. But I still feel very helpless, like I’ve lost confidence in life.

That’s very normal. We all go through low points. But we can’t let ourselves fall into despair; try to notice the good things. I also have one suggestion: you could try doing something new, expand your interests and hobbies, and help yourself find some passion for life.
Okay, I’ll try. But I still feel powerless.

You’re not fighting this alone; we all face difficulties. What’s important is learning how to look for help and not face every hardship by yourself. If you need to, you can seek professional counseling, where there are many professionals who can give you evidence-based support.
Thank you for your suggestions. I feel much better now.
I’m glad I could help. Don’t forget, everyone needs help and support, and you’re no exception. I hope you can keep looking for your own joy and happiness.
Mm, I will. Thank you.
Wishing you well. Everything will get better!

Two months ago, after drinking, I contacted the woman I loved ten years ago. I found out she hasn’t been doing well, and I want to be there for her. I still love her very, very much. We chat every day, but I’ve been married for four years, and my wife loves me a lot. This woman used to be deep in my heart, and now she takes up all of it. I think about her day and night. Should I give up everything to be with her? What should I do?

Hearing how troubled you are, I can really understand how you feel. First, I’d like to ask you: what are your thoughts right now? Do you want to be with the woman you’ve loved for ten years, or choose to stay in your current life?
I don’t know how to choose. I want to stop thinking about her, but she takes up too much space in my mind.

I understand this complicated emotional entanglement you’re feeling, but I want to remind you that right now, you may need to put your attention on your relationship with your current family. Have you had real communication with your wife and tried to find ways to resolve the issues between you?
My relationship with my wife has always been good, but I’m always missing the feelings I had before.

I understand what you mean, but sometimes we imagine the good parts of the past as being even more beautiful than they were. Right now, you may need to look at the relationship between you objectively and think about what consequences it would bring if you insisted on being with your former girlfriend now.
I’ll think it through. I won’t make a decision lightly.
Good. I’m relieved that you’re able to think seriously about this. I suggest you consider seeking professional counseling to help you better deal with this emotional issue.
Okay, I’ll consider it. Thank you for your advice.
You’re welcome. We’re all human; we all have times when we struggle and need help. If you need anything, feel free to reach out to me anytime.
Thank you. I will. I feel much better now.
I’m glad to hear you say that. If you still need my help, just let me know.
Lately I keep thinking about that past experience of struggling with rent and housing, and sometimes I even have nightmares.

Sending you a hug. It’s very normal to feel this way after going through something like that, but try not to let it affect your life now. You could try shifting your attention and finding some meaningful things to do to keep yourself busy, like visiting friends, joining social activities, and so on.
But sometimes it really feels awful, and I think of a lot of unpleasant memories.

That’s right, that feeling must be really painful. But you need to understand that what happened in the past can’t be changed, while you can take control of the present and create your future. So don’t let yourself get stuck in those difficult past experiences. Try to face life’s challenges actively.
What you’re saying makes a lot of sense, but sometimes I feel like I really don’t know what to do.

That’s very normal. Sometimes we need a bit of guidance and help. You could try talking with a professional mental health doctor, or find some friends to talk to and share how you’re feeling. I believe you’ll get some good advice and comfort.
Mm, thank you for your advice. Also, sometimes I feel like I was so stupid. Why did I live with that guy in a place we couldn’t afford?

Don’t blame yourself. Everyone goes through times when they make mistakes. What matters is that you’ve recognized the mistakes from the past and are trying to change your attitude and behavior. That’s growth.
Mm, I’ll try my best to do that.
Okay. I believe you’ll definitely keep getting better. Keep looking ahead. We’re all here by your side, supporting you.
Okay, thank you for being with me and supporting me.
You’re welcome. We’ll always be good friends. Come to me anytime you need me.

I’ve finished my master’s degree and have been working for two years. During that time, I worked at two companies. The first company was very unstructured, and I wasn’t very clear about my work responsibilities. Maybe my boss felt I wasn’t meeting his expectations, so he ended up giving me nothing to do. During that period, I couldn’t feel any sense of value, so I stopped going to work much, and then the company persuaded me to leave. At the second company, the boss cared a lot about interpersonal relationships, but he really didn’t value work quality or efficiency. He also had a bad temper and would get angry for no reason. I had major differences with him on this, and because we didn’t see eye to eye and my relationship with him wasn’t good, I was sent back to the HR department. I’m looking for a job now, but the passion I used to have seems to be gone. I feel really unmotivated and very anxious about the future. I don’t know what would be best to do.

Hello. After hearing about your experience, I can really sense how you’re feeling right now. Having gone through something like this is indeed very disappointing and can feel like a real blow. As for your situation, I think we can look at it this way. You’ve been working for two years after graduation and have been through two companies. Even though things didn’t go as you hoped, the effort you put in is worth recognizing. When you’ve just left school and entered the new environment of the workplace, your experience and skills still need to be built up and improved, so it’s very normal to run into bottlenecks. I’m able to share my own experience with you because I’ve also gone through similar situations, so I really understand how you feel.
Thank you for your understanding and for sharing that. I feel very lost about work right now. I don’t know what I should do, and I’ve also lost confidence in my abilities.

Don’t worry. This is a normal emotional response. We should recognize the state we’re in right now, think about the problem with a positive attitude, and explore our own potential. You can first make some adjustments to your mindset and to your expectations for the future. You can set some small goals for yourself and gradually achieve them. As we keep feeling a sense of accomplishment while reaching our goals, we can also build up more confidence and courage.

What you said makes sense. I also want to try some new things to make myself better. But I’m always afraid of failing. When I think about my past failures, I feel like there isn’t much hope in my current situation.

Sometimes we all have worries and doubt whether we can reach our goals. But what’s important is that we don’t stop moving; we keep going forward. When we think back on things that didn’t go well in the past, sometimes we shouldn’t let ourselves get lost in them. We can look for what those failures can teach us, sum up the lessons, and keep improving ourselves. And we need to believe that although our abilities are limited, the problems we encounter can be solved by continuing to try and look for methods.
I also want to change the current situation, but I feel like I keep repeating the same mistakes, and it’s hard to make progress.

It’s true that sometimes it’s hard for us to calm down, analyze the problem, and find a suitable solution. Maybe sometimes, out of a sudden impulse, we make decisions that are too rushed or blind. So we need to reflect, and other people’s suggestions are very important. You can communicate with people around you as well as professionals to get their opinions and advice. These opinions and suggestions can help us see the problem from different angles and provide us with better directions for thinking.

I think what you said is very right. Sometimes we need to listen more to other people’s experiences and suggestions, and improve ourselves step by step. Recently, while looking for a job, I feel like my anxiety has increased quite a bit, and the future doesn’t feel as clear as I imagined.

Looking for a job is indeed something that can make people fairly anxious. But remember, we can’t bring that anxiety into the job-search process, because anxiety often gets in the way of our thinking. First, we need to find a rational attitude toward our current situation. If you need to adjust your job-search strategy, you can focus your efforts based on your own situation, such as developing your skills and improving your competitiveness. At the same time, you can also appropriately adjust how you present your previous work experience and achievements, so that recruiters can more clearly understand your past experience and abilities. This can strengthen your confidence and help you feel less nervous in interviews. Of course, the process of looking for a job is also, in itself, a process of growth and learning. No matter what the result is, as long as we put in the effort and take part in the process, it is an experience of continuously improving ourselves.

Your suggestions are all very practical, and I also want to integrate them into my life or work. But sometimes I have conflicts with others because of my own thoughts or opinions, and that leads to negative emotions. What should I do about that?

It’s true that sometimes we encounter disagreements with others, and that’s very normal. But we need to remember that everyone’s thoughts and perspectives have their own uniqueness. We can’t simply use our own ideas as the standard for judging other people’s views. First, we can shift our perspective and think from the other person’s point of view, so we can find a solution that everyone can accept. Second, we can express our needs at the right time, so the other person can better understand our thoughts and needs, and then respond in a more constructive way. Finally, attitude is very important. Even if we disagree with the other person, we still need to respect their viewpoint and try to avoid becoming overly emotional or overly attached to our own position.
Thank you for your advice. I feel much better now, and I have more confidence and motivation to face future challenges.

Congratulations. This is a very good start. When facing future challenges, we should actively seek solutions and work hard to overcome difficulties. No matter how big the problems we encounter are, as long as we move forward steadily step by step and accumulate experience, I believe there will definitely be better results.
Lately I’ve been feeling really low, and I always feel like I can’t do anything right. I don’t have much motivation.
Hi, I hear that you’re feeling down and lacking motivation. Could you talk with me about what’s been going on in your life lately?
I’ve had a lot going on at work recently, but I feel like I’m not doing well. And there are some worries at home too, and all of it makes me feel overwhelmed.

I really understand how you feel. Sometimes stress from work and life can make people feel overwhelmed. You could try some relaxation methods, like meditation, breathing exercises, or yoga, to relieve stress.
Thank you for your suggestions, but whenever I think about these things, I feel really helpless, like I can’t do anything right.

That’s a very common feeling, but I believe you can find some methods that suit you and help you get back to feeling more like yourself. You could try writing down your thoughts and feelings; that can help you understand yourself better.
Mm, I’ll try. Thank you for your suggestions. But I still feel pretty awful.
I understand how you feel. In this situation, you may need some professional help. You could consider seeing a psychologist or consulting a professional; they can give you some better suggestions.
Mm, I’ll think about it. Thank you for your suggestions and comfort.
You’re welcome. I’m here to support you, and I believe you can overcome these difficulties and keep a positive attitude.
Thank you, I will. With your encouragement, I feel much better.
I’m very glad to hear that good news. Remember, you’re not alone; I’ll always be here with you.
I’ve been listening to Psychology FM lately and find it pretty helpful, but every time I want to look at the original text, I don’t know where to find it. Could you help me with that?
I understand that you have this need, especially if you want to learn more deeply about psychology. You could try searching on Baidu, or see if there are related books you can refer to.
Thank you for your suggestion. I want to learn more about physical and mental health, but I always feel like I don’t have enough knowledge, and I feel a bit anxious.

Try not to worry too much. Many people have similar feelings. But we can all build up knowledge to better face our emotions and stress. You could choose to attend some psychological counseling, or read related books to help yourself.
I’ve heard that some mental health conditions need treatment, but I don’t know whether I need it. Could you give me some advice?

I can understand your concern, but I’m not a medical doctor. If you think you may have a mental health issue, you could first see a relevant specialist and hear their advice. At the same time, we can look for some information to understand common mental health issues and ways to cope with them.
I want to make an appointment with a doctor, but I’m always hesitant and can’t decide. I don’t know what to do.

If you feel hesitant, you can start with some simple steps, like looking up psychologists near you and arranging an appointment or consultation. When you’ve given yourself some time, you could also choose to attend some psychology courses. Sometimes you may find the right answer deep inside yourself.
Sometimes I feel like I don’t have very good control over my emotions. What should I do?

Managing emotions really isn’t easy; it takes building the right skills and experience. You can start with some basics, such as breathing exercises and meditation. When you feel like your emotions are about to explode, you can also try adjusting your attitude a bit and looking at the problem from another angle. If possible, you could also seek help from a professional counselor.
I feel like sometimes I don’t have confidence, and I’m always worried that I haven’t done well enough.

Building confidence is a gradual process. You can start by trying to challenge yourself with small things, such as doing more relaxing hobbies and building good habits in different areas. When you run into new difficulties, you can also share your problems with others and get help and support from them.
Lately I haven’t been able to eat much, and I don’t really know why. My appetite’s been a bit poor, and my complexion looks really bad too.

Hearing what you’ve shared, I can really understand your worry and unease. First of all, this is a very normal reaction. In spring, our need for food can decrease, and with most of your time being spent indoors right now, your body may be under some strain. All of these can affect your appetite.
But I feel like I’ve already been paying a lot of attention to nutrition and my diet. Why is it still like this?

When it comes to poor appetite, we can try some other ways to improve it. For example, going out for walks more, enjoying the beauty and scents that nature brings us, listening to music, or watching some light and enjoyable entertainment programs to ease the stress on your body and mind. At the same time, you can try more new things and foods to help adjust your sense of taste and your mental state. Of course, it’s also important to keep paying attention to your diet and overall health care.
Thank you for your suggestions. I’ll try them.

No problem! You’ve already taken the first step toward change. I believe that as long as you keep going, you’ll definitely be able to get through this difficult situation. At the same time, remember to keep paying attention to your physical and mental health, and don’t put too much pressure or too many demands on yourself. Take it slowly, and it’s enough to reach a state that feels sustainable.
Mm-hmm, I’ll try to pay attention to that.

Be sure to keep to your own pace, relax your mind, and turn stress and worries into positive motivation as you gradually move toward a healthier way of living. If you need to, feel free to come talk with me anytime.
Thank you. I’m really grateful!
Your effort and belief are the most important things. I believe everyone has the strength to go beyond themselves, and you’re definitely no exception. Hang in there!
I always feel like I’m only in the mood to play on my phone when I have plenty of time, but when a task is urgent, I can take it seriously. Why is that?

Hi, I understand your situation. This is actually because you may have a bit of procrastination. When you have a lot of time, you feel like there’s still plenty of time and no need to rush. But when the task becomes urgent, you realize you have to take it seriously in order to finish it. I’m not sure how you see this situation?
I’ve tried making a detailed plan for myself before, but I can never follow it strictly, and that makes me feel frustrated.

It sounds like your plan didn’t work out. This may be because your plan didn’t fully take time management and self-discipline into account. So would you be able to adjust the plan, prioritize tasks, or look for other tools to help you manage your time better?
I think that really is a very good suggestion, and I’ll try it. But sometimes I feel anxious and nervous because I’m worried the task will be hard to finish.

I understand the impact anxiety and nervousness can have on people, but what you need to know is that these feelings are normal, and everyone has them. You can try taking deep breaths or using other effective relaxation methods. At the same time, remind yourself that there is still room for your skills to improve, and as long as you put in the effort, you can definitely do the task well.
Thank you for your encouragement. That makes me feel very warm. But I’m still worried that I won’t be able to handle many things that may come up in the future.

I understand how you feel, and I hope I can help you. Maybe you need to place more importance on communicating with others and being able to seek help, because sometimes accepting support and help from others is a better solution, and it also makes us stronger and more confident.
What you said makes a lot of sense. I’ll think about it carefully. Actually, talking with you makes me feel very relaxed and comfortable. Thank you.

You’re welcome. I’m very glad I could help you. Also, remember to give yourself some time every day to relax and have fun. This is very important for both physical and mental health. I hope that through your own efforts and some small changes, you can gradually break through procrastination and become more self-disciplined and efficient. You’ve got this!

My husband is clearly doing okay financially, so why isn’t he willing to spend money on his wife and child? He keeps saying we need to save money, save money—but how much is enough? How can I communicate effectively with a man like this? Is being stingy something you’re born with and can’t change? What exactly is going on psychologically for him?

Hello! I’d be very willing to help you work through this. Your husband’s reason for saving money may come from the way he was brought up in his family. It could be that when he was little, his mother often said in front of him that the family had no money, or that his family really couldn’t provide good living conditions for the children because of their financial situation. This may have led your husband to develop the idea that money is very important. You’re right—communication is important. We can try telling him, letting him know that you are there by his side supporting him, and that money can always be earned. The two of you, as a couple, can earn money together, and that may give him more of a sense of security.
Thank you for your answer. I’d like to ask, what are men’s worries like inside? How can I understand him?

Men have their own worries just like women do; they just express them differently. Men tend to prefer solving problems on their own, and they may hide their worries deep inside. We can try communicating with them and listening to them talk about it, which can increase mutual understanding.
I hope he can understand how I think. He always ignores my and our child’s needs, and that makes me really sad. What should I do to help him understand what I’m thinking?

You can try having a talk with him and tell him your thoughts and needs. Try not to criticize him, because that may make him mistakenly think you don’t have confidence in his abilities. At the same time, give him enough sense of security, and let him know you will always support him. This way, it may be easier for him to understand your thoughts.
I understand. I’ll try talking with him. So is his stingy behavior something he was born with? How should I ease this situation?

This kind of stingy behavior may largely come from a person’s upbringing and psychological reasons. We can try to understand his situation and help him find a healthier way of living. At the same time, you can also try changing the way you influence him, and influence him in a more positive way.
I understand. I’ll communicate with him properly. Thank you for your help!

You’re welcome. I hope my answers can be helpful to you. If you have any difficulties or questions, feel free to contact me anytime, and we can work through them together. Wishing you well! The world and I love you.

I've been feeling a bit down lately. Since graduating, I've been working at the school the whole time. The pay is low, and my social circle is pretty narrow. I want to change jobs and move to a different city, but I haven't made a decision yet.
Hi, hearing what you're struggling with, I want to send you a hug first. I can offer you some questions to help you think it through. First, in your current work and life, what feels missing for you?
I feel like the work isn't challenging enough, and my social circle is pretty limited.
So what are your hopes for the future? Is it a higher salary, or richer social experiences?
I hope I can have a job with relatively higher pay, and also a broader social circle.
Changing to a different way of life may mean losing some things you have now. Have you thought about what you might lose?
I might lose the familiar environment and the sense of stability I have at the school.
Those worries are completely understandable. But don't forget, unknown challenges can also bring you new growth and understanding. Have you thought about what challenges you might face in the future?
Actually, I haven't thought about those things.

If your current situation really is making you feel tired of it, then try a different way of life. But before making a decision, be sure to think carefully about what you would gain and lose. You need to make sure you won't regret it.
Thank you for your support and advice. I'll consider a wise choice.
You're welcome. I believe you can find a way of life that belongs to you. Believe in yourself, and believe in the future. Everything will get better.

Hello! In the second semester of ninth grade, I was playing cards with my classmates. After losing almost two or three hundred, I had an evil thought—to cheat. I ended up winning almost 200. But afterward I felt how ugly I was, and I wanted to make up for it, so I treated them to a meal, and I also deliberately stopped cheating and lost more money to make up for it in my heart. But now I still often think about that incident and feel an extremely frequent sense of guilt. I’m also afraid it will affect my future. I hope I can find some relief. Thank you!

Hello. Hearing what’s on your mind, I understand how you’re feeling right now. As long as we are living people, we all make mistakes sometimes, so don’t be too harsh on yourself. The fact that you were able to recognize on your own that you made a mistake, and took some practical steps to make up for it, shows that you have a good mindset and self-awareness. Try not to keep blaming yourself too much, because that will only make things worse. Let go of the burden in your heart, and accept this not-so-perfect self.

Thank you for your encouragement and support, but I still feel very guilty, because I feel like I owe my classmates an apology and compensation. But I’m also afraid that if I do that, they’ll find out I cheated, and it will disrupt our relationship. What should I do?

You’re right. One part of recognizing a mistake is apologizing. But you can also start by correcting yourself first. If you can patiently show real kindness and sincerity, and your own mindset improves, that may be more convincing than simply saying you regret it. Also, when harm has been caused to someone, it’s hard to make up for it directly through a few forms of apology. But if you’re willing to treat that person in a more sincere way, they may understand you and forgive your mistake. You should know that it is because we need the kindness and understanding of others that we can live in this world with peace of mind.

I understand. Thank you for your advice. But I still feel very lonely now, and I feel like no one can understand me. I’m afraid I’ll fall into guilt again and go down a bad path again. Do you have any suggestions?

I can understand how you feel. But no matter how difficult the challenges we face are, we should not lose ourselves. You need to smile at who you once were and accept the state you are in now. Maybe you can try to find some people who support you and share your feelings with them. These people might be coworkers who help you complete your work, or friends around you who have always gotten along well with you. As long as you’re willing to open up and speak from your heart, many people will be willing to give you encouragement and support. No matter when or where you are, you will not be alone, because you are not fighting by yourself.

Thank you for your understanding and support. But what I’m more worried about now is that I’ve developed anorexia, and my eating routine is messed up every day. I’m afraid it will have a major impact on my physical health. Do you have any good suggestions?

That sounds very uncomfortable. The human body is the vessel of our soul, and only when we can care for and cherish our bodies can we have a healthy and pleasant life. My suggestion is that you can try to consciously plan your diet, eat more healthy foods like vegetables and fruit, and appropriately control high-calorie foods and fat intake. At the same time, you can also record your diet and how your body feels each day, and analyze the nutrition and quality of what you take in each day. When you feel your body starting to develop in a healthy direction, your mindset may also become more positive. Most importantly, don’t blindly pursue so-called weight-loss methods that are irresponsible or whose background is unclear. This is not only bad for the body; the harm to your mindset is also immeasurable.

Thank you for your advice. But I still often have depressed feelings, and I feel like I’ve let down my family and society, and that I’m not able to handle my tasks and responsibilities. Do you have any good methods or key points you can share?

Your worries are very normal. This shows that you have a fairly strong sense of responsibility and determination. But excessive worry and pressure can easily have negative effects on the body and mind. My suggestion is to try to categorize and sort through your anxious feelings, find the real reasons behind them, and then look for practical, workable ways to solve them or cope with them. At the same time, you can also try to communicate with peers who share similar interests or experiences and share your worries with them, or seek help from a professional mental health doctor. Occasional relaxation and recreational activities can also help you relieve stress and worry. Arranging your time reasonably, getting enough sleep, and maintaining a healthy lifestyle are also very important.
Thank you for your encouragement and support. I feel much better now. Finally, I want to ask: how can I maintain a healthy and balanced emotional state and mindset?

Maintaining a healthy and balanced mindset requires us to pay attention to many things in daily life, such as caring for our physical health and having reasonable eating habits, keeping positive thoughts and consulting professional doctors, and developing and maintaining our hobbies and volunteer activities. At the same time, in this fast-paced modern society, we also need to stay aware of our physical and mental balance. At the very least, spend a few minutes every day relaxing and regulating your breathing. You can do this through music, yoga, or other methods. Finally, don’t forget to listen to your inner voice, follow your heart when making choices, and discover new possibilities in life. This can also help us build a positive attitude toward life.

My boyfriend and I have been together for 10 years, but now my parents keep creating conflict because of some things between us. They don’t accept him. This troubles me every day, and I don’t know what to do.
Dear, seeing you going through this kind of suffering every day right now, it really must be so hard. I really want to give you a hug~

At first, my boyfriend’s family wasn’t well-off, and his work wasn’t stable either, so my parents opposed us being together. Back then, neither of us was mature, and we didn’t handle the situation well, which made the conflicts keep getting deeper.

This situation really is very painful. The two of you have given so much for love, but you still can’t get your parents’ blessing, and that makes you feel a lot of pain. So we can first sort through your current situation and the obstacles you’re facing, and see whether we can find some possible solutions.
The conflict between my parents and my boyfriend is very deep. Neither side will give in, and it’s really hard for me to bear this kind of pressure.

Sigh, this really is hard. What we can do is first try to understand how things are between you all and what both sides are thinking. When you face this situation, how do you get along with your boyfriend and your parents? What are your patterns of interaction like? It may also be because there hasn’t been enough communication that these conflicts have come up. You can try putting yourselves in each other’s shoes, first trying to understand the other person’s thoughts and the difficult situation they’re in, and then look for ways to solve it.

My parents opposed our relationship from the very beginning. They once arranged to meet my boyfriend, and they also sent text messages scolding him and his family. Later, my father even pushed my boyfriend, and my boyfriend hit my mother back with a slap. After that, my parents absolutely would not accept him anymore.

I can imagine that this was an extremely painful experience for you. But we can try to think about it from another angle, not just focus on that argument. You need to realize that who was right and who was wrong at the time is no longer important, because it can’t be changed now. What matters is looking ahead—how to get out of the deadlock, find a way to change things, and help you find a solution you can accept.
I’ve always been very independent, so I’ve always been firm in how I see my boyfriend. But my parents want me to be with someone else, and I don’t know how to communicate with them.

Being independent is a good thing, but when facing emotional issues, we need to communicate with family and try to seek their support. We can try to approach the conversation with a calm attitude, focusing on confusion rather than resistance. Since you firmly believe this relationship is important, you can share your thoughts with your parents, talk about why the two of you love each other, and try to find ways to overcome the problems together.

My boyfriend does have some behaviors that make me feel confused and worried, but I believe he is a good person. It’s just that sometimes he seems a bit emotional. But I really don’t want my parents and me to hurt each other over this issue.

Since you’re already aware of the issues with your boyfriend, and you believe he is a good person, it’s very possible that you can help him improve some of his behaviors. On the other hand, I can understand your care and respect for your family. Because of that, we can temporarily try to handle the relationship between you and your boyfriend in a way your parents can accept, such as not being overly intimate, or getting out of financial dependence on your boyfriend. But if the conflict between your parents and your boyfriend continues to exist and affects your lives, in the end you will still need to negotiate together, find a better solution, and then do everything you can to make it happen.
Thank you for your encouragement and advice. I’ll think it over carefully.

I’m glad my suggestions were helpful to you. We can’t control other people’s thoughts and behaviors, but we can put effort into our own thoughts and actions. Start with ourselves first, try to understand and be tolerant, and then we can get along with others harmoniously. Lastly, I will always stand by your side and support you.

I've been running into a lot of problems lately, and I don't know what to do. I met a guy while playing games, and the moment I heard his voice, I felt drawn to him. After spending time with him, I realized I seem to have fallen for him. But I already have a boyfriend, and my feelings for him are getting weaker and weaker now.

Hi, I can understand how troubling this feels for you. I want to tell you that people we aren’t actually with are often the ones we most easily fantasize about and imagine things with. Sometimes we don’t really like the real person, but instead develop fantasies around certain qualities they have. Maybe your feelings for that guy aren’t entirely because of who he really is, but more because of your own imagination. So I’d suggest you get to know him a bit more and see what he’s really like. That way, you can judge your feelings more accurately.

Thank you for your suggestion, but I don’t know how to get to know him. We’re not in the same city, so we can only stay in touch through the game. He just broke up with his ex-girlfriend not long ago, and it seems like he doesn’t like me either. That makes me really sad.

I know this is hard, but we need to trust that time can resolve many things. Since he just broke up, he may not want to start a new relationship right now, and his attitude toward you isn’t clear either. I’m afraid that may only leave you feeling lost and confused. And now your relationship with your boyfriend is also at a standstill. I’d suggest you first calm down and really think about your feelings and needs. Don’t make a decision that hurts yourself or others because of a moment of impulse.
You’re right. I’ve been too impulsive. But I don’t know what to do. It feels like I’ve been pulled into an emotional whirlpool.

I understand that feeling. You’re not fighting this alone. But don’t forget, we can always find our way out of difficult situations. When facing difficulties, we need to learn to be kind to ourselves and find our footing. Maybe you can find some other hobbies to shift your attention, and you can also try talking with family or friends and sharing what’s on your mind.
Maybe I really need to re-examine myself and stop overthinking so much. I really do need more support and help right now. Thank you for listening to me.

You’re welcome. I’m very glad to offer you help and support. We need to believe that even if we can’t see hope right now, the future will always get better. As long as you keep going with effort and determination, you’ll find that the strength and courage deep inside you will guide you toward happiness.
Thank you for talking me through this. I feel much better now. I’m really grateful to have someone like you supporting me.

You’re welcome. When you run into difficulties, we’re like family. If you still need help or want to talk with me again, you can contact me anytime. I’ll always be here rooting for you and supporting you.
Thank you. I’ll find my own way forward as soon as I can, and then I’ll tell you about my progress. I’m really grateful for your company and encouragement.
Okay, hang in there. No matter when or where, I’ll be by your side, cheering you on.

Recently I heard that Pei Qi, the three-year-old internet-famous child, already weighs over 70 jin, which is really worrying. I don’t understand why her parents would let her eat so much unhealthy food.

Hello, I understand your concern about this issue. Whatever the reasons behind this situation, the child’s health should be the most important thing. We need some changes in how people think—no longer treating children as tools for making money, but as independent individuals who deserve respect and protection.
Exactly. I think what these parents are doing is really hard to understand. Why would they put their child’s health in a secondary place?

Perhaps it’s driven by a kind of psychological idolization, or by the pursuit of fame and profit. We shouldn’t just blame their behavior, but try to educate and guide them to view this issue correctly. In addition, we need to raise public awareness so that more people pay attention to this kind of unethical behavior.
But I feel like these parents seem to just let things go on as they are, and they won’t listen to other people’s objections. I don’t know how to change their thinking.

You’re right. This is indeed a difficult issue to handle. We need to look for and make use of effective ways to call for public attention, so that incidents like this happen as little as possible. If each of us can make some small changes, we can slowly push society as a whole toward progress and change.
I understand. I’ll also do my part to help push for change in this society. But I’m still very worried about Pei Qi and her family. Their current situation is really not good.

I can understand your worry. This is indeed a difficult issue to get away from. But we can try to face the problem with a more positive attitude. Whether or not the family listens to our suggestions, we can still pay attention to them with a calm mindset. At the same time, we can also provide more help and support to Pei Qi and other children who have been hurt, so they can feel our care.

Thank you for your suggestions. I’ll keep a positive mindset at all times and use my own strength to change this unethical behavior. I believe that as long as each of us works at it, things will definitely improve.

That’s right. I hope we can make some small contributions to this society together and make the world a better place. If you need help and support at any time, I’ll be there for you right away. I hope you have a happy and healthy life!
Over the past year, I feel like it’s been getting worse and worse. I feel empty inside and have no interest in anything, like being alive has no meaning. What should I do?

Hearing you say that, I can imagine how painful this feels for you right now. Your feelings are very real, but they don’t necessarily represent reality. Have you tried talking with friends, or joining some activities, to help break through that sense of loneliness and emptiness?
Mm, actually, I have tried meeting new people and joining new activities, but I always feel like it’s more comfortable just staying by myself.

I understand how you feel, but avoiding contact with others can keep you from finding ways to work through this difficult situation. I suggest you first get used to social settings in a safe environment, and try to find people who share your interests and build friendships with them.
Actually, I feel like I have really low self-esteem. I’m always shutting myself in at home, afraid to have contact with the outside world. What should I do?

You’re not the only person who feels low self-esteem. Many people have had, or are currently going through, feelings like this. You can start with small things, like choosing a topic you’re interested in and looking for groups related to it, or joining some self-improvement courses or activities, gradually building up your confidence.
Mm, I could try that. But a lot of the time I feel like I have no motivation to finish things, and I always slack off.

That’s very normal; we all have times like that. You can break your goals down into small steps and complete them one by one, while remembering to encourage yourself and keep going. If you really feel it’s very hard to handle, don’t give up on yourself. Seeking professional help is a very wise choice.
Mm, I’ll think it over carefully. Thank you for your suggestions and encouragement.

You’re welcome. I’m glad I could offer you some support and help. Remember, you’re not alone. I really appreciate your courage, and I hope you move forward with more steadiness and confidence in the future.

I feel like I’ve achieved nothing in these past twenty-something years, like I have no value. Life feels so heavy and hard... I feel anxious, afraid, inferior, and lonely all day long, and I’m always trying to hide my pain in front of other people... I feel more and more lost. I don’t know where my future is heading, and I’ve even started to question the meaning of my existence...

I can understand feeling this way, but I believe you do have value, and your existence has meaning. Everyone goes through setbacks like this, but remember that stress and feelings of defeat won’t last forever. There will definitely be a better direction ahead.
But the pressure I’m under is just too much, and I can’t seem to get away from it... I feel like I’m about to fall apart, like I can’t keep going...

Stress is a normal part of life, and we need to learn how to cope with it. You could try some ways to ease stress, like deep breathing, meditation, and exercise. At the same time, you can also seek professional help, so a professional can help you understand the problem and find better solutions.
I feel like I’m really useless, like I can’t handle the challenges in life... Am I really completely useless?

Putting yourself down doesn’t help. Each of us has our own strengths and limitations. Your value isn’t decided by the outside world; it’s created by you. When it comes to the areas where you feel lacking, you can try self-reflection, accept those limitations, and look for ways to grow.
I feel so lonely, like there’s no one I can share my feelings with...

We need to stay connected with others and share our feelings and experiences. You can seek help and support from family, friends, or professionals. At the same time, you can also join some social activities and expand your social circle.
I’m really troubled, and I don’t know what I should do...

You can reach out for help from a friend like me or from other professionals, and look for ways to solve this. At the same time, we can also understand our own feelings, help ourselves relax, and try our best to avoid unhelpful behaviors like overthinking and self-punishment.
Thank you for your support. I feel much better...

You can do this. I’ll always support you, and you can talk to me anytime. Remember to think about positive things each day, and don’t ignore your own mood and feelings. We’ll get through this difficult time together. I believe the future will definitely be better.
Lately I’ve been feeling really terrible, and I always feel very anxious.

Hi! I can understand how you feel. Anxiety is a common emotion, and many people experience it. You can try finding some ways to ease your anxiety, such as deep breathing, exercising, or chatting with friends.
But I always feel like I’m not doing well enough, and I’m afraid of being criticized by others.

These thoughts may make you feel even more anxious and stressed. You need to understand that everyone makes mistakes, and no one is perfect. No matter what problems come up, you can think them through carefully and find a solution.
I’ve been having insomnia a lot lately, and it’s hard for me to fall asleep.

This is a very common symptom, and it’s also one of the signs of anxiety. You can try relaxing your body and your mind, like listening to soothing music, drinking a cup of lemon honey water, taking a hot bath, and so on. At the same time, try to keep a regular daily routine and don’t get overly tired, okay?
I always feel like I haven’t done enough for my family, and I feel very guilty.

This shows that you care a lot about your family and hope you can do better. But don’t put too much pressure on yourself. Family responsibilities should be shared by both spouses. Communicating more with your family and sharing your thoughts and feelings can bring you closer together.
I often blame myself for my mistakes, and it feels very painful.

Blaming yourself will only make you suffer more, and it won’t help you. You need to reflect on your issues and look for solutions, while also learning to accept your mistakes and shortcomings. You need to understand that everyone has imperfect parts, and to emphasize again, you are no exception.
I often feel lonely, like no one can understand me.

Loneliness is a very real feeling, but it doesn’t mean you truly are alone. You can find friends who share your interests, or join some hobby groups. Connecting with others can help you understand yourself better and also help you feel less lonely.
Thank you for your suggestions. Hearing what you said makes me feel very comforted.

I’m very glad I could give you some help and support. Actually, there are still many people around you who care about you and love you, and you can reach out to them for help at any time. I hope you can feel happier and more confident with each day.

Right now I feel like living is really exhausting, and I feel so low and insignificant. I’m always suppressing my own feelings to satisfy other people, but in the end no one can understand me. People around me think I’m neurotic and have a bad temper. Now I can only choose to become silent. Sometimes I don’t even want to express myself, but then I have conflicting thoughts, and it’s very painful.

I understand how you feel. You’ve been living for other people, but you’ve never truly lived for yourself. You’ve suppressed your own feelings, but you didn’t receive understanding or care from others, and that has thrown you off balance. But you don’t have to express yourself according to other people’s wishes. You are independent, and you have the right to decide your own life. Once you do these things, you may find that you change a lot.
I understand, but I still don’t want to communicate my feelings with other people anymore.

That isn’t a bad idea. Sometimes silence is the best choice. You can find your balance again by spending time with yourself, and that’s also something many people need to do. Don’t fight with your own inner self. Handle your emotions calmly, spend time with yourself, and learn to regulate yourself.
But I keep feeling very lonely, and I don’t know how to deal with it.

I really understand how you feel. There is always a kind of boundary between people, and this kind of loneliness is not easily solved by actual friends. Most of the time, the feeling of loneliness is an inner experience. When your heart is calm, you can also feel warmth and happiness. If I’m not there with you, you can try some comforting things, like beautiful scenery, good food, nice music, or even watching movies. These can all help ease the feeling of loneliness.
I understand, but I don’t know my own value.

No matter what, your life has its own beautiful meaning. Please remember your own worth. Don’t imitate others, and don’t compare yourself with others. Everyone is different. You just need to be yourself, and maybe your life will be filled with a real sense of happiness.
How can I improve my confidence? I feel like I don’t have the courage to face difficulties.

Courage comes from small, gentle steps. Try to find things you’re interested in, practice them repeatedly, and mastering these skills can be part of the process of strengthening your inner self. You can begin by reading and expanding yourself, pursuing knowledge to gain confidence. When you understand your life and life goals more deeply, you will become more calm and confident.
I feel like I have some direction now, but I still need more contact and more support before I can truly walk out of these shadows.

You need more patience and effort to move toward the way of life you want. You don’t have to give up, because your supporters will always stand by your side. If you have other worries, or need other emotional support, you’re welcome to talk with me anytime. Through continuing to understand yourself and continuing to work hard, you can change yourself. You will become stronger and more confident!
I’ve been doing really badly lately. My girlfriend and I broke up. I can’t sleep at night, I have no appetite during the day, and my heart is full of hatred. I don’t know what to do.

I’m really sorry to hear what you’re going through. I can understand how you’re feeling right now; it often takes some time to slowly work through these emotions. You could try some relaxing activities, like yoga or meditation, or meet up with friends to talk and take your mind off things a bit.
Thank you for your reply. I tried some of the things you mentioned, but they haven’t had much effect. Every time I think of that girl, I feel extremely angry. I don’t know what to do.

I understand that feeling. You could try writing an emotional self-reflection, putting your thoughts and feelings down on paper, or talking to a friend about how you’re feeling. This can help you let out negative emotions and release some pressure.
I’ll try. But whenever I can’t sleep at night, I especially think of her and feel like such a failure. H-how can I deal with this?

A breakup is something that takes time to get through. If what you truly want inside is to care for and love yourself, things will slowly get better. If you’re not sleeping well at night, you could try listening to some gentle music, drinking some warm milk, or doing deep breathing to relax a little.
I’ve tried doing what you said, but I still can’t control my emotions. I feel like I don’t know where to go from here.

Try recording your emotional reactions and thought process, and identify the challenges you’re facing right now, then look for ways to cope with them. A breakup is certainly painful, but it can become part of your growth. Believe in yourself—you definitely have the ability to get through this period.
I’m really grateful to you. Your replies make me feel like I have some support inside. I’ll listen carefully to my own inner voice and also try to ease my emotions. Thank you.
You’re welcome. I believe you can get through this period. Contact me anytime; I’ll be here to support you.

I often feel afraid, because I’m scared of ending up in a situation where I need someone else to help me, and I’m also afraid that other people will get impatient with me. I’ve often been deceived before, and that has also made me feel afraid of people and unable to trust them. I often reject others or shut myself off, which leaves me disconnected from society and makes it hard to interact with people. Teacher, could you share some thoughts on this?

I can sense your fear and the uneasiness inside you. First, I think you need to realize that being afraid or rejecting others is not the same as feeling safe. On the contrary, it can make socializing and daily life even more difficult. Being afraid that others won’t help you reflects a vulnerable state of mind, because situations where help is needed do happen from time to time, but it depends on your relationship with the other person and their moral values, and it also requires considering the danger of the situation and one’s own safety. As for being afraid that others will get impatient with you, I think you can try to notice the other person’s situation, wait a moment, and then try to communicate, reducing blame and deepening communication and trust between you.
I want to understand how psychology evaluates this kind of fear and uneasiness, and how to ease this mindset.

For this kind of fear and uneasiness, psychology involves many kinds of knowledge and techniques, such as cognitive therapy, behavioral therapy, psychological counseling, and so on. The appropriate counseling and guidance would need to be based on your personal situation and needs. At the same time, I suggest you do more self-exploration and reflection, and try to adjust negative emotions through positive thinking or physical action, strengthening self-awareness and self-affirmation.
I feel that there is distance and distrust between me and the people around me, and social interactions are always very difficult. How can I change this situation?

This situation may require you to first become aware of your own emotions and beliefs, and then actively take part in social activities, communicate with others, and share your experiences and feelings. At the same time, you also need to learn to listen to and understand other people’s viewpoints and needs, offer others a certain amount of trust and acceptance, and engage in more interaction and cooperation. This can improve your confidence and capacity for understanding, and it is also helpful for building better interpersonal relationships.
I feel like it’s very hard for me to move on from past pain and experiences, and this may be affecting my health and my life. What should I do?

In this situation, I suggest that you actively seek professional psychological counseling and treatment. With the help and support of a counselor, you can slowly understand and release the pain and anxiety deep inside. You can also relax and soothe the tension inside through things like physical exercise, meditation, drawing, and reading, gradually overcoming the shadow of the past and regaining a positive attitude toward life and confidence.
I want to understand how to build good interpersonal relationships, and how to seek the support and help I need.

Building good interpersonal relationships is a process that takes long-term effort. It requires active and sincere participation in social activities, expressing your own views and needs, and trying to understand other people’s positions and thoughts, with mutual support and acceptance. At the same time, you can also seek professional social skills training and interpersonal communication counseling to strengthen your own expression and communication skills. If you encounter difficulties and challenges in life, don’t hesitate to seek help and support. You can reach out to relatives and friends around you, or to professional organizations, to receive timely guidance and comfort.
I feel like I’m in a state of loneliness and loss, and I don’t know how to regulate myself or release negative emotions.

When facing feelings of loneliness and loss, you can try looking for some enjoyable things and activities, such as listening to music, watching movies, reading, exercising, and so on. You can also take part in volunteer activities or social gatherings, and find like-minded people to talk with and share with. In addition, cultivate positive thinking and habits, such as recognizing your own strengths and good qualities, valuing your own growth and development, and maintaining a positive attitude toward life and positive actions. You can also use psychological counseling or therapy to understand and ease the roots of your negative emotions, and find solutions and a way forward that suit you.
Lately I’ve been feeling anxious all the time, and I don’t know what’s going on.
Hello. Difficult emotions can sometimes be caused by internal or external factors. Could you talk about whether there’s anything specific that’s been making you feel anxious?
Actually, I’m not really sure. I just feel like I’m always worried that something might happen.
I understand how you feel. We can try to help your emotions settle a bit. Would you be willing to do some deep breathing or gentle stretching with me?
Okay, thank you for the suggestion. I’ll give it a try.

You’re welcome. Taking some time to relax is really important. At the same time, you could also try writing down the things you’re worried about, so you can get a clearer sense of your feelings and thoughts.
Mm, I’ll give it a try. Thank you for your advice.
You’re welcome. I’m glad I can offer you some help. Try not to worry too much. This is just an emotion, and it won’t affect your life forever.
Okay, I’ll try not to think too much. Thank you for being here with me and supporting me.

I’m glad to be here with you. You can talk with me anytime, so don’t hesitate. You can also try to find some things to do that help you feel relaxed and happy, so you can feel more positive and face life’s challenges with more ease.
Okay, I’ll pay attention to that from now on. Thank you again for your encouragement and help.
You’re very welcome. I believe you’ll get better and better. If you need to, you can come talk with me anytime. I hope every day goes well for you!

I'm really worried. In the past, it was always my father who disciplined me and guided me. I remember when I was little, my mom was always working, so I had much less contact with her than with my father.
