Hello, I understand your worries. You have good memories of your own upbringing, and now you're worried that your relationship with your mom isn't what it used to be.

Yes. My father passed away five years ago, when I was still in high school. After that I lived with my mom, and I found that I feel like she's the kind of person who doesn't have her own opinions. Whatever other people say, she just follows along. She also doesn't really have any long-term goals, doesn't plan her life, and is always complaining that there are too many things to deal with.

Hearing how you describe your mom, I can feel your concern and care for her. A mother in a single-parent family carries a lot of pressure, and losing her husband also took away a lot of her strength. You could try talking with your mom, planning life together with her, and sharing each other's thoughts, so she can feel supported and encouraged.

But I feel like she doesn't have her own opinions, so it's hard to communicate with her. There is a relative whose thinking is more similar to mine, and I wanted to talk with her, but then I found that our views are very different too. Now I feel really troubled.

I can understand how you feel, but please remember that as your mom, her love and care for you will never change. Try to listen to her point of view, understand what she's thinking, and also give her time to adjust to this change. We can also communicate with her together, try to help her understand our thoughts, and let her know that we will always support her.

But now there is a relative who is taking it upon herself to manage my and my mom's lives, and it makes me very uncomfortable. My mom may know that she can't really give me any guidance, so she directly lets this relative keep more of an eye on me. But I don't agree with that. Parents should take care of their own children. That's the responsibility of being a parent.

Your thinking makes a lot of sense. I also think parents should take care of their own children, and parents should also encourage children to be independent and become their own person. But sometimes people interfere too much because they're worried about the child. You can find a quiet moment to have a good talk with your mom, let her know what you think, and also tell her that you want to solve the problems together with her, so she knows she has your support and love.
But right now I feel really torn. Sometimes I'm under a lot of pressure, and I'm also really worried that my relationship with my mom will become more and more tense.

I understand how you feel. Sometimes when our thoughts don't match our family's, it can make us feel confused and conflicted. But that doesn't have to make your relationship tense. Try to let go of some fixed ideas, and try new things together with your mom. Discover new interests and common ground with each other. This can help deepen the bond between you.
But right now I feel too tired, and I don't know what to do.

Let yourself relax. You don't need to keep pushing yourself to do better all the time. Try as much as possible to look at things with a positive mindset, and you may find that things are not as hard as we imagine, and not as bad either. What's important is to work together with your family to find ways to coordinate and resolve the issues, so everyone can feel happy and at ease.
Thank you for your advice and support. I'll try to put it into practice.

You're welcome. I believe you can handle the relationship between you and your mom well. You have talent, determination, and more importantly, you have love. No matter what happens, we are here to support you.

My mom died by suicide a little over three months ago. When I rushed into that dark, dirty, abandoned bike shed, I saw her in a terrifying state. They couldn’t save her. She didn’t leave me a single word. Since then, I’ve been scared. I don’t dare turn off the lights, I don’t dare sleep, I don’t dare be alone. I really want to know why she did this, where she is now, and whether she blames me. At the end of last year, my mom was diagnosed with late-stage cancer. She had been actively getting treatment, and after four rounds of chemo, her cancer cells were already under control. But my mom never believed it. She felt like she was about to die, like she wouldn’t get better. She refused anything positive and spent every day overthinking. She told my dad and my grandma that she was in a lot of pain. She also told me she wanted to die but didn’t dare kill herself. Why didn’t I take her mental state seriously? Why didn’t I believe her? Why was I still getting angry at her that day and saying hurtful things? That afternoon, she was gone. When she left, she must have been so hopeless, so disappointed in me. She didn’t even look at me once, and just left like that. My mom had always been healthy. I never thought she would get cancer, and I never imagined she would die by suicide. Every single day, I can’t make sense of it. I really want to ask her why. I also often think about the scene from the day she left, what she looked like. Is she suffering in hell now?

Thank you so much for having the courage to share this with me. Hearing what you’ve been through, I can feel the endless pain and longing inside you. Your mom is gone, she left you, and that has left you feeling afraid and at a loss. Please don’t blame yourself too much. You already did your best. Next, I’ll offer you some suggestions to help you get through this difficult place emotionally.
Thank you for encouraging me. But I’m still so sad. Why did my mom leave me? I want to know why she killed herself.

I can understand how you feel. But right now, what matters more is helping you get through this difficult time. The reasons your mom left are complicated. Maybe she couldn’t bear such enormous pain, or maybe her physical and mental state could no longer take any more pressure. Whatever the reason was, please don’t hate yourself or hate her. We need to learn to accept reality, and carry the longing for your mom in your heart. We also need to try to understand the difficulties she was going through.
I want to ask, what should I do now? I’m always wrapped up in those images and that pain. I hope there’s some effective way to ease my pain and anxiety.

Of course. We can try some things together. First, rest is very important. You need to sleep well and keep your body healthy. Second, you can try to speak out what’s in your heart and find someone you trust, such as your father, your grandma, or other relatives and friends, to talk with. They can give you a sense of safety. If you’re willing, you can also see a mental health professional and talk with them about how you feel. After you go back to school, you can go to the school counseling center, where professional counselors can help you.
I’ve talked about it. I told you all my feelings, and that makes me feel much better. Thank you.

I’m very glad I could help you. Feelings need to be expressed and shared. This is a process of being understood and receiving support. Now, we can talk about how you can take good care of yourself in the days ahead, and be gentle with your soul and your body.

I’ll try to communicate with my father and my grandma, and let them know I need their support. At the same time, I’ll try to quiet myself down, write down the days about my mom and the good memories she left behind, and work on moving forward.

Hang in there. You can do this. Try to notice what things might happen that can make you feel glad or happy. Ordinary things can also bring good surprises—maybe a scene, or a good book, or listening to stories your mom once told you, and feeling the happiness that was there before. In every day, in every moment, keep trying to build up positive energy and the ability to regulate yourself emotionally.
Thank you for your encouragement and support. I’ll do my best.

You’re welcome. I believe in you. Lastly, I have one small request: could you write our conversation down on paper, like a letter, and keep it as a memory? Maybe one day, you can pick up these words again and think of us, or when you need to, you can read them again and find your way back to your inner self.
These past few days, my emotions have felt really off. Right now I honestly feel like I'm about to fall apart.
Hearing how you're feeling, I can really understand how much you're struggling.
I've been crying so much that my head hurts, and I feel so confused.
Take a deep breath, and slowly breathe out. That can help ease some of the pressure.
I really want to jump off a building and kill myself, but I just can't bear to leave my mom and my grandpa. I'm afraid they would blame themselves and fall apart.

I really understand how you feel. Losing someone who is such an important source of support would bring your family unbearable pain. But you also need to know that saying it out loud can help ease the pain inside.
But I feel so awful right now, like I'm about to suffocate. Is there anything that can help relieve it a little?
Try finding some hobbies or activities to shift your energy and attention, like reading, listening to music, exercising, or talking with friends.
But I really don't want to talk to anyone. It feels like no one understands me.
Try not to shut anyone out too quickly. You can't predict how others will respond. When you want to talk to someone, if you open that door, others may also be glad to receive you.
I'll try... thank you.
You're welcome. We'll always be here to support you.

My grades used to be pretty good. Later, there were also a lot of people pursuing me, but I didn’t want to just casually get together with someone, so I never agreed. I’m 18 now. From elementary school to middle school and high school, there have been people pursuing me, but I never agreed. In middle school, I did date one boy, but we were only together for a little over ten days, and then that was it. He transferred schools, and I forgot about it. After I started high school, up until now, a lot of people have pursued me, but if I don’t like them, I just don’t agree.

I hear you saying that you’re also very firm in your choices. It takes courage to pursue the life you want. Although right now you may feel you’re not self-disciplined enough, you’ve already done what you believe is right.
Yeah, but I really like it when people praise me. Even though I didn’t say yes, I would imagine these romances in my mind.
That makes sense. We all need some praise and recognition. So, have you thought about how you might get that praise and recognition without hurting yourself?
I don’t know. I always feel like I’m having fewer and fewer ideas, and I don’t want to do anything anymore.

This is a very common situation. What you need right now is some rest and relaxation. You can try doing some things you usually enjoy, relax your body and mind, and let yourself think more clearly about what to do next.
I understand. I’ll do more things I like.
Good. You can also try finding some friends to talk with and share your feelings. Sometimes talking with friends can help you understand yourself better and find your direction.
Good idea. I’ll try to talk with my friends.
Also, you can learn some skills for coping with stress and emotions. For example, deep breathing, meditation, yoga, and so on can all help you balance your emotions.
I’ll try these techniques and see if they help.

Lastly, remember that you have your own right to choose and your own sense of control. Don’t let other people’s expectations and thoughts steer your life. Stay with your choices, and live your own life fully.
Thank you for your support and advice. I’ll really try.
I look forward to hearing good news from you. Hang in there!

Lately, whenever I get hurt or feel sad, I can’t control myself. I even want to hurt others or myself. When I’m in an extremely excited and unstable state, even my nerves hurt, and when I’m extremely sad, my heart feels uncomfortable too. I really don’t know what to do.

From what you’ve described, I understand that this may be caused by holding in too many negative emotions, and this kind of thing happens to many people. When people are young and experience negative emotions such as sadness, anger, helplessness, and so on, if they don’t receive acceptance from their parents—for example, if they aren’t allowed to cry or express fear or anger—then these negative emotions may be seen as bad, and the person may suppress and cut themselves off from them. In other words, this is a defense mechanism that develops while growing up. However, if someone doesn’t learn more mature ways of coping, this defense mechanism can keep being used, and the person may not be able to feel and express emotions normally. Negative emotions themselves carry energy, and when they’re suppressed for a long time, they will naturally erupt at some point, possibly being released in ways that hurt others or yourself. I suggest you learn to feel and express your emotions. If you can’t do that on your own, I’d recommend finding a counselor to help you work through it.
It’s really hard for me to face my emotions. I feel like I can’t control them.

Try not to blame yourself too much. Managing emotions really is a difficult task. It takes time to learn and practice, and it also requires continually seeking help and support. Besides finding a counselor, you can also start with small things, such as learning more about your emotions, trying to express them through writing or drawing, and gradually allowing yourself to accept and understand your emotions.
But I always feel like I don’t have the ability to manage my emotions. I always feel like I’m about to lose control, and that really scares me.

I can understand how you feel, but you need to know that controlling emotions is a gradual process; it can’t happen overnight. Losing control, or feeling out of control, is normal. What matters is that you’re aware of it and keep seeking help and support. During this process, you can also learn some stress-reduction and relaxation techniques, such as deep breathing, meditation, yoga, and so on. These techniques can help you relax and stabilize your emotions.
I’ll try. Thank you for your suggestions. But I always feel a bit lonely and helpless.

People always need support and companionship around them. You can try talking with the people around you about how you feel and seek their understanding and support. If you feel it’s very hard to face the people around you, you can also choose to seek professional help. A counselor will listen to what’s in your heart and help you work through the loneliness and helplessness inside. You could also join some support groups or volunteer activities to meet people who share similar values. You can become sources of strength for each other’s growth and support.
You’re right. I need to change my attitude and stop shutting myself away.

I’m very glad to hear you think this way. Changing yourself takes courage and patience, but as long as you make up your mind, hope is definitely ahead. No matter how difficult the situation you face is, you need to believe in your own strength and ability, and firmly believe that you can walk out of the darkness and welcome a better future.
Thank you for being here with me and supporting me. After hearing what you said, I feel much less stressed.

You’re welcome. I’m very willing to be your friend and supporter, to listen to what’s in your heart at any time and share in your joys. No matter when or where, we can get through difficult times together and welcome a better tomorrow.

Actually, I’ve never really been able to let it go, and I think about it a lot. When I was in second or third grade, I was sexually assaulted by a boy in middle school. Actually, he didn’t understand either—he just touched me, and rubbed his lower body against me. I didn’t understand anything at that time, and thought it was a game... Around fifth or sixth grade, I was online a lot. I had online relationships and things like that too, but the other person was about the same age, and nothing happened. Thinking about it now, I actually feel like I was always too lonely, and I did that because I wanted someone to keep me company. But then in the first year of middle school, I met a man online, he was probably 18. At first, we made a small group to chat, and didn’t chat one-on-one. A long time later, we started talking more, and then he said something about financially supporting me, but I didn’t understand. I thought it was just an online relationship like before, and I happily accepted. But a few weeks later he said he was coming to see me. I thought it was no big deal, but then the nightmare happened. In the car, he kissed me and touched me. I kept resisting. I even naively thought that getting a hotel room just meant he was very tired. Although I didn’t lose my virginity that day, I still feel like I’m not clean anymore. What should I do after having experiences like this? I can’t forget it. I think about it when I sleep. I really hate myself and feel disgusted with myself.

Hi, I know it feels really painful to have gone through something like this. Sending you a warm hug. What you went through was very unfortunate—being touched when you were little, and later being financially supported by someone, with the other person acting unreasonably, leaving you feeling like you’re not clean and with a psychological shadow. But what I want to tell you is that none of this was your fault. Don’t pay the price for someone else’s mistakes. You were young, unaware, and innocent at the time, so you didn’t have the ability to protect yourself, and that’s understandable. But now you’re an adult, and you don’t need to let anything hurt you again.

Thank you for comforting me. I’m really grateful. But I’m still very afraid, and I feel very unsafe. I used to be full of expectations and fantasies about love, but now it feels unfamiliar and scary. I don’t know what to do, or how to face life again.

Actually, in this situation, what’s needed is to seek professional psychological support and help. Because your situation is relatively complex, you need a professional to provide you with advice and guidance. At the same time, you can also try taking part in some social activities, expanding your social circle, and talking more with people you trust, to ease your loneliness and reduce your uncertainty about the future. Also, don’t easily trust strangers online, so you can avoid being hurt in a similar way again.

Thank you for your suggestions. I’ll try to do that. But it’s still very hard for me to let go. Toward that boy and that man, I always have some fear and hatred in my heart. What can I do to let it go?

First, I think you need to try to accept that what they did was wrong, and recognize that you can’t change the past. Thinking about how to prevent similar things from happening again is what matters most. At the same time, you can also take the initiative to seek counseling and get more professional, more effective help. After all, using the right treatment approach is the key to solving the problem, and to allowing yourself to gain positive growth from negative experiences.

Mm, I understand. Actually, there’s a lot of knowledge now about sexual issues and protecting yourself, and I’ll go learn about it. I also think communicating with family and friends is a good way to work through the problem. I’ll think about it more deeply. Thank you for your suggestions. I’m really grateful.
You’re welcome. I’m very glad I could help you. In life, it’s hard to avoid setbacks and difficulties, but I believe you can be strong and brave, and face everything in the future. Hang in there!

I don’t know how to live. Living feels so exhausting. Since I was little, I was excellent in both character and studies. My parents raised me like some kind of wealthy young gentleman, and didn’t let me learn anything outside the “proper” path. They kept pushing me to move upward toward what was lofty, and because of that I became arrogant about my talent and suffered quite a few big setbacks. It wasn’t until I grew up that I realized I had become someone with nothing. Low self-esteem and timidity became the main theme of my life. I don’t dare do anything, and I’m afraid of doing anything wrong. I think I should be perfect, that I should be able to take care of everything, that everything should go the way I want. But I can’t change my looks, and I can’t change my personality. I once felt that because of these flaws, life had no meaning at all, and that I might as well die. But now I’ve barely held on and am trying to fill the emptiness by looking for new meaning in life. But I’m still very afraid and empty. Every day I can’t sleep well; I have insomnia and anxiety, and I don’t know how to face tomorrow. No matter how much I think about it, I can’t find a foolproof solution. I feel like only death would be a release.

Hello. Reading what you shared, I can feel how troubled you are. First, I want to give you a hug. I hope this hug can give you even a little bit of strength, and help you feel that love still exists in this world.
Thank you for comforting me. I feel awful, like I’ve been isolating myself all along.

Actually, you haven’t cut yourself off. It’s just that your thoughts are making you feel that way. As someone who was excellent in both character and studies from a young age and deeply loved by your parents, you have your own strengths and advantages. It may seem like no one around you can understand how you feel, but in fact, there will always be people who can understand you and be there with you.
Sometimes I really can’t feel that love exists. I don’t know whether my parents truly care about me or not.

Sometimes parents may not express love in words. But they definitely care about you very much. When you were little, they may have used their own ways, like good food or fun things, to express their love. But as we grow up, we no longer just ask for good food and fun things; we begin to think about the meaning of life. Adler once said that searching for the meaning of life is itself the most meaningless thing. Because the meaning of life is something we decide and define for ourselves. Right now, what you need to do is set a life goal for yourself that can help you keep living.
But I have absolutely no idea how to do that. I feel like such a failure, like there’s no meaning, and I’m really, really sad.

This kind of situation is very normal. For now, you can first try having breakfast with your family every morning. When you go to work each day, you can joke freely with your coworkers. When you come home at night, you can read novels and let your mood rise and fall with what the main character goes through. Being able to have a good mood every day is not an easy thing either, and that is also very meaningful. Smiles can be passed on—don’t forget that.
Thank you for your advice and encouragement. But I feel like I have so many flaws, and they make me feel very inferior and incapable.
Everyone has their strengths and weaknesses. Since you’ve discovered your shortcomings, you should work harder to correct them. That way, you can truly set a goal for yourself.
But I’m not good-looking either. I can’t change anything.

Your looks do not determine everything about you. You still have a very outstanding heart. In my eyes, you are someone different, and your excellence is not determined by your appearance. Everyone has their own beauty; we just need to discover it.
Thank you for your encouragement. I’ll try to look for the good things in life and set my own goals.

That is exactly the point. You need to learn to look at the world around you through a different lens, and to discover the beautiful parts of everything. Summer is very hot, but the sky really is blue, and the moon goes to work with a halo of light around it. I hope my response can give you some inspiration and courage. You have a truly outstanding soul. Hang in there!

Lately, when I’m getting along with my mom, I don’t know why, but as soon as she says something wrong or says something unreasonable, I can’t help losing my temper, and then we end up arguing. I want to control my temper a bit, or find a suitable outlet. I’m looking for support and advice.

I completely understand how you feel. This kind of situation can really be upsetting. First, you need to recognize that no matter how angry you get, you can’t change what the other person says. But you can control your own response. Next, you can try slowing your breathing and calmly thinking about why you’re reacting that way. Think about whether there are some hidden emotions that need to be released. In this process, you can find an appropriate outlet, like going for a run or writing in a journal. This can help you manage your emotions, while also not causing harm to your family.

Thank you for your advice. I really do need to find an appropriate outlet. I’ve tried communicating with my mom before, but we always get caught in a spiral of arguing, and I already feel very helpless.

Of course, communication is very important, but sometimes conversations can become very emotional, and that may make things worse. You can choose to talk with your mom when you’re calm, and try to let her hear your thoughts and feelings, while also trying to listen to her perspective. If both of you have calmed down, maybe there will be a better outcome.
I understand. I’ll try to control my emotions and communicate with my mom when I’m calm.

Okay. Another important point is that you need to pay attention to your emotional state and protect your inner self. You can do some things at home that make you feel comfortable and relaxed, like listening to music or meditating.
These sound pretty good. I want to try them. But even if I try to stay calm, sometimes I still get angry because of what my mom says. What should I do?

That’s okay. This is an ongoing process. If you feel like you really can’t control your emotions, don’t blame yourself. You can try shifting your attention and doing something else. At the same time, you can also try talking to a friend, or see a mental health professional for help. Remember, don’t feel ashamed or frightened by your emotions.
Okay, I’ll try these methods. Do you have any other suggestions?

Of course. Another important point is to maintain a positive mindset. You need to set some small goals for yourself and keep making a little progress each day. Don’t expect to change all the problems in a short time. In the process of improving your relationship with your family, you may feel frustrated or discouraged, but if you keep a positive mindset, you’ll definitely be able to get through these difficulties.
Thank you for your advice. I’ll work hard to improve my emotions, and I also hope I can build a better relationship with my mom.
You’re doing great. I believe you can definitely do this. If you need help, don’t hesitate to contact me anytime.

Recently I (male, 26) met a woman. We both know a bit about psychology—she’s 31 and has been involved with psychology for 3 years, and I’ve been involved with it for about 7 years. We both want to grow and are willing to grow. I feel like it’s really rare to meet someone you can grow together with. I haven’t been pursuing her for long, but I can feel that she’s a little interested in me too, and I understand what she means. But I learned from our mutual friend that she’s a bit older—31, while I’m 26. I’m a little bothered by the age gap, but I’m also not sure whether I’ll be able to meet someone else who can grow together with me. I’m really torn, and my mind feels very messy. I don’t know whether I should keep pursuing her...

Hello! Reading your message, I can sense your confusion around this relationship issue. You and this woman share an interest in studying psychology, which is wonderful, but do you really understand your own needs? When you’re pursuing her, are you hoping to find a partner, or are you just looking for a study companion? If you want to find a partner you feel drawn to, then age isn’t that important. Many women nowadays pay a lot of attention to taking care of themselves, and relationships where the woman is older are becoming more and more common. Also, if both of you are willing to grow together, then age really isn’t an issue. Don’t miss out on a good relationship because of age. But if you’re only looking for a study companion, then you can keep looking for someone else. You need to clarify your own thoughts and needs, so that you can make the right decision. I hope my response can help you.

Thank you for your advice. I do feel really torn right now. Although I really like this woman, the age gap does make me a little worried. But you’re right—if we’re both willing to grow together, age isn’t really a problem. Can you give me some more advice?

Of course. I’d suggest that you try to get to know each other more deeply, and understand each other’s needs and thoughts from the heart. You can talk with her about how you see this relationship and see what she thinks. If the two of you have the same views and goals, then you can work together to achieve those goals. At the same time, don’t worry too much about the age issue. As long as both of you feel happy and comfortable, age really isn’t that important. Also, don’t care too much about what other people think. Your relationship is between the two of you, and other people’s opinions don’t really matter.

I’ll try to communicate with her more deeply and understand each other’s needs and thoughts. At the same time, I’ll also have confidence in my own feelings and not worry too much about the age issue. Thank you for your support.

You’re doing well. In this relationship, what you need is communication and mutual support. If you feel confused or uncertain, don’t hesitate—have a focused conversation with her. And don’t forget to pay attention to your own feelings. If the relationship between you makes you happy and comfortable, then keep going! I believe you two can grow together and be happy.
Thank you for your encouragement and support. I’ll really try to communicate with her, pay attention to my own feelings, and believe that we can grow together and be happy.

No problem. Anytime you need my help and support, please be sure to let me know. I’ll always support you. At the same time, don’t put too much pressure on yourself. Everything will get better. Hang in there!
Thank you for your support and care. I’ll keep a positive attitude and keep working hard to move forward. If I need to, I’ll continue to ask you for help. Thank you!
No problem. You’re welcome to reach out for help anytime. You’ve got this!

I feel awful. The counselor I saw before required me not to see any other counselors at the same time, and gave me three chances. Once I did look for someone else, I had to end counseling with him. Now I’m really scared of counseling. I don’t dare look for a male counselor again, and I’ve refused contact with anyone. It’s been more than half a year already.

It sounds like you were really hurt. That rule from this counselor is really strange, and it sounds somewhat unhealthy. Thinking about it carefully, could it be that this counselor was using psychological techniques—commonly called PUA—to control you? This is not very normal, and you need to come out of it. The counseling field has all kinds of people in it, and you may have been deceived. You should find a reliable counselor again.

Actually, I’ve always had very high expectations of counselors. At the beginning, I was really happy to be able to get his help, and I was also somewhat dependent on him. But I always felt uncomfortable, and only later did I realize that he had indeed exerted some control over me.

It seems this counselor really did exert too much control over you. Why not try changing your expectations a bit? Find a new counselor and see whether you can build a healthier relationship with them.
I’m really scared to look for a new counselor now. I don’t dare face them.

I can understand your fear, but for your own sake, you have to take that step. Try looking for counselors who are professional and make you feel comfortable. They will understand your concerns and give you the best support.
I know what you’re saying is right, but I’ve kept putting it off and haven’t taken action. I feel like I’ve let my family and friends down.

Remember, you’re not fighting this alone. Your family and friends will support every decision you make. If you don’t take action now and stay stuck for a long time in fear of counseling, it won’t be good for your health. Take action and start again.
I’ll take action as soon as possible. Thank you for your encouragement and support.
I want to say that you’ve already been very brave. Recognizing your own problem and actively seeking help is a very big step. Don’t be afraid. We’re all here to support you.
I've been feeling a bit anxious lately. How should I look at this feeling? And how should I live with it?

Hello! I understand how you feel. Anxiety, as an emotion, can affect our thoughts and behavior. When it comes to anxiety, I personally think the reasons it arises vary from person to person, but there are many different ways to address it. You can try to find the source of your anxiety and take steps accordingly to ease it.
That's true. I feel like anxiety can make me feel really uncomfortable sometimes. I don't know how to calm it down.

It’s okay. Everyone experiences anxiety, and it is possible for us to coexist with it peacefully. Try to see anxiety as a friend, accept it, and face it calmly. In doing so, you may find that anxiety doesn’t cause too much disruption in your life.
I’d like to know some specific ways to deal with anxiety. Do you have any suggestions?

When you are strong enough inside, anxiety is just a temporary emotion. So you can practice meditation, deep breathing, journaling, and so on to help yourself become more peaceful and calm. At the same time, you can also seek help from professionals, who can give you more specific suggestions.
I’ll try these methods, but I’ll still worry that I won’t be able to cope with anxiety in the future.

I understand your worry, but please believe in yourself. No matter when or where, you can find support and comfort within yourself. It’s important to express your feelings and look for support and understanding. At the same time, you can also actively take part in activities you enjoy, so you can feel happier and more relaxed.
Thank you for your suggestions. I’ll work hard to cope with the feeling of anxiety.

You’re welcome. I’m glad I could help you. Believe in yourself—you can definitely overcome feelings of anxiety and have a happy life. If you need more support and help, you’re always welcome to contact me.
I always feel anxious and scared, and I also get gastrointestinal heat and feverishness. What should I do?
Dear, good morning. I really understand how you feel. First of all, you’ve already become aware of your own issue, and that’s the first step toward getting better.
Thank you. But I don’t know where the root of my anxiety is. What should I do?

We can work together to find the root of it. Generally speaking, anxiety comes from uncertainty about unknown events and a lack of a sense of control. In this situation, we can use deep breathing and dialogue with yourself and your subconscious to help yourself believe that you can handle this. For a specific situation, we can try role-playing or mental rehearsal, find the approach and details, and build confidence.
Okay, I’ll try this method. But my gastrointestinal tract has been uncomfortable. What should I do?

We can take two approaches. First, I suggest going to the hospital to get checked and treat the physical symptoms. At the same time, improving your physical functioning and exercising more can help improve gastrointestinal motility.
Okay, thank you for your advice. Then after I finish doing something, how should I give myself feedback?

That’s a very good question. After completing something, we should acknowledge our own efforts, identify where we succeeded, and also find areas we can improve. Believe that you can do it. I’m rooting for you.
Thank you for your support and advice. I feel much better. I’ll definitely keep working at it.
I’m very glad I could help you. Remember, we’ll always be by your side, supporting you.

I’m 24, and my girlfriend is 22. We’ve been together for 4 years. Over these four years, we’ve argued almost every month. They’re usually small arguments, though occasionally they get really intense. Her issues are especially hard to describe. She can’t accept other people disagreeing with her or explaining things, especially me. Whether she’s right or wrong, she just wants others to listen to her. Even if she knows she’s wrong, she’ll find other reasons to argue her case. With things she doesn’t really know much about, she’ll also act like she understands them very well, which ends up making things awkward for her.

Hello! I’m sorry to hear that you argue so often. That can be a burden on both your mood and your relationship. I can understand why this is troubling for you. It sounds like communication with your girlfriend may be somewhat difficult. Here, I’d like to share some suggestions with you, and I hope they may help with your situation.
Thank you. Could you share some specific suggestions?

When your girlfriend runs into an issue, she may need more support and understanding rather than disagreement or explanations. Perhaps her worry about being negated comes from a certain event, or from a lack of trust in herself. You can let her know that her feelings are acknowledged and understood. This can be very helpful for her emotions and for the relationship.
I understand. So what should I do?

In your conversations, you can help your girlfriend feel your understanding and respect, offer support when she runs into problems, and express your understanding and sympathy. If the view she expresses is different from yours, you can gently express your own perspective rather than directly arguing back.
Okay, I’ll give it a try.

In addition, the key is to stay calm and patient. Staying calm and understanding in communication, and helping her feel your trust and respect, is the foundation for building good communication. If emotions rise, it’s better to pause and calm down first, and then communicate again after emotions have settled.
Mm, I’ll pay attention to that.
Finally, I suggest that you interact regularly to deepen your understanding of each other and your emotional connection. This is very beneficial for the healthy development of the relationship.
Okay, I’ll try to strengthen my interaction with my girlfriend.
I wish you both good luck. I hope you can successfully resolve the issues and build a healthier, better relationship.
Lately I’ve been feeling anxious all the time, and I haven’t been sleeping well. I wanted to find someone to talk to.

Hello, I really understand how you’re feeling. Anxiety can affect our physical and mental health. You can try to relax, like listening to music or doing deep breathing, and also find a safe, comfortable place to talk about your feelings.
I’m really afraid of being laughed at or misunderstood by others.

That feeling is very normal. We all have times when we need to be understood and accepted. You can talk to someone you trust, or seek help from a professional counselor. They will fully respect your thoughts and feelings.
I’ve always felt like I don’t have much ability, like I’m useless.

Everyone has their own strengths and weaknesses. Try to focus on your strengths and the things you’ve achieved, and give yourself a little more affirmation and support. Also, doing things you like can build confidence and make life richer and more interesting.
But I’m really tired. I don’t want to do anything, and I always feel like there’s no hope.

Feeling tired or low can be one of the symptoms of depression. We can try to find some positive things to do, like exercising or spending time with friends. These can help us feel more energized and more confident in facing life. If these methods don’t help, you can seek help from a mental health professional.
I’m really grateful that you can stay with me and talk. I feel like I have some new ideas now.
You’re welcome. I’m very willing to offer you support and listen. No matter when or where, we have friends we can rely on, and we can face life’s challenges together.

Lately I suddenly realized I don’t feel anything for anyone anymore. Even when I try to change myself, it doesn’t really help. I don’t have that feeling I used to have with my family, friends, or partner, like I couldn’t bear to lose them. Even if they treat me really well, I don’t feel much; if they treat me badly, I don’t get especially angry either. I don’t even feel much toward my parents anymore, and I don’t even have the mindset I used to have of needing to study hard and earn money so they could have a good life. I’m careless about studying too, I just can’t take anything in, and my memory is getting worse so fast. I really want to remember the beautiful memories I had with them before, but I can’t recall them. I don’t know what to do. This mindset has lasted for a month, and I feel like maybe there’s still hope for me, right? What should I do? I want to go back to being a person with flesh and blood, with feelings.

Hello, I can understand how you’re feeling right now. From what you’ve described, you may be going through a period of emotional numbness. This state may be related to your experiences growing up, or to stress and setbacks in your current life. It seems to be creating inner conflict for you. Through deeper counseling, we can explore these possible causes and help you find practical, effective ways to address it.
Thank you for understanding. I’ve thought a lot about it, but I still can’t solve it. I feel like I’m under a lot of pressure, but I don’t know where it’s coming from.

I understand that what you’re facing right now is very difficult. You need to pay more attention to your emotional needs. We can explore the sources of pressure in areas such as your life, work, and relationships, and work on the difficulties you’re facing.
I just want to treat my own mind well, but right now I can’t focus on myself at all. I feel like I’m in self-exile.

This is a common emotional experience, and we can work on easing it by building strategies for self-attention and self-care. You could consciously let yourself change environments, do some interesting things, and pick up hobbies you used to enjoy. If this situation continues for more than a month, I suggest you see a professional mental health doctor to seek a more in-depth treatment plan.

You’re right. I can try to step back from my environment and relationships so I can think carefully about my emotional needs, and I’ll also seek help from a professional mental health doctor to work through this problem.
Good. You’ve already taken the first step. I hope that with the help of professional psychotherapy, you can find yourself again and rebuild your sense of self.
Thank you for your encouragement. I know what to do now. With direction and help, I believe I can overcome this problem.
That’s right. Let’s work together for your future and your happiness. Please remember, you are never alone; we are all here supporting you.
Lately my mind has been a complete mess. Because of the pressure from work and life, I feel like I’m barely hanging on. I don’t know how to get out of this state. Can you help me?

It sounds like you’re very tense. It may help to take some steps to relax your body and mind, such as doing yoga, meditating, or using relaxation exercises. Also, when you have time, you could meet up with two or three friends, or help other people. That can strengthen your social connections and ease stress.
I always have a hard time falling asleep, and my sleep quality at night is very poor. This has affected my work and life. What should I do?

I suggest relaxing your body and mind before going to sleep, such as listening to soft music or taking a hot bath. Or you could lie in bed and silently repeat some positive affirmations. Doing these things can help you fall asleep more quickly and stop worrying and feeling troubled.

Sometimes the words get stuck in my chest, and even when my face turns red, I still can’t get them out. When people ask me something, I can only answer with simple sounds like “mm” or “ah.” I want to speak but can’t get the words out. I want to explain something, but it comes out as a complete mess. It feels really awful. How can I get out of this situation?

It sounds a bit like social difficulty. It may come from a lack of confidence, a low sense of self-acceptance, and caring too much about other people’s evaluations. The reason this happens may be related to your upbringing, personality, and so on. So rebuilding confidence is key. A confident person can respond to their environment with ease, accept their own blushing, accept that they sometimes don’t do well, and not care too much about others’ evaluations. Let me share three steps for rebuilding confidence: First, focus on your strengths. Write down ten strengths on a piece of paper, no matter what area they are in, such as being careful, having nice eyes, and so on—the more the better. When you take part in different activities, think about these strengths and tell yourself what strengths you have. This can help you improve your confidence in doing these activities. This is called the “spillover effect of confidence.” This effect is very helpful for improving confidence. Second, build an outward image of confidence. First of all, keeping a neat and appropriate appearance helps strengthen a person’s confidence. Second, act with confidence, such as looking straight ahead when walking. It may feel unfamiliar at first, but after some time, confidence will come from within. Also, paying attention to exercise and maintaining a fit body is very helpful for strengthening confidence. Third, learn to smile. Smiling can increase a sense of happiness, which in turn strengthens confidence.
My mood is full of anxiety and unease. I’m always very negative, and I often feel depressed. What should I do?

To ease depression and negative emotions, I suggest taking positive actions to improve your low mood, such as socializing, exercising, or doing art. In addition, you can also improve your mental state through reading, learning, and participating in volunteer activities. When you run into difficulties, don’t get overly stuck in your emotions. Learn to accept your emotions and face the facts, and with the help of friends, family, and professional doctors, take things step by step to get through the difficulty.
Sometimes I feel like I’m not as good as other people and that I don’t have any strengths. I often have thoughts of denying myself. How can I get rid of them?

Self-denial is an unnecessary negative emotion, and it can have a negative impact on your mental state. You need to look at yourself in a positive way and break free from the influence of negative emotions. Remember, no one is perfect, and everyone has strengths. You need to work on discovering your own strengths and make the most of them while avoiding your weaknesses. At the same time, have your own goals and ideals, and keep both your body and mind healthy. All of these can help improve your self-acceptance and help you reach your goals.
I feel like I’m very tired, and I don’t have much motivation left to pursue my dreams.

Good rest can help you pursue your dreams in a more positive way. You can recharge through sleep or leisure. You can also spend time with friends or family and get closer to nature. Give yourself some time and space to process things and enjoy life. The strength for your dreams may begin from there.
I often feel like my sense of presence is very low, and that other people don’t care about me.

People may often overlook or not understand your presence, but that doesn’t mean your existence isn’t important. Everyone has difficulties and shortcomings. You need to pay attention to yourself and rebuild your emotional support system. Communicate with people who truly care about you, and find inspiration and advice. In addition, you can also find your own social circle by taking part in recreational activities or volunteer service, so that you can gain a stronger sense of presence.
I’m always very afraid of being rejected. Because of all kinds of pressure in life, I feel like I have to be extremely careful with every step. How can I remove this tension?

Your issue seems to be a lack of a sense of security, so you need to patiently build that sense of security. This especially requires you to meet your own needs and pay attention to emotional relationships. You can try using relaxation skills to ease the pressure, such as breathing exercises or meditation. In addition, you can also increase your confidence and sense of self-security by taking care of yourself, such as eating healthily and exercising appropriately.
I’m not in a good mood. I always feel really anxious, and sometimes my emotions are all over the place.

I’m sending you a hug. I can understand how you’re feeling right now. Anxiety and mood swings are common psychological difficulties. We all go through these emotional ups and downs, so don’t isolate yourself. Let’s explore this together—what factors are bringing up your worries about the future?
I’m afraid the future will become really bad. I can’t control my own life, and I feel like I lack a sense of security.

Hearing you say that, I feel very concerned. We all face the unknown; this isn’t something you’re dealing with alone. We can start with small things in the present and practice intentionally, gradually building your confidence and sense of control. Have you thought about doing anything to reduce your stress?
Sometimes I try some relaxing activities, but they don’t really ease my emotions.

That’s good—at least you’re consciously noticing your emotions and trying to relax. But it may take trying different methods to find the way of easing things that suits you best. For example, you could try meditation, breathing exercises, or deep relaxation training. Do you think it might be worth a try?
I always feel like I can’t do things well, and I even doubt my own abilities.

Hearing you say this, I can understand how you’re feeling right now. But I believe everyone has their own strengths and areas they’re good at, and no one is perfect. We often only see other people’s polished sides and strengths, while overlooking our own. If you’re still very worried, you could try some new learning experiences and challenges, giving yourself more chances to experience growth and success.
But even when I accomplish certain things, I still feel very empty, without any sense of satisfaction.

I understand how you feel. Sometimes we always feel like it’s not enough, and we overlook the achievements we’ve made. What’s important is that we learn how to appreciate what we’ve accomplished and develop an inner sense of satisfaction. Some training in self-awareness and values-oriented work may be helpful. We can also explore together how to build a more positive mindset and make life feel more meaningful.
Once I run into a setback, I feel like I’m going to fail, and I give up very easily.

This is a common negative thinking pattern. We need to work on moving away from it in order to have a more positive attitude. In fact, setbacks are unavoidable on the path of growth, and everyone encounters them. We can help ourselves cope better with difficulties through self-affirmation, seeking support from others, and slowly building our abilities.
I always find it hard to fall asleep, and sometimes I even have insomnia.

Good sleep is an important part of our mental health. If you’ve been having insomnia, you can also try starting with improving your sleep. For example, creating a regular daily schedule, making sure you get enough exercise and maintain healthy eating habits, and reducing time spent using electronic devices. You can try some of these strategies to ease the insomnia.
It’s hard for me to control my anxiety and irritability.

That’s very normal. Anxiety and irritability are part of our emotional experience. But we can use some techniques to soothe our emotions. For example, targeted relaxation through breathing relaxation, meditation, or exercise. At the same time, seeking support from others is also very important. Don’t forget that the people around you support you.
Thank you for your help. What you said makes me feel very comforted.

I’m very glad to hear you say that. Remember, you’re not alone. I’m here with you as you face these issues, and we can get through this difficult time together. Let’s face the challenges ahead more positively and meet each day’s challenges together.
I recently found out he’s married, and I want to confront him in person and ask whether he has children, and what he was thinking through all of this. But I also feel like all of that is unnecessary.

Listening to you, I feel like you’re in a stress response, maybe because you’ve encountered something that has really upset you. You said you want to move on quickly, and I think that’s what you’re hoping for yourself. Do you want to move on from the shock, or from that relationship?
I think I want to move on from both.

It sounds like you’re finding it hard to let go of your worries about this relationship, and you still want to understand his past. These thoughts are very normal. I understand that you feel unwilling to accept how this ended, but the process may be very painful for you. You may need to actively try to accept your life as it is now.
I feel really awful. I want to understand his situation, but I’m also worried I won’t be able to face it.

It takes courage and determination to learn the truth, and that’s understandable. Still, you could choose a day when you feel emotionally steady and ask him to meet and talk. That might give you some answers, and it could also help you face the future better.
Mm, thank you for the suggestion. But I’m still worried that I won’t be able to control my emotional ups and downs.

Managing emotions isn’t easy. Sometimes we have to face our emotions, experience them, and then let them go. You can try some ways to help keep yourself emotionally steady, such as breathing exercises, exercise, meditation, and so on.
Okay, I’ll give it a try. Thank you for listening to me all this time.
I’m also glad I can help you. I hope you can face life with a positive attitude. No matter what the future brings, there will be good outcomes.
Thank you for your support and blessings. I’ll hang in there.
Of course. I’ll always be here to support you.

Lately I’ve been really sensitive. I feel like whenever I get sick or just don’t feel well, it must be something very serious, or that these discomforts are signs of some serious illness. It makes me very tense and makes it hard to fall asleep. I know these thoughts are too sensitive, but I just can’t stop these negative thoughts. What should I do?

Hearing how you feel, I really understand how troubling this is for you. Actually, we all have our own worries and fears, but we can also use some methods to ease these emotions, such as relaxation techniques. You can start learning some breathing and meditation techniques when you’re calm, and these can help you maintain a better mental state. You can try using relaxation techniques to manage your emotions and anxiety.
Will doing that help? I always feel like I don’t have the self-control to deal with these emotions.

Actually, for anxiety and fear, relaxation training and meditation can sometimes be quite effective. Of course, if you feel like it’s hard to control yourself, you’re overly tense, or you have symptoms like difficulty breathing or a racing heartbeat, you can try easing these emotions through methods such as talking things out with yourself or seeking professional counseling. These methods can help you understand your emotions and problems, and make sure you get appropriate help and support.
How can I better understand and manage my emotions?

Emotion management is a long-term process that requires ongoing exploration and trying things out. You can try assertiveness training, understand your strengths and limitations, and build your sense of self-worth and confidence, so you can better handle emotions and difficulties. You can also build a better self-image by reaching goals and achieving goals, which can help you have better control over your emotions.
Sometimes bad things suddenly come to mind, and it’s hard to control those negative thoughts. Do you have any suggestions?

In this situation, you can try analyzing your thoughts and asking yourself some questions. For example, are these thoughts really reasonable? Could there be other, better solutions? By asking yourself these questions, you can better understand your thoughts and put your focus on solving the problem. At the same time, you can also try shifting your attention and putting more energy into doing things that are more meaningful and positive, which can reduce the impact of negative emotions.
That sounds very reasonable. But I’m still worried that I won’t be able to control those thoughts.

Don’t worry. This is a process that takes time. We can try to find your own sources of enjoyment and hobbies, so you can stay in a happy and positive state. At the same time, you can also think about some positive things, such as the future and achievements you hope for. These can help you better control your emotions and thoughts.
I’m also a little worried—could I have a psychological problem?

If you feel the symptoms are serious and are affecting your life and normal work, I suggest you seek consultation with a professional mental health doctor as soon as possible. Psychological problems are not uncommon, and this also means we need to pay more attention to our mental health and take timely steps to intervene. Also, professionals can better understand your issues and needs, and help you find solutions.
I’ll consider consulting a professional. Thank you very much for your help and suggestions. I’ll practice according to the suggestions you gave me.

You’re welcome. My role is to help and support you. I believe you can get through this difficult time and become stronger and more confident. Remember, you’re not alone. We’re here and willing to listen to your feelings and hear about your difficulties. Feel free to contact me anytime if you need to.

I was born into a very traditional extended family. My father used to be a government official, and my mother is the kind of career woman who is also a good wife and mother. Before I turned 30, I was once a very successful employee. But over these past six years, my business failed, my relationship failed, and my parents have put all their energy into paying attention to me and helping me find a job. Gradually, I’ve become like a giant baby. I have no choices and no self-respect left. I feel humiliated, like I’m somehow incompetent. But I also can’t leave them or ignore their feelings. Before I’ve even processed my own emotions, I have to deal with their emotional ups and downs. What should I choose?

Hello. I’m sorry to hear that you’re feeling so troubled. But you know, everyone goes through low points, and failure doesn’t mean you’re worthless. What you’ve been through shows that you must be someone with heart and ambition. Reflecting on the factors behind this failure may help you become clearer about your future direction and perspective. No one can guarantee that everything will go smoothly. As long as you can find experience and lessons in failure, it can also count as a successful new start. What I’d like to remind you is that we should be grateful for our parents’ care and support, but we also can’t rely on them to direct our lives. You need to have your own goals and sense of achievement in order to get along better with others. If needed, you might try communicating with them honestly, telling them that you need to handle some things independently, and discussing how to divide responsibilities and support. That can also give you better space to grow and become independent.

What you said makes a lot of sense. I feel much better than before now, and I can think about it more openly. But I’m still not very brave about facing my parents. I’m afraid they won’t understand or that they’ll be put off by it.

That’s very normal. Many people worry that communicating with family will lead to conflict. But what I’d like to remind you is that as long as there is sincere communication and understanding, you can gain each other’s support and understanding. You can first prepare yourself mentally, clarify your own thoughts and needs, and then find a suitable time and way to face them honestly. Don’t rush for results or avoid it. I believe you can handle these things well.
I feel a little afraid to face the future. I don’t know whether I can get out from under this shadow.

About the uncertainty of the future, I want to say that everyone experiences it. But don’t give up on yourself because of that. Instead, try to face it actively and make changes. You can try setting some small goals, and through ongoing effort and achieving them, strengthen your confidence and courage. At the same time, pay attention to changes in your emotions and adjust your mindset in time, so you don’t fall into negativity and self-doubt. I believe you have the ability and wisdom to face and overcome your difficulties. Do well with the present, and the future will surely get better.
I’ll do my best to think and take action. Thank you for your encouragement and support.

You’re welcome. I believe you can do it. If you need to, feel free to come and talk with me anytime. I’m willing to work together with you. I hope you can come out from under this shadow soon and move forward happily and healthily.
Thank you for your help and understanding. I feel much more at ease.

You’re very welcome. I’m only doing what little I can, and I hope I can give you some positive thoughts and encouragement. Remember, you are a capable and valuable person. Any setbacks and failures are only making you stronger and more mature. I hope you can continue pursuing your dreams and enjoy the beauty and joy in life.
Thank you. I’ll cherish myself and the people around me, and actively pursue a higher state in life.

That’s wonderful. I can see that you have a lot of confidence and self-awareness. As long as you keep this attitude and keep taking action, you’ll definitely achieve even better results. I’ll always be here rooting for you!

Lately I’ve been feeling some pressure in my relationship with my boyfriend. Sometimes worrying too much can pull you into negative emotions, so try to relax your mind a little~

Try taking the initiative to communicate with him again. Maybe he just wants to understand you more. Sometimes our worries are unnecessary. You can try telling him that you also have shortcomings, and that can help you understand and support each other more.
That’s true. I think I need to learn to communicate more proactively and not keep problems buried inside. But sometimes I really don’t know how to answer his questions.

It’s okay. Don’t blame yourself just because you can’t answer. You can try telling him the truth, and you can also learn together and improve your skills. If you run into something difficult, you can also talk to me about it~

Right. I’ll learn to communicate more proactively, and I’ll also bravely admit my shortcomings. I also wanted to ask you: in the past, when I was feeling down, I would often think that I wasn’t worthy of being loved by others. Is that normal?

People think in different ways depending on their emotional state, and when you’re feeling down, your thoughts may be more negative. But you need to believe that everyone has value and deserves to be loved, and you are no exception. Try to face your emotions, seek help and support, and let yourself grow through adversity.

Thank you for your answer. Your words made me feel much more at ease. I’ll work on stopping my negative thinking habits. If I run into problems in the future, I’ll also talk to people more, and not let myself fall into lonely feelings.
That’s great. You’re already a very brave person. I believe you’ll get better and better. I hope everything goes smoothly for you in your life ahead, and that you’re happy~
Thank you, really. Being able to find someone who listens to me and gives me support really makes me feel very lucky. I’ll live well and love myself well, and I wish you all the best too~
That’s what I’m here for. I hope you stay safe and happy, and you’re always welcome to come chat with me anytime~

Recently, because of the pandemic, I haven’t been able to go back to work, so I’ve stayed home for two months. At first it was okay, because I knew work wouldn’t start again that soon. But now the company is already getting ready to resume work, and I still haven’t received a clear notice. That’s making me more and more anxious. Actually, my job isn’t very difficult; it’s just that I’ve been troubled for a long time now about when work will start again. How can I ease this anxiety?

I understand how you feel. During this special period, anxiety is quite common. Maybe deep down you feel very helpless, because the balance between what you can control and the uncertainty has been disrupted. You don’t know when you’ll be able to start work again. Sometimes it takes a little time to adjust to uncertain situations. But you don’t need to worry too much. What you’re going through now is somewhat similar to what students experience during summer vacation. When things are unknown, it’s normal for your emotions to have trouble adjusting. For now, please try to stay calm, Chaosi Yi, and I hope the new work environment brings you more growth and challenges.
Thank you. I feel much calmer now. Sometimes I wonder if I’m being a little weak, or if my worries are different from other people’s. After all, I can’t cope with sudden changes right now.

I understand how you feel. It may not be easy to cope at a time like this. However, sometimes our worries come from panic and uncertainty, and those can be overcome. Please don’t blame yourself, and don’t overthink it. You’ve already been very brave in facing your thoughts, and that in itself is really good.
I’m still not sure what I’ll be like now. I still have a lot of things to think about when it comes to going back to work, and it’s hard for me to make a decision.

Please try to stay calm. This is completely understandable, and it’s very normal to worry about the unknown. However, our worries are often based on unnecessary guesses. You can make a plan, think about some basic guidelines and ways to act, and figure out what you can do. That way, in your own life, you’ll be able to make reasonable decisions.
But I still haven’t received a notice. I don’t know when this notice will come.

That feeling of not being able to predict things is very painful. Please trust that your leaders and your company have plans and measures for reorganizing work. What you need is to appropriately plan for and handle possible situations, rather than over-imagining things that won’t help you.
You’re right. I need to start making some plans, and that’s really important for me. But I still don’t know. Maybe I’m still very scared.

If you feel uneasy and pessimistic, please don’t hesitate to seek more support, including talking with people around you or with a professional doctor or counselor. This can help you find ways to help yourself. If facing the pressure of going back to work all at once feels like too much, please don’t hesitate to contact me again. I’ll do everything I can to help you.
Thank you. I feel much better now. What you said was really good. I’ll keep paying attention to my own situation.
No problem. I’ll always be here with you. This challenge is temporary, and you can overcome it!
I feel like my thinking is abnormal. A lot of strange thoughts keep coming up, and I really don’t know what to do.

Hello. I believe many people have experienced this, and it can even be a common part of everyday life. This isn’t some rare illness. The fact that you’re actively seeking to solve the problem means you’re already on the right path.
But these thoughts make me feel uneasy and out of control. It’s really hard for me to control them.

Our thoughts are alive, not dry or fixed. As we keep thinking, they keep changing. If we pay too much attention to these thoughts, it may make them feel bigger and more powerful. We need to let ourselves follow what’s inside and accept whatever ideas and thoughts we have. No matter how strange they are, don’t be afraid of them.
But my thinking has become chaotic. I don’t know what I’m thinking, and I don’t know how to deal with it.

If you don’t feel that your recent situation is too severe, and it’s more of an emotional issue, then having a mental health professional make an assessment and provide treatment may be enough. Just like any other doctor, they may ask you questions to understand your situation, then tell you the possible reasons and give you suggestions.
I don’t want to see a mental health professional, and I’m not planning to take medication.

We’re not saying you have to take medication or receive any treatment. The first step should be to face yourself and understand your own situation. You can write down your thoughts and find someone who can listen to you, instead of hiding them or pushing them down. Maybe after you say them out loud, you’ll find that what you’re worried about isn’t actually that complicated or frightening.
But I don’t know who to talk to. I’m afraid other people won’t understand, or will misunderstand my thoughts.

First, it’s important to know that your thoughts definitely don’t make you different or alone. I believe many people have had experiences similar to yours. Find someone you trust and talk about your thoughts with them. Let them help you find a direction, and try not to worry that they’ll have a negative effect on you.
But I don’t want other people to influence my thoughts.
Don’t worry about other people’s thoughts. Just focus on your own real thoughts. I believe you can find a listener who truly cares about your thoughts and won’t judge or label your feelings.
It’s hard for me to calm down, especially at night.

When you feel strong negative emotions, you can try to increase your level of activity. Do things that help you calm down, such as reading, listening to music, or going for a walk. This can not only distract you, but also help you better process your feelings.
I’ll try hard to make myself better. Thank you for your support and encouragement.

I’m very willing to offer you support and suggestions. We need to actively look for a glimmer of light, and I believe you can overcome these difficulties. Whenever you need to, you can come to me to talk or seek help.

After I went home for the New Year, I had quit my job before the holiday, and because of the pandemic I was unemployed for two months. My mom started arranging matchmaking dates for me. She wanted me to marry someone who lived closer to home. I met five or six people, and either I wasn’t interested in them, or they weren’t interested in me. My personality isn’t the kind that warms up to people quickly, and I already don’t really like chatting with people online. My mom kept pushing me. If someone messaged me, I had to reply right away. If they didn’t message me, my mom would still urge me to chat with them. We had several arguments about this, and I cried several times. Later, things didn’t get better. During that time, I slowly gave in. My mom went from urging me to chat with people at first to secretly checking my phone after I fell asleep. I wouldn’t let her, and we argued several times, but it didn’t help, so I could only give in. In the end, when I was chatting or video calling with someone, my mom would even be nearby secretly listening. During that period, I was so mentally tense that when my phone was charging next to me in the middle of the night, as long as someone beside me moved at all, I would wake up with a start.

Hello, I’m very sorry to hear about the difficult situation you’re in right now. From what you’ve shared, I feel that there are some huge gaps in communication within your family. This kind of gap can make you feel disappointed and uneasy, and it can also affect your emotions and mental state. What I want to say is that your conflict and distress are definitely not accidental, but a very common issue.

First, I understand that you are in a lot of pain because your mother is forcing you to go on matchmaking dates, and this has put a lot of pressure on you. I think this is entirely your mother’s will, because she may want to live close to you, or to see you have a good life in the future. At the same time, I can understand why being forced at home to chat with others would make you not want to chat. You are someone who is introverted and doesn’t like interacting with strangers, and at the same time your mother is putting a lot of pressure on you. This puts you in a very conflicted state of mind and makes you feel very uncomfortable.

I suggest that you try communicating with your mother and try to help her understand how you feel. At the same time, to ease your own stress and uneasiness, you could talk with friends or a psychologist, or find things that make you feel better, such as watching movies, listening to music, and so on. If you already feel very distressed, you could also consider seeking counseling. I hope what I’ve said can be of some help to you. If you still have concerns, you can contact me anytime.
Recently, at the branch, I chose becoming a psychology teacher as my career direction. Am I satisfied with my life now?
Client, this is a very good choice. I know this is work you love. Do you feel satisfied with your life right now?
Actually, I’m not very sure. I’m worried this career might hit a bottleneck.

Yes, this is definitely something to think about. But don’t worry too much. Career development is a long-term process, and you should focus on improving your skills and experience. That way, you’ll be able to avoid hitting a bottleneck.
But I always feel like I lack confidence, and I don’t know whether I’m suited for this career.
That’s a very common feeling. Many people have these kinds of doubts. You should believe in your abilities. If you love this career, you can overcome any difficulty. Hang in there!
Thank you for your support, but I still feel very anxious.

Anxiety is a very normal emotion, especially in modern society. You can try to help yourself relax, like practicing meditation or doing some exercise to ease your anxiety. At the same time, you can also talk with friends or family and share your feelings.
I’ll try to do some relaxing things. Thank you for your suggestions.
You’re welcome. We all need to support each other. If you need to, you can always come talk with me.
Thank you. I really appreciate it.
You’re welcome. I’ll always be by your side and help you get through the hard times.

Hello! My husband is always giving me the silent treatment, and it’s making me really upset. I don’t know what to do. What should I do? He often says he doesn’t love me anymore, but I want to keep our family whole. What should I do?

I really understand how you feel, and I feel for you in your confusion. It’s very normal that you want to keep your family whole, but when you feel lonely or helpless in this kind of relationship, it’s important to learn to think about yourself too.
But I don’t know why he’s like this. He wasn’t like this before. I’m really confused.

It sounds like you really want to understand why he has changed, and that’s understandable. Maybe the two of you need to sit down and have a good talk, but before that, you need to consider your own health and safety. Don’t let yourself get trapped in an unhealthy relationship.
But I don’t know how to say it. I’m afraid he won’t accept what I think.

That worry is understandable, but you can believe that it’s very possible to find the right way to communicate. Try to find the right time, place, and way to create an environment that feels safe and mutually respectful. Tell him how you feel, and let him know what support you need.
Okay, I understand. But my emotions are still really hard to control. I want to talk about my feelings, but I’m afraid other people will blame me.

Emotional ups and downs are normal, and wanting to talk things out is also very normal. You can find some safe people, such as friends, family members, or a professional psychologist, and talk with them. They can give you support and offer suggestions. I also hope you can pay more attention to your inner world and try some ways to soothe yourself, such as breathing exercises, yoga, journaling, and so on.
Thank you for your suggestions. I’ll try. But I’m still very worried that if this family isn’t whole, it will hurt my children a lot.

Your worry is understandable too, but what you need to know is that in order to create a whole family, you have to ensure your own safety, health, and happiness. Maybe you need to look at the issue from different angles. For example, you can encourage your children to develop independent personalities, cultivate their interests and hobbies, and have lives of their own. That way, even if your family structure changes a little, they can still receive enough growth and support.
That’s true. I think I need more time and energy to deal with my own issues. Thank you for your suggestions and for being here with me.

No problem. Remember to pay attention to your own feelings and needs, and learn to give yourself some kindness and support. If you need help, you can come to me anytime to talk things through. Wishing you good luck, health, and happiness!

I used to not really feel anything about the company shuttle. I didn’t notice it at first, and later the company even specially removed one shuttle, merging the people from that bus with ours, but there still weren’t any people. I hadn’t noticed before. Hello! I saw what you shared, and I feel really sorry for the difficult situation you’re going through. First, I want to reassure you that you’re not alone, and you can choose to seek support and help.

I understand how you feel. Even strong people have vulnerable moments. Your courage and bravery have already earned my respect.

Your experience with transportation may very likely be related to your worries and doubts. I’d like to ask whether you’ve considered taking steps that give you more control over your situation. For example, taking the public bus, changing your own schedule, or commuting with other coworkers, so that your sense of safety can increase.
Okay, thank you for your suggestions. But I feel like my thinking is still a bit not normal.

That’s very normal. I understand the situation you’ve described, and your emotions also need support from others. You can try communicating with your family and close friends, and you can also look for a professional counselor. They can offer some relevant suggestions and support you in getting through this difficulty.
Thank you. I think that sounds like a good option.
Please don’t give up for now. You can still take action and make positive changes. If you need any help or have any questions, please feel free to contact me anytime.
