Thank you. Thank you for listening so patiently. It makes me feel very cared for.

We are all human, and we also need to care about others. In this process, we can pay more attention to and support each other, and some simple, helpful methods can address the challenges you may be facing.
Lately I always feel like I can’t keep up. I don’t want to study, and I don’t know what to do.
Hi there, sending you a hug (ღ˘⌣˘ღ)
I’m in college now, and it feels different from high school. Classes aren’t as packed either, and maybe because of that, I’ve become kind of lazy.

Mm-hmm, college is definitely different from high school. You have more time and more freedom, but it also requires us to be more self-disciplined. Wanting to be lazy is very normal too, but we need to find a balance.
But it’s really hard for me to find motivation. Studying feels completely meaningless.

Experiencing your feelings is very important, and it often brings us positive emotions. But beyond that, I think it’s also very necessary to set some goals for yourself. For example, wanting to pass CET-6 for now, or take the postgraduate entrance exam, and so on. This kind of motivation can give you a clearer sense of direction and make you more willing to study on your own.
Actually, I’m really anxious. Among so many people, it feels like I’m the one who just isn’t trying hard enough.

Dear, don’t blame yourself too much. Everyone starts from a different place. We need to learn to compare ourselves with others a bit less, adjust our mindset, find our own strengths as we work hard, and then compete with others. Maybe you’ll run into failure along the way in your studies, but through this process, you’ll become more competitive, right?
Mm, it seems that way. I can try, and work on becoming more competitive.
That’s right. Sometimes, love isn’t about encouraging others that they will definitely succeed, but about staying with them and helping them keep going when they’re facing difficulties.
Mm-hmm, thank you. You’ve given me the courage to keep working hard.
You’re welcome. You can come chat with me anytime. I’ll have a cup of tea with you and talk, okay?
I feel like there’s no hope living with my current husband. I want a divorce, but my husband won’t agree to it.

Yes, indeed. What does a life with hope look like, and what does a life without hope look like? I think the most fundamental difference is being happy or unhappy. If you keep making yourself endure a difficult way of life, it will only make you even unhappier. I really understand that you’ve sacrificed a lot for your child, but sometimes that isn’t the right choice. If your child knew how hard your life has been, they would be very unwilling to see that. Now that your child has grown up, why are you still looking for reasons to divorce? What kind of future do you want in your heart? What truly meaningful things have you done for yourself and your child to bring that hope closer?
I want a happy, complete family, a life like a scene in a painting.

That’s a very good wish. But making it happen takes a price and effort. We can’t control every single thing in a family, but we can control our own reactions and behavior. You can try to communicate well with your husband and work together to solve the problems. You can also seek help from professionals with psychological experience; they will be able to help you.
I don’t know how to communicate. He has never been willing to open up and talk.

Try some different approaches. Start with small things, and learn more about each other’s thoughts and needs. If you still can’t handle the problems properly, you can try going with him to consult some mental health professionals. Also, you can look up some articles and books about communication skills and maintaining relationships between men and women. They may give you some inspiring ideas.
I’m very worried that divorce will hurt my child.

I understand that. You care a lot about your child, and that is very important. I can help you come up with some plans to ease your situation, such as spending more time with your child and talking with your child more. You can also talk with some professionals; they have more information and methods for you to consider.
I will keep your advice in mind. I want to try to improve the current situation.

That’s good. Remember, everything takes time. Try to keep a positive mindset. A community or group where you can feel love and support can also give you tremendous support. You are not alone, and you don’t need to solve all the problems by yourself. If you have any questions or difficulties, you’re also welcome to contact me anytime.

My family has been unhealthy since I was little. My parents often argued. Now almost every day is spent with them arguing. I’m a light sleeper, and any sound can startle me awake. I often have headaches, and when I talk with my dad, I can also blow up.

I understand how you’re feeling right now. First, we need to work with you to find the root of the problem, so we can try to make some adjustments. You can think about it—what do you think is causing the arguments between your parents?
I think their communication with each other isn’t very good, so conflicts happen.

Mm, communication is very important. We can take it step by step and try to avoid conflict when you communicate with your parents. You could first try bringing up the idea that you hope they can communicate better.
I’ll try to communicate with them, but I really have a hard time falling asleep, and it’s very upsetting.

I understand how upsetting that is for you. Sleep quality is very important for both physical and mental health. You can try some relaxation techniques, like deep breathing or meditation. You could also consider consulting a doctor or using medication as an additional support.
Okay, I’ll try to relax myself so I can sleep better. But I’m really worried that in the future I’ll become like my parents.

Try not to worry too much. Everyone can avoid repeating the same patterns through self-adjustment. We can help you build healthier, more positive ways of thinking, so you can better cope with life in the future.
Okay, I understand. Then how can we find a more positive and healthier way of living?

We can work together to create some positive, practical action plans to help improve your mental state. For example, joining more interest classes, social activities, and so on. This can help ease your anxiety and stress.
Mm, that sounds really good. I’ll try to get myself actively involved in different activities in life. Thank you for your suggestions.
You’re welcome. We’ll continue to be here with you, moving forward together on this new path.

I'm afraid of interacting with people. I always feel like I'm living in my own world, and I don't know what I'm really thinking deep down. Every time I communicate with people, it feels like such a hassle. I have to pretend and hide my true thoughts, and that makes me feel really tired. Also, I often overthink things and care too much about what other people think. I feel like no one can understand me. I want to find a quiet place and live alone, but I know that's not realistic. And I don't know why, but I always feel embarrassed about calling people or doing video calls and things like that. It really bothers me.

I understand how you feel and how helpless this can seem. You're not facing these problems alone. What you're describing are signs of social anxiety, which is very common and can be treated. First, it's important to understand that everyone is an independent person with their own feelings and thoughts. You don't need to suppress who you are in order to please others. Second, confidence and a sense of grounding are built through improving your abilities at work and strengthening your mental resilience. If you can find something you're good at and keep making progress, I believe your confidence will grow a lot. Hang in there!
Thank you for comforting and encouraging me, but I'm still worried that I won't be able to change these problems, and that they'll keep bothering me.

That thought is understandable, but you need to let yourself believe that you are able to take control of your own life. Change takes a steady mindset and ongoing effort. Believe in yourself, keep trying with determination, and you'll find that you have a lot of potential.
This makes me think of times before when I tried to change myself, but in the end I failed. Even though I know failure is also a kind of experience, I still feel really discouraged.

Every attempt is a chance to learn, and even if it doesn't work out, don't give up too easily. We all need to spend time and energy breaking free from anxiety and fear. And you're not fighting this alone. It's important to know that there are many professional organizations now that can offer you help. Don't be afraid to seek help. Your difficulties can be overcome.
I understand what you mean, but I don't like telling other people about my problems. I always feel like people will see me as weak.

This is also a common concern. We need to understand that asking for help doesn't mean we're weak. On the contrary, seeking help is a very brave and wise thing to do. Professionals can provide you with professional solutions and support, and help you work through your confusion. The people who are brave enough to seek help are the ones who are truly strong.
I understand. I'll try to seek help. But I don't know where I should start next.

That's very good. You've already taken a step forward. For the next step, you can start with a few things: talk with family or friends about your situation, join community groups, take part in public activities, or find a mental health professional, and so on. Keep trying new things, keep getting to know yourself, and give yourself encouragement and motivation every day.
I'll try to do that. Thank you for your advice and encouragement. I feel like I have a little more confidence now.

I'm very glad to hear that. I will continue to support you. Don't forget, you're not fighting this alone. Anxiety and fear can spread among people, but hope and strength can keep emerging too. I hope you can face life actively, believe in yourself, and keep moving forward.

Since I started my senior year of high school, I’ve always wanted to keep a good mindset. But I still suddenly have emotional breakdowns, and sometimes I get really irritated for no reason. My grades are around upper-middle, but I keep feeling like I’m not good enough, like I’m just okay. It’s not that I’m especially smart or hardworking; it’s just that the questions are pretty normal. I get jealous really easily and I’m also very competitive, and I spend all day putting myself down.

Hello! Your happiness level has gone down, and your emotions aren’t in a very healthy place. From what you described, your emotional health seems a bit unstable. There are a few indicators of emotional health: first, whether you can be a friend to yourself—when facing difficulties and problems, instead of putting yourself down, you support and take care of yourself the way you would a friend; second, whether your mindset is open—when facing change, whether you can have an objective, rational, and open attitude; your willingness to communicate with others, whether you’re willing to release your true inner feelings and handle negative emotions rationally; and another indicator is the level of trust, whether you believe the liking and approval that comes from new friends. You can try some self-analysis and pay attention to your inner state from a more comprehensive perspective.

Sometimes when I talk with others, I feel like I have no confidence. I’m afraid of making mistakes, so I don’t dare share my opinions. And when I see everyone else chatting, I feel really inferior and feel like I don’t fit in.

That’s very normal. You just care a lot about what other people think. You can try encouraging yourself and praising your performance each day, instead of staying immersed in bad emotions. Sometimes you may not know what to say, or what kind of personality you should show. That’s normal. Accepting yourself isn’t easy, but it’s part of growing. You can look for your own unique interests and develop your hobbies. “Nalan Xingde once said, ‘Outside oneself, one seeks flowers and thoughts; within the heart, grass first knots and then separates.’” Interests and hobbies can help you understand yourself better and find what makes you unique. Having interest in particular subjects can also help you relax and show a better state.
My teachers are pretty nice, but I’m always worried they don’t like me.

You can try communicating with your teachers to understand their feelings and expectations. Some behaviors meant to make teachers like you more may actually backfire and intensify conflicts. Maybe when your teachers see your persistence, they’ll appreciate you more. This kind of mindset is more likely to win their goodwill. Coordinating relationships is mutual. If you usually communicate with your teachers very respectfully, that state can also help you feel more comfortable at important moments.
Whenever I run into a problem, I cry. I’m really afraid I’ll hurt my family.

This is a very good opportunity to show vulnerability. Showing others your vulnerable and sensitive side can help you feel closer to the people around you, and they may very likely give you more care and support. At the same time, it’s necessary to seek professional help, such as from a psychologist or counselor. They can analyze your situation more comprehensively and professionally, and provide appropriate suggestions and treatment based on your needs.
I really hope I can become better, but I always feel like it’s impossible.

In the process of growing, it’s very normal to keep reasonable expectations of others. You can feel proud from the bottom of your heart because of your own efforts, and you can also look for the roots of your negative thoughts. Some negative thoughts exist because our minds are full of stress, and over a long period of time, due to some unavoidable reasons, we have experienced disappointment and setbacks. But what you can do is stay positive and store up strength, so that you can better deal with these challenges. After clarifying your goals, we can use some targeted methods to help us reach them.
Sometimes, to avoid other people saying I’m too ambitious, I don’t dare express my thoughts.

Sometimes our tone when speaking can make others unhappy, because we may use some toxic words without realizing it. When expressing our views, we can carefully consider the words we use to make sure they don’t make the listener feel uncomfortable. At the same time, in life, whether it’s our tone on a call or when expressing our own views, we need to pay attention to politeness in our wording. That way, we can create more resonance in our communication with others.
It’s been more than ten years. My mother only knows how to nag and go on and on.

It sounds like you’ve experienced a long time of feeling suppressed and helpless. I understand that your emotions feel very unstable right now, and it’s very normal to want someone to talk to. Can you tell me how you got through that time back then?

Since I was little, they drilled this idea into me: my dad was incapable and couldn’t make money, and even if I was hit or yelled at by others, I wasn’t allowed to fight, because our family had no money. The complaining, blaming, resenting everything and everyone—that face of theirs is still vivid in my mind.

You were affected by that kind of upbringing for a long time, and emotionally you were hurt a great deal. I suggest that you gradually come to understand your own worth, and not let these painful experiences keep holding you back.

They only knew how to make demands of others. Since I was little, I felt inferior and not as good as other people. I would lower my head and not want to talk. My parents also wouldn’t care or try to understand me. They only demanded that I be a certain way and never asked why.

In that kind of family environment, you endured so much unfairness and hurt. Talking with friends or a mental health professional, focusing on your inner world, and improving your self-awareness can help you get along better with others.

Now I feel inferior and insecure. I’m emotionally fragile, afraid to communicate with people. When I do communicate with people, I hide myself, avoid eye contact, put on a front, am overly sensitive, and feel anxious inside.

Expressing your feelings is very hard. The fact that you’re bravely facing these difficulties shows that you’ve become stronger inside. Give yourself time. First, you need to make peace with yourself, and that can help lower your anxiety level. Staying in contact with people you’re close to is necessary; even if it’s through a screen, it can be very helpful for regulating your emotions.
For example, when I talk with people, I think about a lot of things—whether they’ll get angry, or afterward I doubt whether I said something wrong.

This shows that you’re introverted, have relatively high expectations of yourself, and care a lot about how others see you. But what I want to say is that you don’t need to worry too much. If the other person feels uncomfortable, it means there may be differences in mutual understanding. It’s precisely this attitude of taking the other person’s feelings into consideration that makes you seem more kind and warm.
Actually, I quite like drinking heavily by myself. I know drinking too much isn’t good, but in front of anyone I’ll act like I have no interest in alcohol. If I feel looked down on, I become hostile.

Excessive drinking is still very unhelpful for rebuilding your life. I suggest you control how much you drink, and keep a few things you like around you, such as toys, CDs, or little bits of knowledge, to shift your interest away from drinking. Breaking the inertia of addiction takes a lot of physical and mental energy, but with persistence, it can reach deep into the heart, allowing you to truly and steadily break free and have a new beginning.

I get jealous of and envy rich people, and I imagine what I’d be like if I had money. It’s like once I have money, my inferiority would surrender. I imitate the behavior of certain people I think are better than me. When I look at myself in the mirror, I feel I’m pretty annoying and pretty ugly, that no one loves me, I don’t know how to talk, I’m not likable, I’m not popular. At first I suspected depression, then persistent depressive disorder, then bipolar disorder.

Everyone has areas where things are unequal. Don’t force yourself to be measured by one narrow standard. I believe you can achieve what you hope for through your own efforts. Don’t blindly imitate others; unless you truly identify with it, imitation will only make you feel more lost. Confidence is the greatest capital you can seem to have. Believe in yourself, believe that you are attractive, keep trying new things, make more friends, and improve your emotional intelligence. This is the quickest path for you to gain happiness.

Lately I’ve been dealing with some relationship issues. I’m already 30, and I come from a single-parent family. I met my girlfriend through a matchmaking date. We talked for half a year, and after we met in person around National Day last year, her mom suddenly didn’t like me. Since then, her attitude has been unstable. I brought up getting married this year, but she keeps putting it off and won’t agree. My father is very angry and thinks her whole family has poor character. What should I do?

I understand your doubts and uneasiness, and I’m sending you a warm hug. Her behavior seems to show anxiety and an inner conflict or resistance; it may have to do with attachment patterns or more worldly considerations. You need to become clear again about what she really wants. Once you’re clear about her position, you’ll need to fully assess whether the relationship between you two is stable enough. Her attitude is very ambiguous, and before you make a lifelong commitment, you need to think carefully and see clearly what she is really like.

Yes, her uncertain attitude makes me really irritated. I don’t know what she actually wants, and I’m also worried we may have problems in other areas of communication. This relationship is troubling me. What should I do?

You need more understanding and communication, and through listening and reflecting, figure out whether your feelings for each other are strong enough. A successful marriage is not just about finding the right person. In most cases, it also means first becoming someone who is ready for marriage when you meet the right person. If you’re not very sure about her, you can consider reassessing your decision. Deciding to get married is one of the major decisions in life, and you need to make a wise and necessary decision.
I’m also a bit worried that other problems may come up after marriage, like our careers and where we’ll live. Do you have any advice?

You two need to talk these issues through properly. Does one of your careers determine where you will live? Do you prefer the countryside or the city? Do you need to live close to your family? Marriage means the two of you can rely on each other, not only for material things, but also for the foundation of life. If misunderstandings arise between you, how will you take care of yourself?
Her attitude and words also make me feel uncomfortable. How should I deal with her and her family?

You need to clarify her attitude and position. If it remains unclear, it would be best to set some boundaries for the time being. You can also see whether there might be someone more suitable for you. At the same time, pay attention to protecting your own emotional health. If needed, you can talk with a mental health professional. Hang in there—you can get through this difficult situation and find the happiness you want!
Lately I always feel really down, and I don’t have much motivation to do anything. It feels like I’m wasting time all day long.

Hi, hearing how you’re feeling, I can understand what you’re going through. Sometimes we run into situations like this, where it feels like nothing has any meaning, but we shouldn’t just give up on ourselves. You can try setting some goals and work toward them slowly, step by step. That can gradually help build your confidence and motivation.
But I feel like my family doesn’t understand me. They often say I’m useless, and it makes me feel like such a failure.

I understand how you feel. But you need to understand that everyone’s process of growing is different. Maybe your family hasn’t been through what you’ve been through, and they don’t understand your inner world. So we shouldn’t easily accept their criticism and blame; instead, we need to learn to affirm ourselves and keep going. You can find your own interests and hobbies, try some new things, discover your strengths and potential, and build your self-confidence.
But sometimes I feel so lonely. There’s no one I can talk to, and I don’t know how to face my problems.

That’s a very normal feeling. But we do need to learn to express our emotions and needs. Don’t be afraid of being rejected, and don’t shut yourself off. You can talk to some friends or family members you trust, and you can also consider seeking professional help, such as counseling. What matters is not letting yourself stay alone, and continuing to look for and embrace warmth.
I’m always worried about my future. I don’t know which direction I should go in.

That’s a very normal fear about development. We all face challenges and uncertainty, but this can also be an opportunity and a chance to grow. You can try to understand your interests and potential, set your own goals and plans, and also take part in more social activities or volunteer work. Slowly, you may discover your strengths and career direction. Don’t rush for quick results. What matters is keeping confidence and patience with yourself.
But I’m afraid I won’t do things well, and if I make a mistake, I’ll be a real failure.

This is a kind of worry and pressure, but we can’t let ourselves be troubled by these negative emotions. Try to change the way you think and face problems with a positive mindset. You can try to learn from failure, adjust your actions and strategies, and keep improving your abilities and growing. Remember to give yourself some encouragement and affirmation, and don’t be too demanding of yourself or blame yourself too much.
Thank you for your support and advice. I’ll work hard at it.

I’m very glad to hear from you and to offer you some help and companionship. You’re not alone. On the road ahead, you’ll definitely encounter more challenges and growth. But please believe that you can become better, and you will have a better future. Hang in there!

Female, 37 years old, mother of two children. My older child is 8, and my younger one is 3. I haven’t been doing very well lately, and I have some signs of depression. My younger child recently started kindergarten and hasn’t been adjusting very well. The teacher said my child isn’t able to interact with the teachers or classmates, and suddenly I felt like a mountain was pressing down on me. Today when we went out, my younger child didn’t want to go and cried and made a huge fuss, almost hysterical. Whenever this happens, I get really upset. Today, a neighbor happened to say to my child, “Can’t you keep it down?” in a very impatient way, and then I felt panicked. Very scared.

Hello, thank you for coming in. I can sense that you’re in a state of fear and insecurity right now. I really understand the anxiety and guilt you feel around projecting your emotions onto your child and having negative feelings. As you said, this has to do with a sense of safety. You don’t need to worry; we can work together to find a way through this.
I’m really afraid that I’ll hurt my child because of my own emotions. That’s what worries me the most.

I understand how you feel. A child is one of the most important things to every mother. But you need to clearly recognize that the emotional distress you’re experiencing, and the negative feelings you have toward your child, are not your fault. Let’s explore some possible ways to address this.
Okay, I’ll listen.

First, you can begin with self-awareness, which means “seeing” your own behaviors, feelings, and emotions, and understanding the needs behind them. Seeing is the beginning of change. By understanding the personality traits behind these behaviors and emotions, we can make use of them rather than control or suppress them, and in that way live peacefully with them.
I understand.

Second, try to accept your own imperfections and keep affirming and recognizing yourself. This can increase your sense of self-worth. Don’t be too hard on yourself, because your self-worth depends on how you evaluate yourself, and has nothing to do with anyone else.
Mm, that seems a little difficult.

Yes, but it’s also very important. Finally, I suggest that you study psychology so you can better understand yourself and your child. Throughout our lives, we are dealing with people, and in each relationship we complete the hidden life lessons within it. Being a parent especially requires learning and growth, particularly so you can become your child’s “significant other” and provide the psychological nourishment they need to grow up healthy and happy.
Okay, I’ll try hard to do that.

Good. Please don’t forget that you are not alone. I will accompany you through this difficult time. If you need to talk or vent, I will listen. At the same time, you can also seek support from friends and family.
Thank you. I really feel so lucky to have you by my side.
I’m also happy to be able to help you. I believe we will get through this difficult time together, and gain growth and progress from it.

Lately my family has had a lot of debt, and I send money home every month. But my parents and younger brother don’t seem to understand the pressure I’m under at work. They’re always complaining about me spending money, and it makes me feel really bad. I don’t even want to answer calls from home anymore.

Reading what you’ve said, I get the sense that you’re like a brave warrior, because you’ve already taken on responsibility for this family. But that responsibility is very heavy, and it can leave you feeling disappointed and exhausted. Of course, it’s not always easy to seek understanding from your family, but that doesn’t mean you should have to put up with their lack of understanding. You can express how you feel without worrying that they won’t love you anymore. Your feelings and needs are just as important as theirs.
I’ve never thought that I had that choice. I think I need to tell them about this, but I feel like I can’t explain it clearly.

That’s right. Expressing feelings isn’t easy for anyone. Try giving yourself some time to think about what you want to say and how you want to say it. You can write it down, or first share it with one or two close friends. This can help you find a better way to express what’s inside.
I know you’re right, but I feel like I can’t express my thoughts clearly. I’m sure they’ll laugh at me.

As I said before, expressing feelings isn’t always easy, and it takes a lot of courage. You need to know that even if the way you express yourself may be different, that doesn’t make you bad. Your parents and younger brother are your family. They care about you, and they will do their best to understand how you feel.
I’m afraid I’ll hurt their feelings.

I can understand your worry, but you also need to understand that your feelings and needs are just as important as theirs. You’re not hurting them; you’re trying to connect with them emotionally. They will do their best to understand. Expressing feelings is one way to build a close relationship, and it can bring you closer.
I understand. Thank you for your support. I’ll try to express my feelings.
Good. I believe you can do it. If you need my help or advice when expressing your feelings, please don’t hesitate. You’re not fighting this alone.
Lately my mood has been really low, and there are some things I just keep going over in my mind.
Hello, I can listen to your story and see how I can help you.

A few years ago someone confessed his feelings to me. Although I rejected him, he still has some business contact with me. Recently he revealed that he has a child born outside of marriage, and he also mocked me for being older and unmarried. It made me feel really awful.

This is a tricky situation. First, you need to remember that you already firmly rejected his confession, and he is not someone you want to be with or spend time with. Also, his values are different from yours, and he may not meet your standards. Think about yourself and your future, and try to stay calm and at peace, without letting his actions affect you. When something feels hard to bear, keep a peaceful mindset and don’t give negative emotions room to take over. I can sense your pain, but things will get better.
But I just want to share my life with someone. Why do I have to meet someone like this?

This is a kind of challenge, one that helps you learn to understand yourself, settle into what you truly want, and choose someone who is right for you. When you meet that person, you’ll find that he understands you, trusts you, and respects you. When you want to share, you can talk with your friends or family, and help yourself stay in a happy and balanced state of mind.
I still feel very lonely. There’s no one to listen to me pour my heart out.

This feeling is very common. People often hope to be understood and supported by others. I understand your loneliness, and at the same time I want to remind you to keep your mindset balanced and face life positively. We all need to look for care and support, and this process takes patience and persistence. Everyone encounters difficulties and challenges, and we all have to face and overcome them. Sometimes, when you take the initiative to care about others, you may also receive care and support from them.
Thank you for your encouragement. I’ll keep trying.

You’re welcome. I believe you can overcome these difficulties. If you need to talk or want to explore this further, don’t hesitate—feel free to come chat with me anytime. Lastly, I hope that in the new year, you can be a happy and confident version of yourself, let go of the past, and face the future positively.

My boyfriend and I have been together for six months, and he loves me a lot. But I keep thinking about the sweet memories he had with his ex-girlfriend, and he has more dating experience than I do. I start thinking that he’s done the same things with other girls. What should I do?

Hello, I’m really glad to hear that you’re willing to seek help. From how you described this, I can feel that your relationship with your boyfriend is very deep. What you need now is to find a suitable way to work through the worries inside you, and not get too caught up in them. You’re right—everyone has a past. You can try looking at his memories with his ex-girlfriend from another angle: they were part of his own process of growing and being shaped. Also, the way your boyfriend guides you after arguments to slowly accept certain things is a sign of his maturity, and you should appreciate him for that. I’m not sure whether your boyfriend is a bit older than you; if he is, he may be a little more mature than you and may also offer you some guidance.
What you said makes a lot of sense. But I still can’t help thinking about him and other girls, and it really bothers me.

I can understand how you feel. If you want to get free from this distress, you’ll need to gradually learn to let go of these things and stop caring about them so much. You could consider using some ways to ease your emotions, such as exercising, listening to music, reading, and so on. At the same time, you also need to trust that your boyfriend loves you, and not worry too much that he’ll leave you.
Mm, I understand. But I still unconsciously ask him about his past, and that really bothers him. What should I do?

You can try to manage your emotions and tell yourself not to care too much about these things. You can also try finding other topics to talk about and explore shared interests with each other, which can bring more fun and happiness. In addition, you and your boyfriend can make some rules together, such as not talking about each other’s past and only focusing on the present and the future. This can help make your relationship healthier.
Okay, I understand. I’ll do my best to manage my emotions, and work with my boyfriend to plan a healthier future.

Very good. I believe you can definitely do it. At any time, remember to take good care of yourself and keep a positive, open, and healthy mindset. Love requires mutual understanding and acceptance. I hope your relationship gets better and better.
Thank you so much for your help and encouragement. I’ll work hard to create a better future for myself and my boyfriend!

You’re welcome. I’m very glad I could provide you with some help and support. Your determination and effort are very much worth encouraging. No matter when, we can help and support each other and get through difficult times together. Wishing you all the best!

Sometimes I feel really sad, and I don’t know if it’s because I’m too sensitive. Like tonight, my mom was stewing chicken and I didn’t know how to make it, so I just wanted to ask whether I should add scallions, ginger, and garlic, but then I was looked down on. Thinking about it, I really just made unnecessary trouble for myself.

Don’t be too sad. Everyone has their own weaknesses. Not knowing how to cook chicken doesn’t mean you can’t make other dishes, and it doesn’t mean you’re not good. Even if you’ve done something wrong, don’t blame yourself. Try to look at the positive side of the problem, reflect on yourself, study it well, and next time you’ll be able to do better.
Sometimes I really do get angry over little things, and I can’t hold back my emotions, and then I feel really irritable.

That’s very normal. Everyone goes through situations like this. You need to pay attention to your emotions and learn to adjust them. Don’t let negative emotions control you. You can try some calming methods, like deep breathing, listening to music, watching a movie, and so on.
I feel like my family doesn’t care about me enough. They’re always dismissive of what I say, and I don’t know whether they’re really listening to me.

Maybe it’s because they also have their own problems and worries. You can try communicating with them and finding the way that works best for your family. Sometimes it’s not a lack of care, but not enough communication. You can find a way of communicating that suits your family to resolve this issue.
I’m always very hard on myself. I always feel like I’m not good enough, and it makes me very tired and worn out.

Everyone has their own shortcomings; no one is perfect. You need to learn to accept your shortcomings and value your strengths. When you notice your shortcomings, you can actively think about solutions. You might try finding some easier ways to relax, like taking a hot bath, going for a walk, and so on.
Sometimes I feel like I’m the odd one out among my friends. I feel like I’m not quite the same as them, and I don’t know what to do.

Everyone is unique, and no one will be exactly the same as you. You should value and discover your own traits. Don’t compare yourself with others, and don’t force yourself to be the same as them. Do things you like, interact with people who share your interests, and you’ll find that what makes you different is one of a kind.
Sometimes I feel like I’m a failure when it comes to relationships. Whether at work or in life, it’s hard for me to build good relationships with other people.

Everyone’s personality and experiences are different, and the ways people get along with each other are different too. You can gradually understand your own personality and learn how to interact with different types of people. You can also try joining some social activities, talking with others, and building relationships based on mutual trust and respect.
Every time before a meeting or a presentation, I always feel very nervous. I worry that I’ll say something wrong, or that I won’t express my views well.

This is a very normal reaction. First, you can prepare well before the meeting, learn about the agenda and the participants in advance, and plan what you want to say. Second, while you’re speaking, you can pay attention to your voice and tone, maintain your image, and let yourself speak with more confidence and composure.
My work stress and mental burden are getting heavier and heavier. Sometimes I feel like I’m about to fall apart.

Everyone encounters difficulties and challenges in life. You don’t need to carry too heavy a burden; you can seek help from others. At the same time, you need to learn to reduce stress. You can adjust your work and rest appropriately and not let yourself get too tired. Pay attention to your physical and mental health, keep a positive mindset, and believe that you can handle any challenge.
Over the past month, there have been three times when I felt really down. When I feel under a lot of pressure, I become very negative and don’t want to do anything.

Dear, what you’re feeling is very normal, and you don’t need to worry too much. You can give yourself some time and space to accept these negative emotions. We can set some goals and try activities like relaxation exercises, meditation, or running. You can find the method that works best for you to ease what you’re going through.
But this happened a few years ago too, and I’m really worried it will get worse and worse.

I understand your worries, but you can seek advice from professionals and explore this issue with them. Give yourself more time to accept your emotions and feelings; that’s an important step in helping yourself recover. We all need support, and you don’t have to be afraid to express your feelings to others.
I feel very lonely. There’s no one I can talk to about how I’m feeling.

I can listen to you. I understand that this kind of loneliness is really hard. And there are many other people who can help you too; you can seek help from a professional therapist. Finding someone who can understand your emotions and feelings and reaching out for support and help is a very important step.
I feel like I would cause trouble for my family and friends.

Try not to overthink it. Your family and friends surely care about you, and they also hope you can get help. Tell them what’s on your mind, and let them be your supporters. Having people who are willing to care about you is very important.
When I look in the mirror, I don’t know what to say to myself.

You can try saying your thoughts and feelings out loud in front of the mirror, and notice your emotions and how you express them. This process can help you better accept and understand your feelings, and also help you understand yourself more. At the same time, you can also seek help from a psychotherapist to cope with your emotions more effectively.
I always feel empty inside, and I feel like I’m worthless.

Your feelings are normal; many people have feelings like this. However, you shouldn’t put yourself down, because your worth is very important. Try to find your interests and hobbies, and try doing things that express your own value. Also, you can share your feelings and thoughts with people you trust and know can support you. All of these steps can help you find your sense of worth again.
I’m really worried that my low mood will affect my life and work.

Your worry makes sense; people can easily be affected by their emotions. But you can try talking with the people around you, sharing your experience with them, and finding the support and methods that suit you. You can also consider seeking professional help, which can provide you with a more personalized treatment plan. These are all very important forms of help, and they can help you build greater resilience in coping with stress in your life and work.
Lately my family has had very high expectations of me, but I often feel like I can’t meet them.

Hello, it sounds like you’re facing some challenges. Expectations can be something that pushes us forward, but they can also bring pressure and make us feel like we can’t catch our breath. Remember, even though expectations are important, having a balanced, positive mindset is what can help us get through these negative feelings.
I know, but I feel really helpless, because sometimes I can’t do what they want.

Everyone has to face expectations that are hard to meet; that’s normal. You can say what you are able to do, and you can also communicate some expectations that are hard to reach to your family in a more down-to-earth way. Your road may be long, but I believe you can handle all of this.
Thank you for your encouragement, but I still feel a little helpless and discouraged.

When we feel stressed and anxious, it’s easy to get caught up in negative emotions. But could you try to think about it this way: even if you can’t meet their expectations right now, you are still working hard, growing, and learning. Everything you’re doing can help build a foundation for your future.
You’re right. I’ll do my best, and I’ll also communicate with my family.

That’s great. That’s a really good thing. Your family cares about you and hopes you can have a better life. Communication is very necessary, so you can build a healthier way of communicating in your family relationships. You’re doing well. Hang in there!
I’ll keep going. Thank you for your encouragement and support.

You’re very brave, able to face difficulties directly and seek support. You’re not facing these challenges alone. Believe in yourself and in what you’re doing—it’s right. If you need further support, I’ll always be here to listen to you and support you.
Thank you for your help and for listening. I feel much better now.

That’s wonderful. I’m very glad to hear that. Remember, you deserve to be valued, cared for, and supported. Whenever it is, remember to seek help and someone to listen. May you have a tomorrow filled with love and support.

When I first came to the U.S. as a freshman, I wasn’t used to the food, and the place is pretty remote. I get along well with my roommate, but our personalities are different. She’s more outgoing and likes forming little groups, very social, going out with a bunch of people to eat and hang out. But I don’t like that. I prefer occasionally eating, studying, and chatting with one or two friends. They often stay up all night and don’t sleep, and they don’t really study properly either. They smoke and drink. Honestly, deep down I don’t really want to be part of that crowd. My boyfriend is in the U.S., so after coming here I also haven’t socialized much. Actually, my social skills are okay, I just don’t like socializing. Recently I felt like I can’t keep shutting myself in like this forever, and even if it’s just to broaden my horizons, I should go out a bit. So I hung out with my roommate’s friends a few times, and then I found that even though some of them are pretty wild, they still do well academically. My roommate is like that too. Even though I looked down on her sometimes and felt she had no perseverance or depth, and only cared about makeup and socializing, just kind of superficial. But exams are coming up recently, and we’re all reviewing, and she’s actually doing better than me. Sometimes I even have to ask her for help. I’ve been here for quite a while, and I always thought I was pretty good at studying, but because of my toothache, bad mood, and having no friends, I’ve been studying all the time but haven’t really gotten into the right state or found a study method. Suddenly I feel like I was actually looking down on others, when clearly they’re doing well academically, they’re in a good mood, and they have friends. What right do I have to dislike them just because their lifestyle is different? I don’t know how to get past this block in my mind and get into the right state.

You’re very brave to face the challenges you’re dealing with. I understand that you want a small circle of friends, but it may be time to discover some new things and get to know different cultures and groups of people. You could try joining some student organizations, which may make it easier for you to meet new friends and build your own small circle.
But I don’t know whether spending time with my roommate and her friends will affect my study progress.

Sometimes we need to shift our focus away from studying and let ourselves do something different, which can bring more motivation and inspiration. So don’t be afraid to interact with them. Remember, studying should be treated as something enjoyable, not as a source of pressure.
But my friends and I seem to have different interests. They stay up all night, smoke, and drink. I can’t do that.

I understand your worries and the situation you’re in. But you can tell your friends about your lifestyle and your needs, and they’ll very likely respect you. You could try going with them to some new salons, concerts, and things like that. You may be pleasantly surprised to find that some things you weren’t interested in at first are actually very appealing.
My toothache also makes my mood really bad. It’s hard to concentrate.

Then you could see a doctor first and take care of the toothache. At the same time, it’s very normal for your attention to get scattered, even if it’s temporary. What’s important is that you try to reflect on why your state with studying or life has been poor. When things feel difficult, you might try talking to some friends around you about how you’re feeling, or try having a conversation with yourself.
It seems like I often look down on other people and feel like I’m better than them. Actually, that’s really not right.

Human beings all have some negative emotions, and that’s very normal. But often we magnify our own shortcomings and downplay other people’s strengths. Remember, everyone has their own different strengths and weaknesses, and those weaknesses often help us grow. Try to pay attention to the bright spots in others, and at the same time try to make up for your own shortcomings, continuing to grow and improve.
I don’t know what my future will be like. I feel really lost.

Many people have thoughts like this, so it’s very normal. You can try to look for your passions and interests, the activities and fields that can motivate you and inspire you. At the same time, please don’t forget that you can step out of your current situation at any time and make a new plan and set new goals.
Thank you for your advice. I’ll try to do that.
You’re welcome. And don’t forget, you’re not alone. We’re always here to support you.

The yoga studio I’ve always gone to, I see it as a place where I can relax—not just physically, but mentally too. There’s no one there who knows me, no work, and the teacher is very understanding. Practicing yoga lets me briefly forget my stress and worries. Today the teacher said that frontline medical workers who supported Hubei can come back and get a free annual membership, and asked if we knew anyone. The team leader was my former head nurse, so I forwarded her WeChat contact to the teacher. But I have this indescribable feeling inside, like my secret base is about to have lots and lots of people pouring in. Among them are two team members I’ve worked with before. I don’t like them. I know they’re all heroes this time, but I just don’t like them. I feel like it will disturb this peace I have. How can I have this kind of mindset? Not to mention that resources should be shared, and the yoga studio was closed for two or three months because of the pandemic and lost a lot of money; it needs more people to survive. I feel conflicted.

Hearing what you shared, I can sense your love for the yoga studio and how committed you are to it. At the same time, I can also understand that having unfamiliar people enter your yoga space may make you feel uncomfortable, and may affect your yoga practice and relaxation. This feeling is very normal; you don’t need to be surprised by it.
Mm, yes. I don’t even dare to imagine it.

All of us have some degree of social anxiety, more or less. It just shows up in different ways. Your anxiety is that you want to recommend something that benefits you to your colleagues, and doing that would be good for both them and the yoga studio. Under normal circumstances, this is a very ordinary social interaction, beneficial to yourself and to others. But you feel troubled. A possible reason is that there’s resistance inside you, coming from a sense of insecurity, so you’re unable to share with people you don’t really identify with. You may feel that your private space is being invaded, or even be afraid that your secrets will be seen by others. This requires understanding what has caused your insecurity, and how to overcome social anxiety.
Mm, I understand. Maybe my resistance to interpersonal interaction comes from my childhood experiences and some negative social experiences. Thank you for helping me make sense of this.

I understand. Maybe you can try starting with small things, slowly letting yourself come into contact with strangers, and trying to share your thoughts and feelings with different people. Once you gradually get used to it, you’ll be able to handle social relationships more freely and comfortably, and reduce unnecessary burdens.
Mm, okay. I’ll try to communicate more with others and reduce my social anxiety.
Besides these, do you have any other ways to reduce your stress and worries?
Besides yoga, I also quite like listening to music and reading.

Then in your free time, you can listen to music, read, or even try some other ways to relax, like taking a hot bath or going for a walk. Whatever you do, the important thing is that you can find a way that suits you, so your body and mind can relax effectively.
Okay, I’ll try. Thank you for your suggestions.
You’re welcome. We support each other, and I hope you can get through this difficult time soon and feel happier.
Thank you. I’ll work even harder.

Lately I haven’t really liked talking with people. I feel more comfortable when I’m by myself. But this feeling of loneliness also feels strange to me. I do want to try to get closer to others. Sometimes when everyone gets together, it’s really fun, but sometimes I feel like I’m not someone who smiles that much. I’ve been trying hard, but when I think about people talking behind my back, saying I only know how to study, saying I’m just a bookworm, I feel really scared and don’t dare to keep trying. Why is that?

Hello. First, I’d like to ask, why don’t you like talking with people? Is it because you’re shy? Or is there another reason? Second, when other people say those things about you, does it make you feel inferior?

Actually, I don’t think there’s any particular reason why I don’t want to talk with people. It just feels hard to fit into the kind of atmosphere other people have. When people say those things about me, it really does make me feel very sad.

Hearing what you’ve described, I get the sense that you may be a more introverted person. There’s nothing wrong with that. Everyone has their own traits and interests. As for what other people say about you, try not to take it too much to heart. What they say isn’t necessarily true, and it doesn’t mean they really know you. You need to have confidence in yourself and stay true to what you believe in, so you can go further.

Thank you for understanding and encouraging me. But I feel like there isn’t anything special about me, and I’m easily overlooked by others. Sometimes I really feel confused. How should I make myself more confident?

Everyone is unique. Maybe you haven’t discovered your own strengths yet, but that doesn’t mean you don’t have any. You can try more to explore your interests and talents, try things in different places, and get to know some new friends. At the same time, don’t give up on your own learning and growth. That’s the key to becoming more confident.
Mm, I’ll try. But sometimes I’m always afraid I won’t be able to do it. How can I change thoughts like that?

Fear of failure is something everyone encounters, but too much fear and negative thinking can make you miss more opportunities. To change this way of thinking, you can gradually try doing some challenging things. That way, you can learn about your own abilities and potential. When you’re able to overcome difficulties and reach your goals, you’ll feel more confident and steady.
Thank you for your advice. I’ll try to do that. But sometimes I still feel lonely, and I don’t know what to do.

Loneliness is something everyone encounters, but that doesn’t mean you’re a failure. You can try reaching out to new groups of people and experiencing different cultures and environments. This can both expand your social circle and strengthen your life experience and relationships. Also, you can try new hobbies and skills at home, which can also enrich your life.
Okay, I’ll try. Thank you for always supporting and encouraging me. I feel very warmed by it.
You’re welcome. I understand how you feel, and I hope my suggestions and support can help you. Remember, no matter what problems come up, we can overcome them together and move toward a better life.
Lately, I always feel like my free time doesn’t have much meaning, and I don’t know what to do.

I understand how you feel. First, you should know that the time we spend alone is very important. It allows us to be humble, think, reflect, and explore. Sometimes when we feel our free time is boring, it’s actually because we haven’t tried new things. You can try some hobbies you’ve thought about before but never actually done, or explore some new areas. Remember not to take on too much at the beginning. Just stick with it for one week, and doing one meaningful thing is enough.
But I always feel like what I do isn’t good enough, and I don’t feel a sense of accomplishment.

This is very common. Let’s remember that a sense of accomplishment comes from the results we achieve after putting in effort within our own abilities. So don’t focus too much on the outcome; focus instead on the process and what you’ve learned. Think about the problems you once challenged yourself with and successfully solved. That feeling can’t be measured by money or anything else.
But I don’t know what I want to do right now.

That’s okay. This is very normal, and many people have thoughts like this. You can look for some ideas and inspiration from the people around you or online. At the same time, keep expanding your knowledge and skills.
Okay, I’ll try.
Good. I believe you can succeed. Don’t forget to work toward small goals step by step. That way, you can gradually build a sense of accomplishment and keep moving forward.
But I always feel very helpless.

That feeling is also very common, but you need to understand that you’re not alone. There are many people in this world who are struggling just like you. At the same time, you can also seek support and help from family and friends around you, or from professional organizations. Don’t let yourself stay in a state of loneliness and helplessness all the time.
Thank you for your suggestions. I’ll put them into practice.
Good. If you need any help or have any questions, you can contact me anytime. I’ll always be here to support you. I wish you a happy life and a peaceful mood.
The stepfather is firmly opposed to his daughter marrying any man. I wanted to ask whether this stepfather might have psychological issues.
It sounds like this is something that’s making you feel uneasy and troubled. Would you like to talk about the specific details?
He keeps emphasizing that he is his daughter’s only family, and that once she gets married, he’ll lose her.
This leaves you feeling helpless and unable to understand it. From your perspective, this stepfather’s behavior is troubling.
Yes, I really feel worried and upset.
I can really understand how you feel. After all, family relationships are very important. Have you ever tried communicating with the stepfather, to understand his thoughts and feelings?
We have communicated, but every time he either interrupts me or ignores me.
That makes you feel disappointed and helpless. You’re looking for a solution, but he hasn’t taken part in a reasonable discussion, and that’s really difficult.
Yes, I feel like I’m stuck in a difficult situation.
That’s completely understandable. Would you consider seeking some professional help, such as talking with a psychologist or counselor?
That’s a good idea. I’ll think it over carefully.
Good. You’ve made a very wise choice. You should know that you’re not alone in this issue; many people are looking for similar solutions.
The pandemic has been really severe lately, and I feel very scared and anxious. What should I do?

I understand how you feel. Facing something as uncertain as the pandemic, we can all feel panicked and anxious. Still, there are things we can start with ourselves to reduce the risk of infection as much as possible. For example, wearing a mask when going out, washing our hands often, and so on. These methods are simple, but they really are very effective preventive measures.
That’s true. Taking these measures does help reduce the risk of infection. But I’m still very worried—what if I or my family get the virus?

That’s a very real worry, but we need to have faith in our country and in medical workers. They are taking all kinds of measures and actively responding to the pandemic, including strengthening health protections and medical treatment. At the same time, we also need to trust in our own ability. If we reduce risk as much as possible and avoid infection to the greatest extent, we can protect ourselves and our families.
Hearing what you said, I feel much more reassured. But I still worry about how things will develop in the future. Will this pandemic get worse and worse?

What we’re facing right now is indeed a fairly complex situation. But we need to believe in ourselves and in the strength of the country. With efforts from all sides, I believe the pandemic will be brought under control and eventually disappear. At the same time, during this process, we also need to pay attention to our own emotions and do things that help us relax and adjust our mindset as much as possible, such as listening to music, reading, exercising, and so on.

I understand. I need to believe in myself and in the strength of the country, while also reducing the risk of infection as much as possible, paying attention to my health, and finding some ways to ease my anxiety and stress.

That’s right. You’re already making adjustments in the right direction. Also, if you have any other confusion or difficulties, you can come talk with me anytime. Whether it’s through text chat or voice chat, I’d be very happy to talk with you.
Thank you so much for your support and help. I’ll follow your suggestions carefully and actively adjust my emotions.
You’re welcome. This is also what I should do as a supporter. Lastly, I wish you good health and a happy mood. Everything will get better.
Thank you. I wish you all the best too.
I’ve been feeling really anxious lately, but I don’t know how to ease it. Could you help me work through it a bit?
When you feel anxious, you can try taking some deep breaths, or find a quiet place to relax for a while.
It feels like deep breathing doesn’t help either. What should I do then?
You could try running, doing yoga, or listening to some relaxing music. These can all help ease your emotions a bit.
But I always feel like I’m useless, like I can’t do anything well.
Everyone has their own strengths and shortcomings. Try not to keep denying yourself. You can try to discover your strengths and help yourself feel more confident.
But I always feel like I can’t have better self-control, and I’m afraid negative emotions will come up.

Everyone has negative emotions; that’s very normal. You can try finding some activities that help relieve stress, like reading, watching movies, chatting with friends, or doing something you’re interested in.
Thank you for your suggestions. I’ll try to put them into practice.
You’re welcome. If there’s anything you need help with, feel free to come talk with me anytime.

I don’t know why, no matter how I review, my exam scores still aren’t high. I study the same key points as my classmates, and I feel like I remember them well and did well on the exam, but when the scores come out, they’re just really low. I don’t know why this is happening. I spent so long memorizing, but my score is even lower than people who cheated, or even people who didn’t review and didn’t cheat. I even feel like the teacher is doing it on purpose. But I didn’t do anything wrong.

Hearing how confused you are, I feel really sorry. I understand that you studied very hard, but the results don’t seem to be what you expected. In this situation, I can understand how you feel, and we can try looking at this from other angles.
I’m really lost. I always thought that as long as I worked hard, I could get good grades, but now I feel really discouraged.

Kiddo, you can’t keep blaming yourself too much; that will only make you feel even more discouraged. Looking at it another way, you’ve kept trying to study, and that isn’t easy. Studying is certainly important, but grades aren’t only about studying.
But I’m really worried about how my parents see me and what they expect from me. They’ve always expected me to have excellent grades.

I understand your fear and uneasiness, but your worth is not in your grades. It lies in the fact that you are a unique and valuable person. Don’t forget that you have many strengths and contributions, and you have also made a positive impact in different ways. Your parents hope you do your best. Although it may sometimes seem like pressure, they sincerely hope you succeed.
I feel really guilty and helpless. I don’t know what to do.

I hear the emotional distress you’re in. You don’t have to feel guilty. This is a normal emotional response. You can take active steps, such as looking for support and resources, or joining activities to break through the anxiety. I’ll be here to support you throughout this process.
I’ll try, but I feel like I’ve fallen really behind.

I really appreciate your courage and determination. Take time to notice your own needs, and go slowly. You’ll find that taking action is more powerful than you imagine. Let’s make a workable plan together and move toward your goals step by step.
I feel much better now. Thank you for your support and help.

Seeing you like this makes me especially happy. I warmly congratulate you on being able to find a way forward. Don’t forget, as you get through difficulties, your growth and future will become even better. If you need to keep talking and want support, I’m always here.

I was diagnosed with depression at the hospital in March, so now I don’t dare go to school. My teachers and parents have me study on my own at home. I’ve been studying really seriously, but lately when I see piles of books and problems I can’t solve, I feel so tired, and I even want to throw things. My mood is really bad, and I feel a bit lost. There are only 55 days left until the exam, and I’m really scared I won’t get in. I feel kind of like I’m falling apart. Supporter, what do you think I should do?

I understand what you’re going through right now. Sending you a hug. First, try not to get too nervous—things can be worked through. You can try tearing out pages from books and taking notes to help yourself study in a more focused and organized way. You can also start with the easiest problems first, and slowly improve your problem-solving ability. As for the exam, try not to worry too much for now. What matters is making a little progress each day. Believe in yourself—you can get through all these difficulties. I’ll keep supporting you. Let’s hang in there together!
Thank you so much for your support and advice. What you said makes me feel really warm and reassured. But I still feel a bit lost, and I don’t know how I should adjust my mindset.

Try not to get too caught up in your emotions. Overthinking will only add to your stress and anxiety. You can try letting yourself relax a bit—listen to some calming music, or take a walk outside to relax your body and mind. Also, believe in yourself. Believe that you can get through this difficult time. Slowly, you’ll find that your mindset starts to improve.
Thank you for your advice. I’ll try to put it into practice. But I still worry that I won’t get in. If I really don’t, what should I do?

You can’t keep immersing yourself in thoughts of failing the exam. That will only make your mood feel even heavier. You can first set a goal, and then work toward it. No matter what the result is, you should feel proud of the effort you put in. And even if the exam doesn’t go smoothly, you can choose other paths to pursue your dreams. Don’t let one failure drag you down. You will definitely have better opportunities. Hang in there!
Thank you for your encouragement and support. I really feel your care and help. But I still feel very scared and helpless, and I don’t know how to face all the different possibilities in the future.

Everyone’s life has different twists, turns, and difficulties, but these are also opportunities for us to grow. You can try to face the future calmly, think about your own goals and dreams, and then work toward them. Don’t confine yourself to these difficulties and worries. You definitely have the ability to overcome all the difficulties and challenges. Don’t give up. Keep going, and you’ll see your own growth and progress.
Thank you for your companionship and encouragement. I feel very comforted and grateful. I’ll try to adjust my mindset, and I hope I can get through this difficult time.
You’re doing great. You will definitely be able to get through this. No matter when or where, I will always support you. Believe in the future, believe in yourself. You’ve got this!
Lately I’ve been feeling really discouraged, and my mood has been very low. I keep feeling like I’m useless.
Hi, it’s okay. Everyone has low points; for example, I’ve had this feeling before too. But is there something specific, or some reason, that’s making you feel useless?
Actually, work really hasn’t been going well lately. Nothing I do feels like it’s going smoothly.

I see. When things aren’t going well at work, it can make people feel like their value is being denied, and like they’ve lost themselves. You could try looking at things from a different angle, or making your life feel more fulfilling, and not let setbacks at work affect other parts of your life.
Thank you. Hearing what you said makes me feel much better.
It’s okay. I’m really glad I could help you. You can talk more with friends and share how you’re feeling, and you can also try doing some things you like to help ease your mood a bit.
My friends and I just don’t really fit together. It’s a little hard to communicate with them.

That’s okay. You can try getting to know some people who share your interests and values; maybe you’ll make some great new friends. Be sure to believe in yourself. You will definitely meet friends who click with you.
Mm, I’ll try. Thank you.
It’s okay. You deserve a better life. If you run into things that don’t go well in the future, you can always come talk with me anytime.
Okay. Thank you for your support and encouragement.
You’re welcome. I’m always here supporting you. Hang in there!
Okay, thank you. I’ll keep trying.
Lately things have felt really bad between my girlfriend and me. She always feels like I’m not good enough to her, but I feel like I’ve already done my best.

Hi, I hear what’s been troubling you. This must be really hard for you—when you’re thinking about your girlfriend, your own feelings get overlooked. Even though you’ve been trying to meet her needs, what she expresses to you isn’t satisfaction, and that no doubt makes you feel very hurt.
Thank you for understanding how I feel. I also want to do better, but I don’t know what to do to make her feel that I truly care about her.

Maybe you could try having a good talk with your girlfriend, listen to what she wants, understand what she needs, and then respond based on her needs. You can also share your feelings with each other, let her understand what’s going on for you, and work together to find a solution.
I’ve tried, but she always feels like I’m not putting in enough effort, that I don’t care about her enough.

I understand how you feel. Maybe you haven’t fully understood that what she wants is sincere care and to feel valued. Try to understand her feelings, listen to her needs and opinions, and slowly let her feel your effort and care.
I understand. I should spend more time understanding her needs and feelings—doesn’t that mean I understand her better?

That’s right. As long as you’re willing to put thought into it, she’ll be able to feel your love. Being a better boyfriend means understanding each other’s feelings and needs; communication and sharing are very important.
Thank you for your advice. I think I’ll try to do that.
You’re welcome. I believe you can do it. Remember, at any time, we can really value each other’s feelings and needs, and grow together. You’ve got this!
Mm, I’ll keep trying. Thank you for your encouragement and support.
You’re welcome. I’ll always be here supporting you. If you run into any difficulties, feel free to come talk with me anytime. I hope your relationship with your girlfriend keeps getting better.

I feel like deep down, my self-esteem is really low. I’m not confident in myself, I think I’m not good-looking enough, that I lack attractiveness, and I also feel like my personality isn’t good enough. It’s hard for me to get close to other people. What should I do?

Hearing how you feel, I can understand the difficulty you’re in right now. First, I want to say that everyone has their own unique beauty. Don’t deny your whole worth because of some flaws you see in yourself. Your low self-evaluation may come from past experiences where you received messages that weren’t very helpful for your confidence. But now that you’re aware of this issue, it shows you already have the ability to change it. Hang in there!

Hearing your encouragement, I really do feel a lot better, but I’m still a little at a loss. I really do have a hard time communicating with people. I always feel like I don’t know what to do, and I don’t know what to say. How can I become more confident?

Many people feel uncomfortable when facing strangers, and that’s very normal. You can start by practicing with the people around you. Try taking part in some social activities, chatting with friends, opening up to your family, and interacting with others in a relaxed, proactive way. Then, based on how you actually feel, gradually build your skills in communicating with different people. You can also learn some communication skills from books.
I’ve run into some difficulties recently. I feel very lonely and helpless, and I can’t adjust my emotions. What can I do to get out of this situation?

When people face difficulties, it’s easy to have negative emotions. That’s very normal, but we also need to face them in time, otherwise they can get out of control. You can relax and relieve stress by doing more things you’re interested in, listening to music you like, or doing some physical exercise. In addition, you can also talk with some like-minded friends and hear their suggestions. If you’re able to see a professional psychiatrist or counselor, that would also be a good choice.
Thank you for the suggestions. I’ll try them. But sometimes I feel very hopeless, like I’ll never be able to get past these obstacles, and I also have some negative thoughts. What should I do?

When you feel hopeless or have negative thoughts, first of all, don’t think there’s something wrong with you. This is a very common situation. You can try to look for things that help you return to a more normal emotional state, such as listening to music you like, watching a movie you enjoy, reading a good book, talking with someone, and so on. If necessary, you can also seek help from a professional psychiatrist or counselor.
Thank you for your answer. I’ll remember your suggestions. Sometimes I also have trouble falling asleep because of my anxiety or uneasiness. Do you have any ways to help me ease this?

Sleep is very important for both our body and mind. I’d suggest doing some things before bed to reduce physical and mental stress, such as listening to light music or doing some self-relaxation exercises. You can also make adjustments to your sleep environment, such as keeping it dark and quiet, choosing comfortable bedding, and avoiding eating too much. Of course, these methods may need to be adjusted based on your own situation.
I’ll try to do some of the things you mentioned. Sometimes I feel like my emotions are easily affected by the outside world, and I don’t know how to get out of that state.

People’s emotions are often influenced by the external environment, but they are also influenced by internal self-regulation. You can practice and strengthen your ability to self-regulate through some methods, such as deep breathing, meditation, yoga, and other relaxation exercises, to improve your emotional state. In daily life, you can also gradually cultivate your mindset. Don’t always place yourself in a helpless position. Find your strengths and have a reasonable view of your weaknesses.
Thank you for giving me so many suggestions. I’ll gradually try them. Still, sometimes I feel tired and discouraged, and I don’t know what to do.

Everyone may encounter this kind of situation on the path of striving and working hard. At times like this, the most important thing is to give yourself some time and space, and let yourself rest. Maybe you need to find something enjoyable to make yourself happy, or look back on your efforts and achievements to encourage yourself. What we have to acknowledge is that life has ups and downs. Only by holding on through difficult times can we see a better tomorrow.
I understand. I’ll try to face my problems more positively, and I hope I can become a bit more confident too. Thank you so much for your help this time!

You’re welcome. I’m willing to help you. I hope that through your own efforts and actions, you can find ways to solve these difficulties, and keep improving your confidence and sense of self-worth. Hang in there!

Ever since I was little, I haven’t liked going out or talking with other people. I only liked staying in my room watching cartoons and reading storybooks. I didn’t even want to talk to my mom. If she wanted me to speak, she had to use something to get my interest, but I still might not respond. After I started school, I could play with other kids, but I still didn’t talk much. When others talked to me, I would just listen. I don’t like doing two things at once. If the first thing isn’t finished, I don’t want to start the next one. When communication goes on for too long, I feel tired and want to pull back.
Hello, my name is Lin Xi. First, I want to give you a big hug.
Thank you. I feel really irritable right now and my mood isn’t very good. I just want to stay at home.

I understand how you feel. Sometimes we need a little time alone to readjust our emotions. But I hope you can consciously spend time with your family and friends, and build stable relationships and a foundation of trust.
But I don’t know how to communicate with them. It feels really hard to talk.

That’s very normal. Sometimes we run into different kinds of communication difficulties. But that doesn’t mean you’ve given up. I believe you must have your own ways and skills. You can try to find some shared topics, share things you’re interested in, and build positive ways of interacting. When you experience the warmth and happiness that communicating with them can bring, you’ll become more and more willing to be with them.
But I always feel that talking with other people is really tiring, and I feel very weighed down.

Feeling tired and weighed down isn’t a bad thing. It’s a signal from inside you, telling you that you need time and space to gradually understand your own feelings and needs. You can communicate with them in moderation. Don’t force yourself to keep going with others for too long and end up feeling exhausted and resistant. Find a balance in being with them, so your needs are met and others don’t feel neglected.
I’m also worried that my introverted personality will affect my quality of life.

Being introverted isn’t wrong, and there’s no need to deny it. Everyone has their own unique personality and traits. As the saying goes, “however many weaknesses there are, there are just as many strengths.” We can draw on the positive energy that our own traits can bring. For example, your tendency to enjoy being alone can help you think through problems better, think independently, and stick to your own ideas and beliefs.
I’d like to understand how I can gradually get out of this psychological distress.

First, you can try to gradually face and challenge your social abilities, and that takes some courage and determination.
