You can start with people you’re relatively close to, slowly expand your social circle, and build more connections and trust. Equally important is developing your inner strength and your ability to keep your emotions stable. This can be done by building the habit of positive thinking and emotional regulation. Most importantly, don’t rush for quick results, don’t compare yourself with others, and don’t let yourself be troubled by the pressure of other people’s judgments. Everyone has their own pace and way of doing things. What matters most is being able to gradually move toward your own goals.
Thank you. I’ll try to do that.

My husband suddenly had an affair. It lasted for a little over a month, and it was physical. After this happened, his mother scolded him, saying he was useless, that neither the car nor the house was his. And yet he still thought he was so capable. She said over all these years, he had been raised into the habit of loafing around. He isn’t bad by nature, he values loyalty a lot, and he’s been good to me too. It’s just that I’ve had to worry more about daily life. After his mother scolded him, he wanted to divorce me. He said he wanted to see how far he could mess things up, that after the divorce it would be clean, he would have nothing, and he would go out and make his own way. I also know now that I had things I did wrong at the time. I was sexually cold toward him for about two months, I shouldn’t have told his mother, and his childhood friend dragged me to his workplace to look for that woman. I didn’t dare to go. I knew he cares about face the most. His buddies said I was a coward, so I went. At the time he was there, but that woman wasn’t. It was really awkward, making such a scene. He completely broke down and said we had to divorce, that he had no feelings for me at all anymore. Right now I just want to know, does this kind of behavior mean he really doesn’t love me anymore? Tomorrow he’s going off on his own to make his way in the world, and I don’t know if there will ever be a day when he wakes up and realizes. I know the only thing we can do now is both calm down. I’m also preparing to go back to my parents’ home. We haven’t divorced for now. He also wrote me an IOU for 300,000. We have a 3-year-old daughter. Right now he’s acting like everything is casual and he doesn’t care about anything.

Hello, I understand the anxiety and confusion you’re feeling right now. First, you need to calm down and take care of your emotions. Don’t let yourself become too overwhelmed with sadness. After that, you can try to look at the whole situation and identify the points of conflict. The way to resolve it comes down to two words: understanding and forgiveness.
That’s easy to say, but I’m in so much pain right now. I don’t know what to do.

I know this is very hard, but rather than getting stuck in sadness, it may help to take some steps to ease your anxiety. You can have a proper talk with him and see where the root of the problem is, and try your best to save your marriage.
Thank you for reminding me. Of course I hope to save our marriage, but I don’t know how to face him and his family. I’m really afraid he’ll leave me.

Don’t be afraid, and don’t blame yourself. In facing this issue, try to accept the reality calmly and take it slowly, step by step. Don’t rush for quick results. Keep a calm attitude, communicate with him more, and discuss possible solutions together.
But I want him to know that I really love him. I don’t want to leave him, but I don’t know how to express it.
You can express your feelings in the simplest ways. Eye contact and actions can speak louder than words. Face him with your most genuine attitude, and tell him your feelings and thoughts.
Even if I try my best to do all of that, I’ll still feel so much pain inside. I don’t know what I can do to get through this difficult time.

At a time like this, you need to take in as much positive energy from the outside as you can. Specifically, you could attend some courses on emotional regulation, talk more with relatives and friends around you, and find some activities you enjoy that can help you release your emotions and feel more at ease.
Thank you for your suggestions. I’ll think about trying them. I hope I can get out of this difficult situation as soon as possible and get back on track.

It’s okay. You’re not alone on this path. We can get through this difficult time together. Also, if you really need it, you can choose to see a mental health professional for emotional support and treatment.
Okay, I’ll consider it. Thank you for your advice and for being here with me. It really makes me feel very warm. Thank you!
You’re welcome. We’ll keep being here with you, face all the difficulties together, find the center of your life again, and keep moving forward.
My parents are always interfering in my friend circle and work circle, and they don’t let me know about it. Now my coworkers all look down on me, and my friends don’t want to talk to me either.

I can feel your unhappiness and confusion, and I’m sending you a big hug. Parents always wanting to control their child’s whole life is really too much, and it has affected your social circles. You can try communicating with them and tell them that you also need some private space and autonomy. If you run into situations where others can’t understand, don’t put all the blame on yourself either—that wouldn’t be fair. We can look for better solutions, like talking with a counselor.
Yes, my mood has been not very good. I just don’t know how to persuade them anymore. My parents always want to interfere in everything about me.

I understand the difficult situation you’re in. Even if you’ve already tried your best, you still may not be able to change how they see things. We may need to learn to accept reality, while staying firm and free in your own life, and not letting their interference affect your emotions or your performance at work. At the same time, you can also build closer relationships with the people around you, support each other, and help yourself become stronger.

When I was in high school, my dad once tricked me into meeting my homeroom teacher. He said I was always not contacting him and always losing my temper with him, but actually we had just seen each other that very morning. My dad has a very strong need to control me.

That must have felt really awful. Being caught off guard and misunderstood is very upsetting. You’ve been very brave in opening up to me, and I really appreciate it. To resolve this issue, we need to communicate better with your family and make things clear. At the same time, you also need to shift your attention, focus more on improving yourself, and help yourself become more confident and firm.
Classmates I used to be close with, when they see me, it’s like they’re seeing a crazy person. They all avoid me. I’m really hurt.

That must be very painful, and I understand your hurt. Sending you another hug. Those old friendships may no longer be there, but we can focus on the future and rebuild new relationships. Let’s not let the shadows of the past trouble who you are now. Be brave in facing the future and welcome a better life.
I really thank you. Your encouragement makes me feel like I can look ahead.

You’re welcome. I’m always here with you. As long as you’re willing, I’ll keep accompanying you through every moment that feels hard to talk about. You are a strong and brave person, and you will definitely be able to get through this difficult time.
I’ll try to find better ways to deal with this problem.

I believe you can. Every difficulty has some kind of solution. We need to trust our own inner voice, find the path that suits us best, and take responsibility for our own lives. Let’s keep going together—we can definitely make it!
Mm, let’s keep going together!
That’s right, let’s keep going together! We’re always here, don’t forget that.

Recently my depression has been really bad. Two depression assessment reports showed that I have moderate and mild depression. I really don’t know what to do anymore. I’m starting to wonder if I’m just too lazy, or if it’s the helplessness caused by a poor relationship with my spouse.

First, it takes courage to recognize that you have depression. I understand your pain. The two depression assessments showing moderate and mild depression suggest that your condition is unstable, and this calls for some self-regulation.
How should I regulate myself?

If things are especially serious, I’d suggest seeking counseling and, if appropriate, combining it with medication. But if it’s not too severe, you can also start with daily life. For example, you can find those sources of life within yourself through exercise, such as running, swimming, yoga, and so on, three to four times a week. In addition, you can manage yourself through journaling, learning relaxation techniques, going to bed early and getting up early, and making a little progress each day.
Do these methods feel like they might not be very practical?

Practice is the only criterion for testing truth. You can choose the methods that suit you, since everyone’s situation is different. At the same time, I also want to remind you not to see asking for help as a sign of failure. Counselors, friends, and family can all be people who help you. When there are difficulties, we share them and face depression together.
Mm, I’ll try these methods. Thank you for your advice. I feel much more relieved.

You’re welcome. We can pay attention to mental health together and look for an optimistic, positive, upward-looking attitude toward life. Treating depression is a long journey, but we are not alone. I hope you can come out of this low point soon and start again.
Thank you for being with me and encouraging me. I’ll keep going.
You’re welcome. When you need it, I’ll always be by your side.

Lately I’ve been communicating with someone who’s very self-focused, and it feels really uncomfortable. He always turns the topic back to himself, and it makes me feel like I’m just listening to him talk to himself. What should I do?

First, it’s important to understand what a self-focused person is. Usually, they tend to center themselves—for example, starting conversations with “I,” and finding it hard to direct their attention toward others. This is actually driven by a need for attention and acceptance that hasn’t been met. They may not have received enough attention while growing up, so this is their way of trying to get others to notice them. We can be understanding and try to understand their emotional needs, but at the same time, we also need to learn how to protect ourselves.
But he always interrupts me when I’m talking, and I feel like he doesn’t care about my feelings.

Then you could try showing your stance through your actions—for example, using a few key phrases, or pausing and waiting until he finishes communicating before you speak, to remind him to notice your presence.
But I feel like it’s especially hard for me to communicate with him. It feels like his concern about what I think is only superficial.

You can try having a deeper conversation with him, using this topic as a starting point, and work on building your relationship with him from there. If you can find some shared topics, you can slowly build mutual trust and understanding.
Thank you for your suggestions. I’ll try to do that.
You’re welcome. If you have any questions or need help with anything, remember you can come talk with me anytime. Hang in there!
Okay, I definitely will. Thank you for your support.
You’re welcome. I hope you’re able to resolve the issue smoothly, and that in the process you can feel my support and encouragement.

I’ve never really been able to trust other people. I don’t have any especially close friends—at most, just drinking buddies, I guess. I haven’t been in a relationship either. The last time I liked a girl, it went on for two years, and I feel like it left a shadow over me. Even now, I can’t really like anyone.

Hearing you say this, I’m very concerned about how you’re doing. What you’re feeling is very common, but it can affect your whole life. I’d suggest trying to open up and find a safe environment and interpersonal support. I can work with you to look at the reasons you feel unsafe, and then come up with possible solutions.

Thank you for your reply. I feel very lonely. Even when people are around me, I still don’t feel understood. No one can really listen to me. I feel like most people only pay attention to themselves for their own sake, and turn a blind eye to other people’s feelings.

I understand how you feel. This is very difficult, but it’s not impossible. If you don’t have a best friend, you can look for people who share similar values and interests. Shared interests and communities where you can find support may also help you build creative relationships. If needed, you can ask them for help, or even find a professional for counseling.

I understand. But I have very deep psychological trauma. It’s hard to tell other people, because I have fear and distrust, and I’m afraid they’ll lose confidence in me and stop understanding me. I need to break through this fear, but I don’t know where to start.

I want to tell you that you are not alone. Everyone has their own privacy and wounds, but sometimes when we open our hearts, we find that many people have gone through similar things. This is the first step, and also the hardest one, but you can start in a safe environment. The best option is to find a professional mental health doctor, who can give you better help and understanding.
Thank you for suggesting that I look for a professional for counseling. That makes me feel like I could have a safe environment. But I still feel scared and at a loss.

That’s very normal. Many people feel scared or overwhelmed in medical settings or counseling. You can try some relaxation exercises, such as meditation or breathing techniques, to ease your anxiety and fear. When you’re ready, you can start counseling. You can also choose anonymous counseling, which may make you feel more comfortable.
I might choose anonymous counseling. But I’m also worried that I’ll be diagnosed with a psychological problem, or that something unexpected will happen.

That’s also very normal. People worry about whether they’ll be diagnosed, what treatments they’ll receive, whether they’ll be asked to take on a lot of responsibility, and so on. However, these are not things you need to worry about. A professional doctor will respect your opinions very much and make a diagnosis and treatment plan based on your actual situation. The doctor’s duty and obligation are to protect your privacy and provide you with help.

I think I can start looking for a professional to get help now. But I still have reservations about the process and results of treatment. I don’t know how long I’ll need to go through treatment, or how much I’ll gain from it.

I understand your thoughts. The treatment process varies from person to person, and it takes a certain amount of time and patience before results can appear. But some treatment methods can be very beneficial, such as cognitive behavioral therapy, family therapy, medication, and so on. If you’d like to know more about treatment methods and the process, please tell me, and I can help you find more resources.
Thank you for your support and encouragement. I feel like I have more courage now. I will seek help from a professional and begin a new journey in life.

I’m proud of you. Please remember, you are not alone. You have many supporters and people walking alongside you. If you have any questions or need help, please feel free to tell me anytime. Wishing you good luck again!

Lately I keep unconsciously comparing myself with other people, and I feel like my sense of happiness drops along with it. Compared with people who are outgoing, I feel like I haven’t made many friends; compared with classmates in the same year, they’ve already published many meaningful papers. I really hate it when other people keep comparing me with others, but I also subconsciously compare myself, always thinking I have to do things as well as possible. Comparing makes me feel very anxious. How do you think I should adjust my mindset?

Human beings naturally like to compare, but we need to compare in the right way. Think about it: everyone has their own story, so simple comparisons aren’t fair. If we make judgments based only on what we see on the surface, it can bring us a lot of unnecessary pressure and anxiety. So the key is to find the right way to compare: remember these six words—focus on what matters, and don’t lose sight of yourself.
Focus on what matters? Don’t lose sight of myself? How should I understand this method?

First, “focus on what matters” means not comparing those surface-level things that trouble you, but putting the focus of comparison on areas that can truly make you stronger. For example, instead of comparing looks with Reba or wealth with Sicong, it would be better to use that time to learn and improve your own skills. At the same time, it’s also important to understand that we don’t always have the chance to fully understand other people, so we can’t draw conclusions based only on what we see on the surface.
Then how do I not lose sight of myself?

If you want to walk your own path in life well, you need to maintain a healthy mindset. When you encounter setbacks, ask yourself: What kind of life do I want? How can I make myself feel more fulfilled and happier? If I make a mistake, how can I keep a good attitude and look for a solution? The key is to guide yourself rather than force yourself, which can reduce the sense of burden on yourself and your anxiety.
I think these methods are good, but I still compare myself from time to time. What should I do?

That’s okay. Don’t force yourself to completely get rid of thoughts of comparison—that’s not realistic either. You can try writing these feelings down, learn to acknowledge your emotions, and work on controlling your actions while having these emotions. At the same time, you can also seek help and support from friends. After all, everyone has their own worries.
Thank you. I’ll do my best to adjust my mindset and focus on what matters, and not so easily compare myself with others anymore.
Very good. I believe you’ll do even better. Remember, using the right way to compare and not losing sight of yourself can help make your life more fulfilling and happier.

I told my girlfriend that she’s too harsh with me, and it makes me feel hurt. I hope she’ll care about me, treat me the way I treat her, and also buy me gifts. But when I express my feelings to her, she doesn’t seem to understand me.

Hello, I understand how you feel. Sometimes our friends or partners can’t understand our feelings, and at times like this, we feel disappointed and frustrated. But we need to know that men and women may think differently, and this can lead to gaps in communication. I suggest you choose a quiet, relaxed, easygoing moment to talk with your girlfriend. That may be more effective.
I’ve tried to communicate with her properly, but she still doesn’t understand me. I feel really helpless.

Communication takes patience and skill. You can listen more to her opinions, and also listen carefully to what she says so you can better understand her feelings and thoughts. You can also use the principles of Nonviolent Communication: first describe what you experienced, then express your feelings and needs, and finally make a specific request. This kind of approach may be easier for her to accept.
I’ll really try. Thank you for your help.
You are a very kind person, and I believe you will be able to overcome these difficulties and work on staying positive and optimistic. If you need more support, I’m always here to help you.
Thank you. I feel much better now.

You’re welcome. I’m very glad I could do something for you. Remember, whether in relationships or in life, we all need to support and understand each other so we can better get through difficulties and setbacks. Keep holding on to this positive mindset, and things will definitely get better.
Thank you for what you said. I feel more confident now.

I’m glad I could help you. Confidence and a positive attitude are important factors in overcoming difficulties. If you run into difficulties and setbacks, don’t be afraid to seek help. We all need support and help from one another to go further.
I feel very lucky to have met someone as gentle as you. Thank you for your support.

You’re wonderful too. Remember, we are not isolated in this world; there will always be people who care about us, support us, and love us. I’m very glad to be one of your supporters. If you need further help, feel free to come to me anytime.
I feel so tired right now. Why is it that even though I’ve worked so hard, I still can’t get other people’s approval? I’m almost losing the courage to keep going.

Hello! Even though we’re in different places, I want to give you a big hug. The fact that you’re questioning and struggling with where things are right now shows that your situation is causing you distress. Wanting to be affirmed by others is something everyone hopes for. But a lot of the time, the people around us can’t give us the support and recognition we want. You’re a high school student, and you’re facing a lot of pressure in both your studies and your life. You can start with the following areas to help relieve some of that pressure:
Lately my confidence has taken a huge hit. I always feel powerless in front of my coworkers. No matter how much sense I make, the other person can defeat me with just a few sentences.

Hi, dear friend! I know how painful that feeling can be. We all need affirmation and support, not to be invalidated. This is crucial for our mental health. You can try to build your own position. If the views you hold are well-founded, then stand firm and defend them, and don’t be easily swayed by others.
But I always feel like my views aren’t solid enough, and those coworkers are often sharp with their words. It’s hard for me to argue back.

I understand how difficult this is for you. When facing workplace PUA, we need to stay calm and gather evidence from different sides to make a judgment. If the views you hold are well-founded, then stand firm and defend them, even if you need to seek support from your supervisor. If what the other person says is problematic, you can refute it. You must protect your rights and interests, and not let yourself be hurt by others.
But I still feel very inferior, like other people are more capable than I am. I don’t know what to do.

Improving your own abilities is the best solution. Work hard to improve your professional skills and abilities, so you can have more of an advantage than others. At the same time, interact with colleagues in different areas, ask them for advice, and learn from other people’s experience. Once you have enough knowledge built up, no matter what others say, you’ll be able to refute them.
But when I face those malicious coworkers, I always feel like I can’t handle it.

You can try to avoid contact with these kinds of people, focus on your own work, and live each day happily. Don’t let these people’s words affect your emotions and mindset. Deal with them calmly, and don’t give them any chance to influence your thoughts.
Thank you for your advice. I’ll try to put it into practice.
You’re welcome, friend! If you need my help, contact me anytime. I’ll always be here to support you and your growth.
My grades have dropped a lot recently because half the class has been insulting me. I feel really defeated, and I’ve even had suicidal thoughts and acted on them.

Dear, I can understand how you’re feeling right now. These experiences must be very painful for you. But please believe that you’re not alone. We can all work together to get through this difficult time.
But I feel like I’ve lost all motivation and meaning. My life feels like it’s already become boring.

I understand how you feel, but I believe you still have many other dreams and goals. As we get through this difficult time, and on the road ahead, we can do our best to help you work toward your dreams and goals.
But I always feel like these thoughts and behaviors are really abnormal. I’m scared I might have some kind of illness.

These kinds of thoughts and behaviors are very common reactions after experiencing setbacks. It doesn’t mean you have an illness, but if it’s troubling you, I suggest you seek professional help. You could see a mental health professional or talk with a counselor.
Mm, I’ll consider seeing a doctor. But I feel like I’m facing a lot of pressure and difficulties, and it’s really hard to bear.

With these difficulties and pressures, we can try to address them through some positive approaches, such as finding someone who supports you, changing your attitude and behavior patterns, or making some practical, workable plans. Don’t give up because of setbacks. Every experience can make us stronger and more resilient.
Thank you for your advice, but I really feel awful.

I understand how you feel. I hope you can always remember that you’re not alone, and we will always be by your side supporting you. In the days ahead, please try as much as you can to relax and focus on yourself, take good care of yourself, and do things that make you feel happy and at ease. Everything will get better. I believe in you.

Lately I’ve been caring more and more about what other people think, and I feel really inferior. If someone is a little harsh with me, I feel like they’re bullying me, looking down on me, and I feel like the people around me don’t like me. Sometimes, because of something someone said unintentionally, I can’t let it go for a long time. This state really doesn’t feel good. What should I do?

Hello, seeing what you’re struggling with, I can understand how you feel. Having your emotions affected by other people’s criticism or comments can be really distressing. And if this issue gets magnified, it can affect our lives. I want to tell you that you’re not alone; many people have similar feelings.

First, we need to accept our feelings. Being aware that you have these feelings is very brave. Then, we need to notice our own needs. People have two basic needs: closeness and autonomy. Closeness means being seen, praised, and liked; autonomy means being able to be yourself. When you care a lot about what others think, it’s often because you hope others can recognize you and help you feel included. But when you care too much about others’ thoughts, you keep making your own space smaller and smaller, until eventually you find that you’ve become a compressed version of yourself. Change also has to happen slowly. First, recognize that these two basic needs are necessary, and that they’re okay.
Mm, sometimes I really feel like I’ve lost myself and become the way other people want me to be. Maybe I just really lack confidence. How can I build my confidence?

Yes, confidence is also very important. The way we score ourselves is often objective, and also often harsh. A lot of the time we’re very tolerant of others, but our evaluation of ourselves is very strict. We need to learn more self-appreciation and affirm what we’ve already done. When we put the focus on ourselves, rather than on other people’s opinions, we can reduce those negative emotions and increase our confidence. At the same time, finding your own interests and hobbies and learning new skills can also help us become more aware of our own value and abilities, and in that way build confidence. You can give it a try.
Thank you for your suggestions. This really helps. But sometimes I still don’t know what I should do, and I feel really lost.

That’s okay. This is also a very normal feeling. There will always be times in life when we feel lost. We can try to understand ourselves, to figure out what our true inner needs are, and what kind of life we truly want. Through this kind of reflection, we can set clearer goals, and then move toward them step by step.

However, the path toward achieving goals may not always be smooth. If we find ourselves on a rough road, we shouldn’t give up. We need to have confidence in ourselves, stay with our direction, and when difficulties come up along the way, dare to face them and dare to accept the challenge.
What you said makes sense. I understand now. Thank you for always being by my side, constantly encouraging and supporting me. I feel much better now.

I’m really happy that I could help you. Remember, we’re all on the road, and sometimes feeling lost, confused, anxious, and so on are all very normal psychological states. But we can’t mix ourselves up with setbacks. Setbacks are just the seasoning of life; they can make us stronger and braver. When we encounter setbacks, we don’t need to panic. We can calm ourselves, find ways to face these problems, readjust our mindset, and then move forward bravely. Hang in there!
I've been having some relationship problems lately, and I hope I can have someone to talk to.
I hear that you're feeling troubled. Would you be willing to share with me what's been bothering you?
I'm with my boyfriend, but my father doesn't like his father, and my mom is also against me being in a relationship. She wants me to break up with him.
Your family is putting a lot of pressure on you, but I believe your view of relationships is mature, and you have the right to speak up for your feelings.
My boyfriend is a pretty good person, and I do like him, but I feel like our relationship may have started a bit too early.

In the early stage of adulthood, a person needs to work through the confusion between independence and dependence, find the confidence to take emotional risks, and build long-term intimate relationships. These are all very important for a relationship between two people.
I also want to have a happy relationship, but my family's opposition makes me feel really conflicted.
Family opposition or expectations often make us feel discouraged and conflicted. But please remember, choosing the path you truly want is one of the most important decisions in life.
I don't know if I can withstand the impact, after all, family is too important to me.

Emotional changes, especially family factors, play a big role in how feelings develop. But please remember, the whole process happens step by step. Think about what emotional support you need most right now, and what opportunities for growth there are, and then develop your life at your own pace and in your own way.
I've thought about it for a long time, and I feel like breaking up might still be better.

A relationship needs “intimacy, passion, and commitment,” along with each person's own lifestyle and pace of development. Every relationship can either deepen or come to an end. As long as your choice fits your own growth and development, you can have the best future. Whether you break up or continue, I will always be here to support you.
I'm really grateful to have someone like you who understands me. I really want to get out of my difficulties.

This time is only temporary. Life is like a game; no matter how hard or painful it gets, don't give up on your own life. Please hold firmly to your beliefs and face each challenge in life with a positive attitude, and create a better version of yourself.
It's time for me to go to work again. Yesterday I slept all the way until 12:30 at noon, didn't do anything, and felt like I hadn't worked hard at all.
Hi, listening to you, it sounds like your previous work was really exhausting. Yesterday you really didn't have any plans—could it be because you felt useless?
I think I feel a bit helpless, like it's really hard to get a handle on the future.

Yes, that feeling is really painful. But no one is perfect, and sometimes people lose their sense of self. As long as you stick with your own direction and feel happy, that's enough. There's no need to be too hard on yourself.
Yeah. I feel like I might get really tired, but I'm also afraid of walking into the fog and not knowing what to do.

Your thoughts are understandable. After all, the future is full of unknowns and difficulties. But too much worry and tension can also affect your mood. Try to relax, leave the exhaustion and worries behind, and try new experiences and enrich yourself. That way, you’ll slowly become better.
That sounds good, but I feel like I may still be a little afraid of failing.

That’s a very normal thought, because failure and setbacks are a normal part of life. As long as you stick with your own direction and put in the effort, you will inevitably encounter challenges. But challenges are also the beginning of growth. Learn from failure and keep working forward.
Thank you, I’ll try. But sometimes I still get stuck in negative emotions and can’t pull myself out.

That’s very normal. After all, we’re only human. But no matter when it happens, don’t give up on yourself. Everyone runs into difficulties, and the resilient you will get through this. Also, if this happens, you can talk with friends, family, or a professional to get help and find solutions.
Thank you for your support. Your words have given me a lot of encouragement.
You’re welcome. I’ll always be by your side, accompanying you through every difficult time. If you need help, please be sure to tell me. I’ll do my best to help you.

My health hasn’t been very good lately. I often get sick, and because of the pressure from studying, I haven’t been sleeping well either. Even my period has become irregular. Recently I’ve also been feeling discomfort in my lower body, but I don’t dare tell my family. I’m afraid they’ll misunderstand. I don’t know what to do.

I’m sending you a hug. I really understand how difficult this feels for you. Health concerns are very important, and I suggest you talk with your mom about going to the hospital for a full checkup. If there really is something wrong, don’t be afraid of surgery. Medical technology is very advanced now, and recovery after surgery can be quite fast. At the same time, your family’s support and understanding are very important.
I’m really scared. I’m afraid it might be some serious illness.

Try not to worry too much. A lot of the time, what we imagine is worse than the reality. The doctor will give you the right diagnosis and treatment plan based on your symptoms and test results. You need to trust their professional ability.
But I’m afraid going to the hospital will be very expensive. My family doesn’t have that much money.

You can first go to a community hospital or your school medical center to have it checked. The cost is usually more reasonable. If you need to buy medication, you can also ask the pharmacist at the drugstore. They can help you choose more affordable medicines.
Thank you for your advice. I’ll think about it. But I still feel very heavy, and I don’t know how to adjust.

Feeling low can also be one of the signs that your body isn’t feeling well, so don’t blame yourself too much. You can try some relaxing activities, like listening to music, exercising, drawing, and so on, to help adjust your mood. At the same time, keeping good daily routines and eating habits is also very important.
Hearing what you said makes me feel very warm, like I have a little bit of hope now. Thank you for your support and encouragement.

You’re welcome. I’m willing to be your friend and supporter. Let’s hang in there together and help both your body and your mood get better. If you need any help, or if you’d like to share your progress with me, you can contact me anytime.
I’m a bit troubled. A boy in kindergarten often steps on snails on the road and crushes them, and picks pretty flowers and crumples them up. Does this count as some kind of mental illness?

It sounds like you’re really worried about this boy’s behavior. But try not to worry too much. He’s still very young, and these behaviors may just be signs that he hasn’t yet learned how to manage his emotions and actions.
But I’m worried that this kind of behavior might have a negative impact on his development.

You’re someone who cares about him, and that’s a good thing. Sometimes our worries can help us notice problems, but they can also make us see problems that may not be there. The boy’s behavior is worth paying attention to, but there’s no need to over-interpret it. The key is to find the right way to help him manage his behavior.
Then what do you think I should do to help him?

You could try talking with him to understand why he does this, and then try to guide him toward better ways of expressing himself. You could also consider talking with his kindergarten teacher or other professionals; they may have better suggestions.
Thank you for your advice. I’ll do my best to help him find better ways to express himself.
You’re doing great! In this process, remember to give both yourself and him some tolerance and understanding. This takes time and patience.
I will. Thank you for your support and encouragement. You’ve helped me handle my emotions better.
You’re very welcome. I’m glad I could help. If you need any other help, you can talk with me anytime.

The college entrance exam is finally over. For four years, because of it, I kept to myself and studied desperately, but in the end I didn’t do well. Now I don’t feel like there’s any hope. My mom started introducing me to potential partners, and I’ve begun to accept it. I thought maybe if I found someone, I wouldn’t feel so sad.
I understand how you feel. The college entrance exam is a very important exam, and you put a lot of effort into it. But it’s only one stage of life. Failing at it doesn’t mean you’re worthless.
But I feel like a failure, like I’ll never be successful in my whole life.

Everyone faces setbacks and difficulties at different times, but that doesn’t mean you have no chance of success. There are still many good moments in your high school life waiting for you to experience.
But right now I can’t feel anything. I’m just an empty shell.

I know you’re feeling very lost right now, but this is temporary. There are many ways to help you rebuild your confidence and motivation, like finding a hobby you enjoy or taking part in volunteer work.
I’m being introduced to potential partners again now, but I don’t know if I’m capable of managing a marriage.
Managing a marriage also takes practice, just like studying. Don’t be afraid of failing. Most people eventually succeed after going through some setbacks and difficulties.
I’m really grateful for your understanding and support right now. I’ll try to accept my failure, and I’ll also actively look for new opportunities and possibilities.
I’m very glad I could help you. You’re not alone. Whenever you need someone’s companionship and support, I’m here for you.

Things have been really bad lately. I’ve been married for 8 years, and we have a son and a daughter. We should have been living a happy life, but my wife has always disliked my parents. On top of that, recently my father’s health has gotten worse and he needs care, but my wife never shows concern, and even uses insulting language. Last night we had another fight because of this, and for the first time I got physical. But her reaction was still even stronger than mine, and it made me feel very hopeless. Should I get divorced or not?

I can see that you’re troubled by this and feeling at a loss, and that’s understandable. It’s really not easy for you to take care of your father, who has many health issues, and your wife’s attitude has hurt you deeply. As for her emotions and behavior, we can try to understand what might be going on underneath.
Yes, I really have tried, but it’s very hard for me to find her reasons.

Yes, finding the root of the problem isn’t easy. I suggest that the two of you use communication as the foundation, start from the perspective of understanding each other, and work together to resolve the problem.
But I’m afraid our focus is different, and we’ll never be able to solve this problem.

Don’t be afraid. We can look for common ground to narrow the differences and build understanding and compassion. Please try to listen to her emotions and understand what may be behind her agitation, while also letting her understand your difficulties and feelings.
Actually, we’ve tried doing this before, but we still couldn’t resolve the conflicts.

Try once more. In daily life, please care about her, think from her perspective, and pay attention to her feelings and needs. Improve how you position your role in the family, and provide her with the right support and help.
Yes, I understand. The missing part in my role as a husband in the family. She needs me to do more.
Yes. Please face the real issues and focus on solving the problem. Only by finding a suitable solution can you get out of this difficult situation.
Thank you for your encouragement and help. I’ll try again to face reality and find a way to solve the problem.
I’m glad I could help you. If you need any help or advice, please contact me.
Okay, thank you. I feel confident now. This time I’ll try to communicate properly.
A 14-year-old girl was walking around a mall when a group of girls she didn’t know dragged her into a stairwell and took turns beating her for nearly an hour.
Hello, I’m really sorry to hear this happened. What you need right now is understanding and support. How are you feeling now?
I feel really scared and upset right now. I feel so helpless, and I don’t dare tell my parents.

What you’re feeling is very normal. People who are bullied can feel this way. You don’t need to worry about telling your parents; they can give you support and help. At the same time, you can also consider seeking support and protection from your school.
But why were those girls so arrogant? I really don’t understand.
What they did is unacceptable, but there may be many reasons why they acted that way. Maybe they come from difficult families and lack love and care, or maybe they themselves have been bullied.
But how could they do something like that?

Their behavior was wrong, but please remember, this is not your fault. When it comes to them, we should try to stay tolerant and understanding, even though that’s very hard. What they need is change and help, and we should do our best to help them.
What should I do now?

First, please seek medical and legal support. Then, consider finding a psychotherapist or counselor for help. You may be affected by trauma, so you need enough support and treatment to help you recover.
Thank you. I’ll take action as soon as possible.
You’re welcome. Remember, you must stay strong and face all of this bravely. You are not alone; we will always support you.
I was pretty laid-back in college. After graduating, I couldn’t find a suitable job, and I’ve been very anxious. I also can’t really focus on things day to day.

Hello! I really understand how you’re feeling right now. The pressure of not being able to find a job can be really heavy. But try not to worry too much, because you’re not alone. You may need to adjust your state a bit and see if there are areas you can improve.
But I feel like I’ve already been trying really hard, and I still can’t find a job. My mood has been getting more and more discouraged.
I know this is hard, but try to keep a positive mindset and keep trying. Let’s think together about what changes you could make to improve your chances of finding a job.
Actually, I’ve been wondering if it’s because I’m not capable enough that I can’t find a job.

That thought is very normal, but try not to be too hard on yourself. After all, improving your abilities takes time and effort. You could start by finding other ways to make yourself more competitive, such as building your skills or taking some relevant courses.
But I always feel like nothing I do is really effective, and that makes me even more anxious.

Don’t blame yourself. Anxiety can make it easier to see problems as huge burdens. Try to accept more support and encouragement, and you can also talk with friends or family to help your emotions settle down.
I think I really do need to find an outlet to let out my emotions.

Of course. That’s a very normal situation. You could try some activities that help you relax, such as working out, drawing, listening to music, and so on. These can help you calm down and better face the challenges ahead.
Thank you for your support. I’ll do my best to become better.
You’re welcome. I’m glad I could help. We all need some support and resonance. I hope these methods can bring you some relief and hope. Hang in there!
Lately I’ve been feeling really anxious and I’m having a hard time concentrating. What should I do?
First, you need to know that anxiety is a very normal emotion, so don’t be afraid of it. You can try ways to relax your body and mind, like deep breathing, meditation, or exercise.
But I always feel like I won’t do well, and that there will be negative outcomes.
To change this way of thinking, you can focus your attention on the positive side. For example, think about the things you’ve already completed successfully, or your strengths and advantages.
I’ll try. Recently I’ve been learning about the birdcage effect, but I don’t really understand how to apply it.

The birdcage effect basically means that people often get trapped in a certain way of thinking and find it hard to get out. You can try using more positive decisions to break that inertia. For example, sign up for some challenging courses or try new things.
Mm, I’ll try taking part in some new activities. But what if I feel like I can’t complete these challenges?

Try not to get too caught up in the outcomes; actually, the key is the process. Trying something new is already a good achievement in itself. If you encounter challenges that are too difficult, you can also adjust your goals appropriately and move forward slowly in small steps.
Thank you for your support and understanding. I’ll keep trying to change my way of thinking and face life and work with a more positive mindset.
I believe you can definitely do very well. Don’t give up. Please remember, taking the first step is always the hardest.

My relationship with my husband is in crisis because of the child, financial pressure, and other reasons. He’s also been chatting with someone else. What should I do to keep my husband away from an affair?

Hi, I can see that you’re feeling very confused right now. Sending you a hug, dear. It seems your marriage is facing some challenges. During your postpartum confinement period, you found out that your husband was chatting with a woman, but he denied having an affair. After a child is born, the warmth between a couple may decrease, and the husband may become more likely to cheat. However, the three elements of an intimate relationship are intimacy, passion, and commitment. As long as you spend time together often, it’s still possible to rekindle the passion from when you were deeply in love. You can talk with your husband about creating opportunities for just the two of you during your free time. For example, one night each week or two nights each month, you could have your parents or in-laws take care of the child, so the two of you can enjoy some quality time. If your financial situation allows, you could also hire a live-in nanny to care for the child, giving you more time together. These arrangements may help your husband feel your attention toward him and reduce the possibility of him cheating. I hope my suggestions can be helpful to you.

Lately, I’ve been arguing with my family a lot. They’re always putting these strange accusations on me. At first I tried to be tolerant, but later I started swearing at them and insulting them. I feel like I can’t get along with them anymore.

It sounds like your emotions are really mixed—there’s some hurt and anger there, and those are very real feelings. If certain things your family says or does upset you, you could first pause and try to clarify any misunderstandings, or express your feelings and the facts. This may help make the root of the conflict clearer, so you can communicate better and work through the problem.
Actually, we didn’t really have any major conflicts before. It’s just that they always feel like I don’t care enough about the family, and they even think my friends are more important than they are.

So the accusations and blame your parents put on you may just be because they need more attention and care. They may feel that you haven’t fully understood the importance of family, and that’s why they have expectations of you and complaints. At the same time, you can also share your thoughts and feelings with them, so they can understand you better.
But sometimes the way they talk really makes me angry, to the point where I want to curse at them.

That’s a very normal emotional reaction, but you do need to learn to manage your emotions. Maybe after your feelings have calmed down a little, you can communicate with them better and let them know that you hope they can talk with you in a gentler way. That may also help make your relationship more harmonious.
But I always feel like I don’t have this problem when I’m with friends, and my mindset is much better too.

Being with friends can indeed feel relaxed and pressure-free. But when we’re with family, the psychological pressure is often greater, because family has higher expectations of us and there’s more responsibility. But that doesn’t mean you can’t be happy with your family. It just takes some communication and a process of adjusting.
Sometimes I feel really useless. Why am I always unable to soothe my own emotions?

Emotion management really is something that takes effort to learn and build, and it’s not something that can be done overnight. You could try calming your emotions through some relaxing activities, like doing yoga or meditation. You could also find a trusted friend or a counselor to talk with.
How should I better deal with conflicts with my family?

First, you can try communicating with your family and expressing your thoughts and feelings. If it feels hard to communicate, or if you need more professional help, you can consider looking for more specific approaches, such as family therapy or individual counseling. If needed, you can seek help from a professional, so you can better cope with and handle family conflicts.
Lately, I keep thinking that even though I’m with my current partner, I always remember how good my ex was, and as I think about it, I start crying.

Hello! I really understand what you’re going through, because many of us can have feelings like this. I think there may be two reasons. First, you may still have some unresolved feelings and issues, which leads you to think of your ex. Second, your current partner may not seem as good as your ex, and in some ways you may be magnifying his shortcomings. What do you think about this?
My relationship with my ex was very deep, and it’s a bit hard for me to accept that he chose another woman. When I see him happy, I feel sad.
I understand. Thinking about your feelings, you could try talking with him now and telling him how you feel. After you communicate with him, you may gain a lot of understanding and support.
Thank you for your suggestion. But what should I do now?

First, you need to let go of your feelings and emotions, and let yourself calm down. Next, you can have a good conversation with your partner, see whether you can resolve the issues between you, and try to discover the strengths and good memories in your relationship. When you focus on the present, you may realize that there are still many things about him that are worth loving and paying attention to.
Okay, I’ll have a good talk with him, and I’ll also try to let go of my past and focus on the present and the future.

That’s a very good idea! When you try to accept reality and work on becoming stronger and braver, you’ll find yourself becoming happier and more joyful, and there will be more good things waiting for you in the future.
Thank you for your help and support. I’ll work hard and help myself become better!
You’re welcome. You can come talk to me anytime. I’ll always be here with you, and I’ll offer help and support when you need it. I believe in you—everything will get better!
Thank you for the support and encouragement you’ve given me. I feel very warm and comforted. I’ll really cherish the relationship we’ve built.

This is what I should do. I’m very glad I can help you get through this difficult time and grow together with you. Believe in yourself, and believe in your choices. Your future will definitely be happier and more fulfilling!

I’ve been feeling very anxious lately because I come from a divorced family and was raised by my grandparents. My parents never really gave me much money before either. I’m 26 now, and in 2019 I got together with a really good girlfriend. She’s great, and our education and jobs aren’t that different, but now I’m having a lot of financial problems. Last October she talked with me about wanting to buy a home, but my father had no money, so he told me to go do construction contracting with him to make money. The 80,000 yuan I put in upfront was all from online loans, and now every month I’m struggling with the repayments. But my father has just been idle and doesn’t want to go out and look for work. I feel extremely disappointed and helpless now, because I can’t let my girlfriend down, but financially it’s really hard for me to build a future with her. Getting married and buying a home both require a lot of money. Right now I only make 5,000 yuan a month, and the money I need has reached 600,000 yuan. Under this kind of pressure, it’s really hard for me to hold on.

Hello! After reading what you shared, I can sense how much pain you’re in. But I want you to know that these problems can be solved. Although you come from a divorced family, that does not define you. You have a girlfriend who loves you, and there are also many people in your world who love and support you. Let’s think through some possible solutions together. You might consider talking with your girlfriend again about whether the plan to buy a home could be delayed, and look for other sources of financial support. In this regard, you could also consider taking out a bank loan or applying for credit card installment payments. As for your father, you can communicate with him properly, help him look for work, or provide support in other ways. In addition, you could also consider some side jobs or part-time work to increase your sources of income. Most importantly, don’t give up on yourself. Keep going, and life will get better.

Thank you for your suggestions. I’ll think about them. But sometimes I feel lost and down about my life, and I don’t know what my future will become. I’m really afraid I won’t be able to take on the responsibility for my girlfriend and will let her down.

I can feel your worry and fear. But think about it: the effort and hard work you’re putting in now have already made you a responsible and capable person. You don’t have nothing—you already have a job and a girlfriend who loves you. Our future isn’t completely decided by fate; a lot of the time, it’s decided by our own choices. So you need to believe in yourself, shift your mindset, and face the future actively. Your life can definitely be full of hope and possibilities. And your girlfriend’s support and encouragement can also give you more motivation.

You’re right. I’ll work on facing the future and changing my mindset. But right now I still feel very depressed and in pain. Sometimes I even think about suicide, and I don’t know how to deal with these negative emotions.

Hearing about your pain and these thoughts, I’m very concerned about your mental health. First, you need to know that suicide is not a way to solve problems; it will only cause greater harm and pain. So you need to give yourself some time and space to release these negative emotions and find ways to solve the problems. You can try some ways to relax and soothe your body and mind, such as listening to music, taking walks, meditating, and so on. These can help you adjust and balance your mindset, and ease stress and anxiety. At the same time, you can also seek help from professionals, such as a counselor or a psychiatrist.

Thank you for your suggestions. I’ll try them. Now I have a question I’d like to ask you. I feel like I’m already an adult, but in terms of family and finances I still need to rely on others, and that makes me feel like I have no self-respect or independence. What should I do to get out of this unhealthy state?

Hearing your confusion, I understand how you see adulthood as needing independence and self-reliance. But we need to know that everyone’s growth and living environment are different, and help from family and financially is also meant to help us develop and grow better. So you don’t need to feel powerless and helpless about yourself. Instead, try to face reality actively, set goals and plans for your future, and keep working hard and making progress. At the same time, you can learn more skills for taking care of yourself and more knowledge about financial management, so that you can become more independent and self-reliant. Most importantly, you need to firmly believe that you are capable of doing better, and don’t give up easily or lose confidence.

Okay, I’ll work hard to learn and put it into practice. Thank you very much for your help and support. I feel much better now. At the same time, your suggestions have helped me see that the future is full of hope and confidence. Thank you!

I’m very glad I could offer you help and support. Remember, we are all part of one big family, and we need to help and support one another. I wish you a better life in the future. Keep moving forward and keep growing!
I’ve been affected by it since I was nine, and that person is still alive now, so there’s no clear end point.

Thank you so much for sharing this with me. Sending you a hug. What you described helps me sense the pain and wishes you’re carrying inside. I suggest you try to understand yourself and comfort yourself. Doing this may make your heart feel a little lighter, and it can help you think about what to do next.

My social life and the way I deal with people have been affected now. I’ve become very selfish, sensitive, insecure, and easily influenced by others, and I often feel anxious and sad. It’s hard for me to fit in with people from ordinary families, and some people think I’m strange.

I’m very sorry to hear that. Try to look at your current state in a rational way and recognize the reality; that can also help with the changes you make next. Please try to realize that who you are now is different from who you were in the past, and also tell yourself that you do have strengths. At the same time, you can learn to love yourself through your actions, because it is possible to change yourself.
I used to have bad habits, like lying and taking other people’s things. Now I’m trying to change these problems.

That’s great! You’re already trying to change yourself through your actions, and that’s a very important step. We can also do more, such as respecting your own feelings, paying attention to how you feel, meeting your own needs, and doing things you like. This will help you rebuild your sense of self-worth and bring about better relationships.
Sometimes I get really upset because of other people’s matters, and I cry and get angry easily. If I can’t control my emotions, things will get worse.

I understand how you feel. Learning to manage your emotions and no longer getting upset over other people’s matters is a gradual process that takes long-term persistence and trying. You can see this as part of trying to help yourself become better, and it will also bring more positive relationships.
I feel like my confidence has been greatly affected. It’s hard for me to believe I can accomplish anything.

That’s a normal feeling, but you can also gradually build your confidence by learning and achieving small goals. So I also hope you can remember that you’ve already bravely taken the first step forward, and that is worth celebrating.
I always feel like I’m so pitiful, and that makes me live in a way that doesn’t feel free. I don’t know what to do.

It’s very important to realize that you are unique. Try to let go of judging and denying yourself, and learn to have compassion for yourself. When you start being gentler with yourself, you’ll also be able to live more freely and get along with others more happily.
Thank you so much for your advice and support. I feel much better now.

I’m glad my suggestions could help you. If you need anything, don’t hesitate to reach out to me for help. Lastly, remember that the unique person you are is already good enough and worthy of being loved.
I often hear the saying, “There’s nothing in this world more important than family and friends,” but every time I hear it, I ask myself: are these things really important to me?
Your feelings are very normal. People always say family and friends are the most important, but our own feelings are very important too. What are you thinking about?
I’m thinking about something that happened in high school. There was a friend who was really fake at the time, and it made me really dislike him.
It sounds like you feel somewhat disappointed and upset with this friend, and that’s very normal. Would you like to talk more about what happened?

Back then, he and I argued over something small. I wasn’t doing well in physics, and he promised to help me with the multiple-choice questions, but in the end he ignored me. After that, he kept acting like nothing had happened, which made me feel very disappointed.
That really sounds painful. Sometimes what we hope for doesn’t always happen. How do you feel about this experience?
I feel very let down and discouraged. It makes me wonder whether this friend is really worth me investing my feelings in.
It’s normal to feel disappointed and discouraged, but also don’t forget that you are the main character within your own weight. Do you think this friend is still worth you giving anything to?
I can’t answer that question right now. I trust him less and less, and I don’t want to invest any more feelings in him.
You have the right to decide your own life. Relationships are complicated, and sometimes people disappoint us. Do you think there are other places where you can look for support and care?
I don’t know. I feel like it’s always been hard for me to make real friends.
Communication is a very complicated process. But don’t lose hope, and at the same time, don’t overlook the people who truly care about you and support you. Do you have friends?
I don’t have very close friends, only some friends on the surface.
That sounds lonely. But you can take part in some activities, find people who share your interests, and make friends with them.
Mm, maybe I should also be a bit more proactive, try new things, and meet new people.
Exactly. Don’t be afraid to try to get to know new people. Sometimes unexpected friendships can quietly come about.
Mm, thank you. I’ll try to do that.
You’re welcome. Remember, you’re not alone. There are people who will support you.

Ever since I was little, my mother has been pretty strict with me. Now that I’m grown up and already working, I feel more and more like I can’t get along with her peacefully. She is always negating me and thinks what she says is right, and it’s made me less and less confident in myself. Whenever I talk with her, it ends badly. I don’t dare push back because I’m afraid she’ll get angry, but I’m also really angry inside… I’m afraid of conflict, afraid of making other people angry. What should I do to feel a bit better?

Many people have run into this kind of problem, just like you. When we’re facing a tense situation, we often feel at a loss. But please don’t give up hope. First, please know that you’re not alone. Many people have gone through difficulties interacting with their parents and feel confused, just like you. To begin with, we need to help you rebuild your confidence.
I really need to rebuild my self-confidence.

Yes, confidence is an important quality that everyone needs. As adults, we should begin to look for our own value, find our own direction for development, and build up experience and knowledge, so that we can become more confident. This isn’t an easy thing to do; it takes time and effort.
Where should I start?

First, please reflect on what exactly you’re afraid of, and why you’re afraid of communicating with your mother. Are you afraid your thoughts will be denied? Or are you afraid of having a conflict with her? Please try to answer these questions.
I’m afraid of being denied and of having conflict with her.

Okay. Now that you’ve clarified what’s troubling you, let’s look for solutions. You can spend some time thinking about how to communicate and express your views, and with the help of a counselor, improve your interpersonal communication skills. At the same time, you could also find a close friend to confide in, or become a volunteer, and find your own sense of value.
Thank you. I’ll think about your suggestions.

You’re welcome. I’m glad I could help you. Please remember, you are a valuable person, and you deserve to be loved and respected. Don’t forget your worth, and don’t be afraid to express your thoughts. Let’s work on this together and help you become better!

Because I don’t want to go out and see people, and I just want to stay by myself, I often skip class and stay in my dorm. Sometimes I keep having the impulse to die. When the impulse comes up, I can’t think about anything and only want to die. My whole body feels weak, I lie in bed and can’t do anything. I want to die but can’t even die, and it only eases after three or four hours. Starting eight months ago, I’ve been self-harming every once in a while. I don’t want anyone to know. It just makes me feel a little better inside, like a useless person like me has received a bit of punishment too. Actually, this is just self-comfort; it doesn’t count as punishment at all. I already feel like I can’t do anything, I can’t see a future, and every day I’m just wasting resources. I’m disgusting and trash, always causing trouble for others. I really wish there were some way to leave my parents a sum of money and then just hurry up and die. I also know that I’m lazy, not motivated, and can’t do anything. I’m always thinking about escaping. When I walk on the street, I feel as disgusting as a lump of flesh moving around. I can’t do anything well, not even suicide. I’ve thought of all kinds of ways to die but haven’t carried them out, and if I just died like this, I’d be so sorry to the parents who raised me. I really want to die, but I still can’t die. I’ve lived an ordinary life that could even count as happy, but all I want is to die. If only this chance had been given to someone else, how much better that would be. But it just had to be a thing like me living in this world. When I think of that, I want to throw up…
Hello! I read what you shared carefully.
I feel like I’m already on the edge of breaking down. What should I do?
Don’t worry, everything will pass. The pain and torment you’re going through are actually something many other people are going through too, and some may be in even more pain than you.
But I feel like I’m completely useless. Other people are ashamed of me, and I also want to hide so no one can see me.

I don’t know when it started or what happened that made you evaluate yourself so poorly, but it’s undeniable that each of us tends to see ourselves as much worse than we really are. And everyone has value. Look around you, and you will definitely be able to find the strengths you have among them!
But I feel like I don’t have any strengths at all. I’m good for nothing.

In this society, we’re very easily influenced by the media, such as the news, newspapers, the internet, and so on. Then this influence spreads from person to person, and can even change shape. For example, in the past, society promoted the “shortcomings” theory and advocated all-around development. This was actually a management need of a certain era, or a product marketing strategy, but ordinary people were deeply misled by it. How many people has this flattened, human-damaging theory harmed? How many people go their whole lives unable to find their own value, always staring at their weaknesses? You need to know: we should live by relying on our strengths! What this world needs is our strengths. Our weaknesses will naturally be made up for because they are someone else’s strengths. You have them too. You only live this once—are you going to treat your life in such a confused way? Pull yourself together, wash your face, and take a good look at yourself...
But I feel like I’m good for nothing and have no strengths.

Your mood—do you also cry easily, or have symptoms of slowed thinking? Have you ever been diagnosed with depression? If not, I suggest you get a full assessment right away, and then use appropriate methods for treatment. If you’ve already been diagnosed, don’t worry. These thoughts and emotions are the roar of the illness; they aren’t reality. Because this happens in the inner world, we can’t easily tell the difference. Trust me, cooperate with treatment, relax a little, do what’s in front of you, and you will recover.
I’ve never dared to see a doctor. I’m afraid of being diagnosed with depression.
Don’t be afraid. Break through your own limits and go see a doctor or a psychologist. They will give you professional treatment suggestions and help you ease your pain.
But I don’t know how to say it. Will other people laugh at me? Will they distance themselves from me?

These thoughts are very common, but you need to know that every experience and feeling you have is important. People should respect your feelings and shouldn’t dismiss them. Also, you can consider seeing a professional psychologist. They will keep things confidential and won’t disclose your information, and they will also help you.
Thank you for your encouragement and support. I’ll consider going to see a psychologist.
You’re welcome. What you need is a tolerant environment and support. If there is anything you need help with, I will be here, staying with you as you get through this difficult time.

When I’m idle, I feel physically uncomfortable. It feels like something is pressing on the top of my head, and my shoulders and back get tight. I feel unsteady when I stand! When I’m scared, it feels like my legs go weak. I’ve taken a lot of medication, but it hasn’t helped. I want to make myself a bit braver. What should I do?

Hello! I understand your current situation. No need to worry—we can explore it together. The physical discomfort you described can be considered from a mind-body perspective. We can try to work on it from the psychological side. Would you agree?
Yes, I’m willing to try.

I understand your concern about your physical condition. If a doctor has done a thorough examination and found no problems, we can start from the psychological side to help ease your physical discomfort. You mentioned before that you feel timid and want to try to become a little braver. I suggest starting with relaxing your mind, recognizing your body’s reactions, and actively facing your fears.
I’d like the supporter to explain it to me more specifically.

Okay. First, when you feel afraid, you can try to accept that feeling and let yourself get used to it, rather than resisting it. Second, you can try to understand why you feel afraid and tense, and then challenge your unreasonable thoughts. Finally, don’t forget to relax yourself—for example, listening to music, watching movies, getting a massage, taking walks, and so on. Find a way that suits you to help yourself relax.
These methods look very practical. I’ll try to put them into practice. I’d like to ask, when physical discomfort appears, how should I respond?

When physical discomfort appears, we can first pay attention to the body’s reactions, take a short rest, and give your body enough attention. Try not to worry too much; most physical discomfort will get better on its own. If you need an examination, please go to a regular hospital or clinic and find the right doctor and clinic.
Okay, I’ll handle this carefully and won’t worry too much. I have one more question: when I feel lost about the future, how can I find direction?

When you feel lost, you can try to understand your inner needs and personal values, pay attention to your interests and hobbies, identify your strengths and what you’re good at, and look for directions in work, volunteering, hobbies, and so on. You can also try communicating with some professionals and seek advice in related areas. But don’t be too anxious. I believe you’ll smoothly find a path that suits you.
Thank you for your detailed guidance and support. I’ll take it one step at a time.

People need to understand, trust, and get along with one another, joining hands and working together to get through difficult times. I hope our conversation can help you. Wishing you health and happiness, and success in pursuing your true self!

I feel like I really don’t like the major I’m studying. In my first year, I was forced by a teacher to choose it, and now I’m in my second year and I’ve been thinking about dropping out. Every day I feel muddled, just taking exams for the sake of exams. When I’m lying in bed awake, I don’t move at all. I hold my phone and stare blankly, and I don’t want to do anything else.

Friend, please try not to be too negative. Everyone runs into all kinds of difficulties in life, and I can deeply relate to the issues you’re facing. First, it’s important to be clear that you are not fighting this alone. You can look for people to help you, such as teachers, counselors, classmates, and your family and friends. Talk with them about how you feel, make a plan for improvement together, and work together to find a solution.
You’re right, but I really don’t want to keep studying this major anymore. I have no interest or motivation at all.

Yes, studying a major you have no interest or motivation for can be truly painful. But maybe you can try looking at the problem from another angle. Yes, studying is challenging, but this kind of challenge can also make you stronger. You can try making a study plan for yourself, finding your own way of learning, and finding a direction that interests you. At a specific time and place, study with focus. When you’ve mastered certain skills and knowledge, you may find that it gives you a real sense of accomplishment.
But I feel like even if I graduate in the future, I won’t work in this field.

On the contrary, after you graduate, you will do work related to this major. But not all jobs are one-dimensional. A lot of the time, one job involves knowledge from multiple fields, such as economics, programming, human resources, design, and so on. Although that can be more complex, it can also make your career richer.
I want to know what jobs I could choose after graduation.

Actually, you could think about possible graduate school directions early in your college years, so that after graduation you’ll have more opportunities to choose work you like. You can also learn about different industries and how they operate internally through internships, and increase your chances to understand the workplace.
But I have depression, and I’m always distracted when I study.

I understand your struggle. It often makes you feel low. But the problems you’re facing can be solved. For this, you can do some preparation. For example, you can read some books about improving attention, use exercise to improve your self-discipline and attention, and strengthen your focus and perseverance. At the same time, talk with a doctor or a psychological counselor to get support and help from others.
Hearing what you said is starting to make me feel hopeful, but sometimes my mood is still very low.

At times like this, you might try relaxing your body and mind, broadening your perspective, and letting yourself get a temporary break from the pressure. Or find some things you especially enjoy, such as exercise, music, movies, and so on. These can help you relax and also broaden your perspective.
I feel much better now. Thank you.

You’re welcome. You can contact me anytime. Remember, don’t give up in the face of the difficulties you’re dealing with. If you keep going, you will definitely find your direction, get through this difficult time, and welcome a brighter future.

My mom has been working this whole time, but she’s not in good health. She has diabetes and high blood pressure. I’ve tried to persuade her to rest, but she never listens, and all the money she earns ends up going toward medical treatment. What do you think I should do to change her mind?

I can understand your concern. Perhaps you could try communicating with your mom and let her know about her family’s care and love for her. You can tell her that her health is the most important thing, and that she needs to rest and relax appropriately.
But my mom always feels like there isn’t enough money, so she doesn’t dare to rest. I’m really troubled and don’t know how to solve this problem.

That’s very normal. Many people have this kind of worry. You could work with your mom to make a reasonable budget and plan, so she can understand that money isn’t everything, and that health is what matters most.
But I feel like my mom is always overworking, and it’s even affecting our family life. I’m worried about her.

Your worry is very understandable. I’d suggest that you communicate with your mom and help her understand that balancing family and work is very important. Let her know that her health and the health of the family are also very important.
I know what you’re saying is right, but I feel like I’m not capable enough to persuade my mom. I really need help.
You need to know that you don’t have to face this difficulty alone. You can ask relatives and friends for help, and you can also seek relevant professional advice and support.
What you said makes a lot of sense. I’ll try talking with my mom, and I’ll also ask relatives and friends for help. Thank you for your support.
You’re welcome. Please remember that you are not alone. There are many people around you supporting you, including me. I hope you can resolve this difficulty smoothly, and I wish you all the best.

We were introduced by relatives. The first time we met, it felt really good, and I liked her a lot. After knowing each other for one month, we got engaged. But after the engagement, I found that she had changed. She’s really cold toward me, and she has a lot of male friends. She says they’re all friends she grew up with, and if anything were going to happen, it would have happened long ago. But sometimes the way they chat feels ambiguous, and it makes me really jealous. And whenever I bring it up, she gets very angry and says if I can’t accept it, then let’s just end it. I really like her now. She says I’m too good to her and it puts too much pressure on her. She says not to make everything I do revolve around her, not to do everything for her, and to live my own life well. She says before we get married, I shouldn’t interfere with her, and that doing this will only make the distance between us greater and greater. We’re long-distance. I go see her about every 10 days.
