Her family treats me especially well. We’ve been together five months now. She says I’m getting more and more childish, and that everything I do annoys her. What should I do? Please, teachers, give me some advice. I really want to win her back. I don’t want to lose her.

I’m sorry to hear what you’re going through. First, I want to say that I can sense how conflicted you feel: you want the relationship with your girlfriend to get better, but you’re also afraid of losing her because of it. You’ve been trying hard to please her and make her happy, but it seems you haven’t received the response you hoped for. Maybe you could look at this from another angle: is it possible that you’re being a bit too eager, both with yourself and with the relationship between you two?

I can’t not be so eager, because I really love her. I want to be with her. But I always feel like she’s happier and more at ease when she’s with other people, and I’m just an accessory in her life, so I feel very anxious.

I can understand how you feel, but we all need to know that love isn’t built on binding someone or controlling them. If we force ourselves to become part of someone else’s life, it will only make the distance between the two people grow wider and wider. On the other hand, exploring and developing your own unique hobbies and interests may make your girlfriend more drawn to you. This is actually a process of mutual respect and mutual support. I believe you can do it.

But I always feel like she’s keeping a certain distance from me. I don’t know how to understand what she’s thinking, and I don’t know how to start communicating with her. I’m afraid that as soon as I say something, I’ll make her angry.

If you feel there’s a sense of distance between her and you, you can try giving her a little time and space to discover her own interests and hobbies. At the same time, you can also develop your own hobbies and interests. This can not only make you a more interesting person, but also leave her more time and space to think and develop her own interests. Doing this can also have a very positive effect on your relationship.

Thank you for your advice. I really do need to try handling our relationship more in this way. But in the process, I’ll still feel very nervous. I’m afraid I’ll do something wrong, and afraid I won’t do well enough.

That’s very normal. Everyone feels pressure and nervousness when they’re in a relationship. You can try taking deep breaths, relaxing your body and mind, and giving yourself more emotional support and encouragement. Remind yourself that even if it doesn’t work out, it’s not something terrifying. I believe you’ll become more confident, and that confidence will come through in how you act with your girlfriend, making her admire you more and want to be with you more.

This really is a good suggestion. I do need to find my confidence and handle our relationship more positively, because I really don’t want to lose her. Also, I want to ask: how should I go about understanding her feelings and thoughts?

That’s a very good question. Actually, understanding the other person’s feelings and thoughts is more of a skill in learning and communication. You can take the initiative to ask her, and express your understanding and care to her, so she can feel that the interaction and communication between you two isn’t one-sided. At the same time, you can also try observing her words and actions, and from those, get a sense of what she may be feeling inside. In this process, you need to notice that sometimes the effectiveness of communication doesn’t depend on how much you say, but on how you listen to what she says. Thank you for your question. I believe you will definitely make progress in this area.
Thank you for your answer and suggestions. I’ll try to do these things. I hope I can handle our relationship better, and I also hope she and I can understand and support each other more.

I believe you can succeed! You’re already looking for ways to solve the problem, and that in itself is part of your growth. Believe in yourself and believe in each other, and you will become happier. In this world, there will always be someone waiting for your arrival.
My girlfriend is very close with someone in her dorm, but lately that person often argues with my girlfriend and gets angry over little things. What should she do?
First, your girlfriend should find a firm place within herself, be clear about her own likes and boundaries, and not completely go along with other people’s thoughts and expectations.
But she feels like maybe she’s becoming selfish, and she doesn’t want to lose her friend.

From what you’ve described, she hasn’t really become selfish; she’s adapting to a new situation. The difference between friendship and romantic love can be subtle, but it’s not impossible to balance. Encourage her to think carefully again about her own needs and values.
But she feels misunderstood by others, and conflicts still keep coming up.
Some misunderstandings are hard to avoid. But as long as she communicates honestly with her friend and explains her attitude and thoughts, the situation can ease.
How can I help her?

You can offer support and help when she needs it, and encourage her to stick with her own choices. But you also need to keep a good sense of your own boundaries and not get overly involved in her matters.
There’s another issue. Lately she’s really cared about what others think of her, and she doesn’t know how to get rid of this anxiety.

Everyone has anxiety to varying degrees, and there’s no need to deliberately try to eliminate it. But she can use some methods, like deep breathing and practicing meditation, to regulate her emotions and ease the anxiety.
Okay, I’ll talk with her. Thank you for your advice.
You’re welcome. I hope things go smoothly for you both.

I started counseling in 2020. Last year, my depression of ten years recovered, but now I suddenly realize that the depression came from the loneliness that had built up, accumulated, been suppressed, and feared inside me since I was little. There’s an emptiness inside me.

Hello, I really admire your courage in exploring deep inside yourself, in discovering your own loneliness, and in bravely using counseling to heal from depression. You’ve already taken a solid step forward. Let’s give you some recognition for that together.
Thank you for your praise, but my loneliness really runs too deep. I feel very helpless.

I can understand how you feel. You’ve been experiencing a kind of loneliness similar to “existential loneliness”—deep, intense, and helpless. But please believe that you are not alone. People like you, who dare to face their inner struggles, are not so easily isolated. You could explore Irvin Yalom’s book Existential Psychotherapy, or take part in individual counseling to help yourself move out of the distress of loneliness.
I’m still very worried. Even though I’m trying so hard, I don’t know whether I can overcome loneliness.

Don’t lose confidence in yourself. Loneliness isn’t something sinister, and it isn’t unbeatable. We need to get close to ourselves and search for our true existence. It may take a lot of time and energy, but the process of thinking itself is already a kind of release, a kind of relief.
I just feel that it’s really hard to keep facing loneliness all the time.

That’s very normal. Loneliness is a normal human feeling. If you’re able to look at loneliness in a more positive way, your emotions will also be positively affected. When you get caught in negative emotions, you might try going for a walk, exercising, or listening to some music. This can help regulate your emotions a bit and help you feel more relaxed.
What you said makes a lot of sense. I’ll try it.

Good. I believe you’ll definitely be able to make progress. At the same time, you can also communicate more with the people around you and make more good friends in your life. That can also ease your loneliness.
Thank you for your suggestions. I’ll really try.
You’re welcome. I’ll continue to be here with you and support you through each part of the journey. If you run into any problems, you can come to me anytime to talk.
Thank you for your support. I’ll remember that.
I hope you can move through a period filled with love and support, and become a stronger, more self-aware person.

In 2018, I was diagnosed with bipolar disorder and depression. I’ve been through counseling, dropped out of high school, and I’m still taking medication now. Lately I haven’t really had any thoughts about the future. I just don’t know how to keep living, and I don’t know whether I like the traditional Chinese medicine I’m studying now.

Hearing what you’ve said, I deeply feel that your illness is not your fault, and it does not in any way affect the value of your self-understanding or your personality. You may be feeling helpless right now, and that helplessness comes from the unfair and unequal treatment your mother once experienced, while you were unable to help her. The fact that you want to study hard and work hard is enough to show that you have a loving heart and want to protect yourself and your family. But your uncle wouldn’t let you go to school, which disrupted your hopes, and that has left you feeling extremely unsettled. Actually, on the road of life, we all need to be recognized and affirmed. This is a normal part of growing as an independent person. The story behind your tears may be a kind of guilt, feeling that it was all your fault, and that only makes you feel even more helpless and discouraged.

I remember when I was little, I saw my mom being surrounded and beaten by a group of men at the entrance to our home. It was at night, and only my aunt went up to try to stop them, but it didn’t help at all. After going through these things, I swore in my heart that I would protect my mom for the rest of my life. So everything that happened afterward came from that childhood shadow. To help my mom make a better life, I did everything I could to study hard and bring her honor. Every time I heard my parents arguing, I would cry too. I’m 22 now, and it isn’t easy to find the meaning of life. I don’t really have any thoughts about the future either.

What I need to tell you is that you’ve had it very hard, and all of your pain and helplessness were not caused by you. Your experiences may make you feel sad and helpless, but they do not affect your determination and will to accept yourself. You can’t keep letting the pain of the past decide your future and your life. Instead, you need to have the courage to face challenges, accept your imperfections, explore your future, and create new value in your life.

Every time I think about going to school, I feel scared, but I also really want to study because I miss my old classmates. My uncle is a pretty authoritative person. He wants me to study traditional Chinese medicine, but I also want to resist and decide my own future direction. What should I do?

Actually, your heart has already given you the answer. What you truly want is to go to school, gain knowledge, and fulfill your own dreams. Traditional Chinese medicine is your uncle’s idea, and it may not be the direction that suits you best. You have your own thoughts and choices. Your choices may meet setbacks and bring certain difficulties, but that will never affect your value or the wonderful ways you can grow. As for your family issues, I’ve just reminded you that you need to have the courage to love yourself and this world.
Mm, I understand. Thank you for helping me see things more clearly.

Actually, helping you see things more clearly is not only my responsibility; it is also key for you to analyze problems rationally yourself. We all need to give ourselves a chance to face the things we fear. On the road of life, we may encounter all kinds of difficulties and challenges, but we need to hold on to our own ideas and use our strengths to overcome difficulties.
Mm, you’re right. I still have some things I’m not sure about...
Please tell me. I’d be very willing to talk with you and explore them together.
I feel like my mood has been pretty low lately, and I don’t know what’s going on.
That’s a good question. What are some things in your life that make you feel happy and pleased?
I like singing and drawing, but I always feel like I don’t sing well or that my drawings aren’t quite good enough.

If singing and drawing can make you feel happy and pleased, then why give up these hobbies? You can continue to develop these interests, while also recognizing your shortcomings and the room you have to improve. We all need a little bit of courage to face our imperfections, and then we can discover where our true value lies.
I think I can pick these hobbies back up. Thank you for your advice.

First, you need to learn to view yourself with a positive mindset, and at the same time understand the strengths and talents you have on your path of growth. Your childhood trauma has made you feel confused and helpless, but it has also trained in you a strong, unyielding quality and the belief to bravely take a step forward. Give yourself a positive and warm mindset. I hope that in your future life, you can find true happiness and meaning.
Thank you for your help. I’ll work hard and walk my own path seriously.
May you face challenges in your future life, overcome difficulties, and create value and meaning that belong to you. Hang in there!

I finally found someone I like, but now I have to transfer schools. I signed up for a few summer prep classes for the two months of summer break, and two of them conflict. One is the class the person I like is in, but the other teacher is really good. What should I do?
It sounds like you’re feeling really torn. So, do you feel that studying or the person you like is more important?
I want both, but I can only choose one. It’s so hard to decide!
I understand how you feel. After all, both are important. But if you can’t have the best of both worlds, you need to decide which one matters more for your future.
But if I don’t choose the class with the teacher who teaches well, I’ll really regret it.

Yes, sometimes making decisions is just that hard. Still, you can try looking at this from a longer-term perspective. What you need is a better future, and that means you may have to make some compromises. So, which choice do you feel would ultimately benefit you more?
I think studying is probably more important.

That decision sounds like it’s based on what you need for your future, and that’s a very good choice. But what if you clearly share your thoughts with the person you like now? Maybe the two of you can work through this together.
I understand. I can try communicating with him about it.
That’s right. Having a good conversation with him is also a very good choice. This may bring you closer, and I believe you can find a solution together.
Thank you. I feel much better now, and I’ll try to work this out.
I’m glad to hear that. You’ve made a very wise choice. Whatever you choose, I believe your future will be bright. Good luck!

I’d like to seek some mental health support from you. I divorced my ex-husband, whom I had been in a relationship with for 12 years. The gap between us was too big to maintain the marriage, so we separated peacefully. I don’t feel much attachment to that relationship. After the divorce, I started a new relationship with an online friend, A, whom I had known for 8 years. I was the one who brought it up. A said he had liked me for a long time. Actually, I liked him a lot too; it’s just that because I had a boyfriend, I had always treated him as a friend.

I really appreciate that you’re able to express your feelings, and that when facing your past relationship and a new partner, you made your own choice. You’ve done very well in that regard. May I ask what is troubling you now?

My ex-boyfriend is already in the past, but the relationship between A and me changed very quickly, and we started a long period of long-distance dating. I began to worry that this might bring some risks to my life.

Long-distance relationships often bring a lot of inconvenience, but they can also bring many new possibilities. Still, your worries are understandable. If you have any thoughts or concerns, you can share them with me. I’ll offer help and support when you need it.

Yes. A is very motivated when it comes to looking for work, and he wants to develop his career in Japan. At first, I also promised to support him, but I’ve found that he still isn’t stable enough in some of his tendencies. I’m worried this will bring risks and affect my life.

Your concern comes from your sense of responsibility and your careful attention to risk. I think that’s a very wise judgment. Let’s think through this possibility together and see what solutions might reduce the risks and improve the situation.

Thank you for your support, but I have another concern now. A and his mother are very close, and both of his parents are in China. After being together for almost a year, we finally met in person. But after I went back, he actually brought up breaking up, saying it was because our family conditions weren’t good.

That’s really painful. Your reaction to this situation is very normal. You need some time to understand these feelings and deal with what happened. But A making a decision like this only shows that he may lack a responsible attitude and respect. You deserve better.
I tried to communicate with him, but he ignored me completely. He deleted all my contact information. This makes me feel hopeless and powerless.
I know this feels terrible. You can use this time to learn some skills related to managing emotions, and also think about some new options and approaches.
I’ve already learned a lot of psychology knowledge. Although I know how to cope, I’m always in a lot of pain inside. How can I recover as soon as possible?

The pace of emotional recovery varies from person to person. But you’ve already been doing well in healing this wound in your heart. You can look for pleasure and enjoyment in different ways, such as reading, joining social activities, and talking with friends. At the same time, remember to take good care of yourself: get more rest, exercise more, and enjoy the beautiful moments life brings you.
Your suggestions are really great. I’ll give them a try. Thank you for the help and support you’ve given me.
I’m always here to help you. Whenever you need me, I’ll be here to offer you support and help.
I feel like I don't know what my strengths are. It seems like I know a little bit of everything, but only a little, and I don't know what I'm really good at.
Mm, I understand how you feel. Sometimes it's hard for us to notice what we're good at, but that doesn't mean it isn't there.
So what do you think I should do?

Maybe you could try doing new things more often, like learning something new, challenging yourself to try work you're not familiar with, or taking part in volunteer activities. In that process, you may often discover interests and abilities you hadn't noticed before.
But I always feel really lost, and I don't know what I truly like.

That's normal. Doesn't everyone go through this kind of stage? Maybe you can start writing down things you're interested in or things you find meaningful, and look for where your enjoyment lies from there. Also, don't forget to give yourself time to discover and explore.
But I always end up feeling discouraged and unsure because of it.

That's a very normal feeling. You don't need to rush to find the answer, and you definitely don't need to put enormous pressure on yourself because of it. Just keep trying to look for the answer, and believe that one day you will find your own path.
Thank you so much for your encouragement. I'll try to take action.

You're welcome. Whenever you need help, you can come to me. Your journey is a long one, but compared with beating yourself down, accepting yourself and continuing to move forward is what we should be doing more.
I'll take good care of myself. Thank you!
No problem. I wish you all the best.
Lately I keep feeling very incapable, and whenever something comes up, I feel uncertain.
Hello! The state you're in right now is understandable, so try not to blame yourself too much. Being able to notice your own difficulties is a very good first step.
But I feel like I can’t do any job well.

You don’t need to be too negative; your way of thinking needs some readjusting. You can think back to times when you succeeded before, and see whether there are skills and knowledge you can continue to build on.
I feel like I really lack leadership and interpersonal skills.

It’s good that you’ve identified your weaknesses. Now, making a plan to gradually make up for these areas will definitely help with your work. Learn leadership and interpersonal skills, and try to put them into practice at work.
I seem to always hold back and hesitate, and I don’t dare try difficult tasks.

Let yourself become more positive and confident. You can take part in some suitable training and activities to improve your skills and confidence. Believe in yourself, and as you keep trying more, you’ll improve, and slowly you’ll be able to overcome difficult tasks.
But I’m always afraid of other people seeing me fail.

Don’t give up on yourself. Learn to accept failure, because trying always comes with risks. How others see you isn’t important; what matters is that you’re doing what you believe is right. Keep going, and you’ll definitely be able to overcome this difficulty.
Sometimes I feel very numb, like I don’t have any feelings.

This is also quite common. You can try looking for things that feel meaningful to you to motivate yourself. For example, taking part in volunteer activities, running, chatting with friends, and so on. At the same time, pay attention to your body and your rest, and maintain good living habits.
Thank you for your advice. I’ll definitely try hard to put it into practice.
I’m very glad I could help you. Remember to keep a strong sense of belief, trust yourself, and know that we’re all here by your side supporting you. You’ve got this!
My child is 10 years old, a boy. His mother and I divorced when he was a little over one year old. I’ve been raising him on my own ever since, and we live with my parents.
It hasn’t been easy for you. You’ve taken on a lot, but you’re not alone. We’ll walk alongside you.
When we first divorced, my ex-wife would come see the child once a week. Later it became once a month, and then gradually she stopped seeing him and stopped calling too.

This is not your fault. You already gave your ex-wife the opportunities she needed to have contact with him, but she wasn’t able to make good use of them. We can work on not staying angry with her, while also being clear that she is no longer the most important person in your lives.
I once asked my ex-wife to take the child to see her, but she always made excuses.
You can stop calling or texting her to ask when the child can go see her. You can record your child’s experiences and growth on a calendar, or keep the notes and essays he writes for you.
My child and I often talk, and I ask him whether he misses his mom. But he says he doesn’t, and even seems a little resentful.

This is very normal. His psychological trauma may be very hard to fully heal. Try doing some other things too, such as taking him to a professional counseling center and letting a professional clinician talk with him.

Recently I saw an assignment he wrote at school. The title was “My Wish About My Mom.” In it, he wrote that he really wants to live with his mother, especially when he sees other classmates’ moms often coming to pick them up. That makes him miss her even more.

This is exactly when he needs you. You can tell him that his life now is better than before, and that he is living with family now. Every child has a mother and a father; it’s just that his mother is not by his side. Let him know that he is still deeply loved and cared for by everyone.
Can doing this really ease his pain?

It may not fully ease his pain, but your support, and giving him everyone’s love and care, can protect him from being hurt further. We suggest that you seek professional help, such as a counselor, psychotherapist, and so on.
Okay, thank you very much for your opinions and suggestions!
I’m glad to help. Remember, you are not alone. We are all here to help you and your child come out from under this shadow and move toward the future.

I’m 36 this year, and I have a 7-year-old son. I want to have a second child, but when I talked to my son about it, he cried really hard and said no. He said he would cry and break toys. How should I handle this?

Hello! Your child’s reaction has left you feeling confused and uneasy, and that’s very normal. Having a second child is a major decision, but your son’s feelings are something we need to take even more seriously. Would you be able to set aside the idea of having a second child for now, and first focus on your son’s emotions and needs?
I want to find my son a little companion, so they can keep each other company in the future. I also feel that having another child could grow up alongside him.

That’s a good thought! But having a second child isn’t the best choice for every family, because it involves many factors, such as finances, capacity, responsibility, and so on. In the end, whether or not to have a second child depends on your own wishes and needs. You need to think it through carefully, and your son’s opinion should also be one of the important factors to consider.
I’m worried that a new child would affect the stability of our whole family, especially my son. How would he react?

After the baby is born, there will be a period of adjustment. You’ll need to give your son enough time to understand and adapt to this change. You can communicate with him more, understand his feelings and thoughts, and at the same time let him know that you will always be there with him, and that no matter what happens, you won’t abandon him.
But my husband doesn’t really care that much about the child’s emotions. He thinks that as long as the baby is born, they’ll end up liking each other.

I understand. Everyone has different views on children’s growth, but children’s emotions and needs cannot be ignored. You can have a good conversation with your husband, tell him your worries and thoughts, and help him also pay attention to changes in your child’s emotions.
I’m really afraid that having another child will have a bad impact on the family and affect our family harmony.

Having a child is a very wonderful thing, but at the same time, it also requires thorough preparation. You need to consider all aspects, including your family situation, financial capacity, and ability to raise children. If you do decide to have a second child, then you’ll need to face together all the issues that may come up in the future, and work to maintain harmony and stability in the family.
If I have another child, I’ll cherish them even more, but I’m afraid our current family conditions won’t be able to meet the needs of two children.

I really understand how you feel. When considering whether to have a second child, you need to take both real-life circumstances and personal needs into account. You can list out the practical situation and the possible impacts one by one, and make full preparations and plans, so you can make a better decision.
Thank you for your advice. I’ll think it through before making a decision.
I’m very glad that you’re able to think about this issue in an objective and rational way. Whatever you decide to do, we will always be here with you and support you. You’ve got this!

I graduated from junior college three years ago. I’m 25 this year, and I’ve had a mental health-related illness. I have to take medication for life, though the dose is very small. The side effect is that I’m a bit sleepy and tend to sleep too much. In 2017, I had just graduated with a major in accounting, and I worked as an accounting intern. In Beijing it was 3,000 yuan a month with housing included. I’m introverted, and I had a fear of interpersonal interactions from my original family. My mentor also didn’t want me to ask her questions. After three months, the company transferred me to a customer service position. Because of the impression my first job left on me, and the pressure from my supervisor, I did customer service for three months but the pressure was too much, so I quit again. Now, after having my child, I came to Beijing four months ago and went back to the same company, but on another project, working in reception. As someone who’s introverted and doesn’t react quickly, I’m finding it very hard. Seeing my 20-year-old younger coworkers, who only have a high school education but react quickly and are skilled, I feel really panicked and blame myself for being useless. My mom said when I go back for the New Year she’s going to beat me, because this year I’ve been going back and forth between Beijing and my hometown, and the travel costs have been a lot. My personality is indecisive, and I can never make up my mind. In my original family, my parents divorced when I was 1, and I was raised by my eldest aunt, and at one point my second aunt also raised me. My stability is especially poor, and it’s also very hard for me to stick with a job for long. I’ve spent over 1,000 yuan on counseling too, but it hasn’t solved my problems. My family also says I’m slow to react, like a fool, and that no boss would want me.

Hello! Reading your message, I feel really sorry for what you’ve been through. You were separated from your biological parents at such a young age and went through so many difficulties and grievances. I can really understand why you would feel inferior and introverted. In terms of work, you’ve already done quite well. You graduated from junior college and have experience as an accounting intern and in customer service, and that’s really something. Your family doesn’t support or understand you, and recently you’ve also been troubled by your personality and memory. These difficulties are making you feel very helpless, right?
That’s right. I want to find someone to talk to. I’ve already spent almost over 1,000 yuan on counseling.

I can understand how you feel. At times like this, it can help to think about doing things that regulate your emotions, such as enjoying music, reading, or exercising. When you feel troubled, seeking support from friends and relatives around you, or seeking help from a counselor, can also be helpful. So what is troubling you the most right now?
I feel like I’m very useless. I always drag things out when I do things, I can’t make decisions, and sometimes I also have memory problems.

Looking at it, this is a matter of how you see yourself. Sometimes we label ourselves, and that can make us feel very helpless. You’re actually not that useless. If we look at work and study separately, you do have quite a bit of work experience. And when it comes to making decisions, you can work on that through communication and asking others for advice. For memory difficulties, there are also many ways to help improve things, such as strengthening your memory in different ways, like keeping a diary or drawing mind maps. You can also do some stress-reducing activities, such as yoga or listening to relaxing music.
I’ll try my best.

Okay. I believe you will definitely find your own way to get through this difficult time. What you need now is to emphasize some positive and constructive role labels for yourself, and do things that make your life a little easier. These can both help regulate your emotions effectively and support your memory. If you need, I can recommend some resources and tools to help you do these things.
Okay, thank you very much for your support and encouragement.

There’s nothing to thank me for. We are all ordinary people, just using our own ways to help those who need it. If you feel that I can help you, contact me anytime. I’ll do whatever I can to help you make changes.

Lately, I feel like a lot of people, when they’re getting married, think, “This is love,” and that they have to be with that person. I think that’s really impulsive, and many people ignore their parents’ objections, but the outcome doesn’t turn out well.

Hello. Hearing your concern, I want to say that sometimes people really do tend to make impulsive decisions when it comes to love. That’s very normal. But when we make this decision, we often forget the advice and reminders from people around us, and even ignore our own inner voice. That can be very risky.
Yeah, I feel like too many people act impulsively because of feelings and don’t think about the consequences.

Yes, because love can easily make us overlook real-life considerations and make us become blind and impulsive. But we need to know that ignoring the consequences will only end up hurting us. So we need to calm down a bit, think through the consequences of each decision, and then make a decision.
But sometimes I feel like I can’t control my emotions. What should I do?

I understand how you feel. But we need to know that controlling emotions is an ability that takes practice to develop. We can help ourselves manage our emotions by giving ourselves some buffer time, calming down, and analyzing the situation rationally.
Then how should I find the right person to marry?

Good question! What’s important is that we need to slowly get to know the other person and determine whether they share our values. At the same time, we need to consider whether they are suitable for us, so that we can choose a marriage partner who is more likely to bring us happiness.
But I feel like my family never trusts my choices, and that makes me very sad.

This is indeed a very difficult issue. But no matter what, we need to see the other person’s strengths and weaknesses, and then evaluate them. If your parents don’t support your choice, you can try to resolve the issue through communication. If communication doesn’t work, then we need to be more firm in our decision and be prepared to take responsibility for the consequences it brings.
Thank you for your advice. I’ll think it over carefully.
You’re welcome. I’m glad I could help you. If there’s anything you need help with, feel free to contact me anytime. I wish you happiness!

My little nephew is nine now, and my child is three and a half. The environment both of these children grew up in after they were born was really awful. Before they were even one, their parents divorced. Family members often scared them, hit and scolded them when they were so little, ignored them, disliked them, forced them, controlled them... and so on. The adults’ own ignorance, incompetence, helplessness, fear, and anxiety were taken out on the children. Those kinds of hurts are things even adults couldn’t bear, yet they were put onto very young children. Just thinking about it feels like being pricked by thorns. Now my little nephew is nine, and earlier on he was already showing some personality issues. I’m very worried, and I sincerely want to ask: trauma from infancy, early childhood, and childhood is almost impossible to get past, right? I’m worried about these two children, but I myself don’t have the ability to do much.

I completely understand your worry. No matter what kinds of difficulties and pain we go through, we can’t let them stop us from moving forward. Please first try to relax a little, take some deeper breaths, and notice the present moment.
Okay, I tried to relax a little. But I’m still worried about my nephew’s problems.

I know this is hard. But we can take it step by step. First, we want to let them know they are welcomed and needed. Try to see them in a positive light, support their interests and hobbies, and help them build self-esteem and confidence.
I can understand that. But I’m still worried that their trauma will affect their future.

Yes, that’s also a very real concern. But don’t forget, we can also help them plan for a future full of hope. Let them experience good things as much as possible, and work with experienced professionals to make sure their development fits their needs and abilities.
That sounds good. Do you have any specific suggestions?

Of course. I’d first suggest looking for some reliable support organizations to help you explore different skills and resources. Also, you can look into some related therapy courses or alternative therapies to help them ease stress and anxiety.
Okay, I’ll try. Thank you so much for your care and suggestions.
You’re welcome. We’ll work on this together. Lastly, remember not to overlook your own needs and mental health; that’s also an important step in helping them. Wishing you all the best!
I feel inferior because of my appearance, and I want a divorce, but I’m also afraid of being criticized.

Hello, I can understand how you feel. I’ve also experienced this kind of psychological pressure before and didn’t know how to cope with it. But we need to try to find our true value and what we’re really pursuing beyond other people’s judgments and expectations. Because our worth shouldn’t revolve only around appearance; it comes from our inner qualities, talents, and personal character.
But my husband cares a lot about appearance, and I always feel like I’m not good enough.

I understand your worries and fear. But we shouldn’t fix ourselves around other people’s expectations and standards. You can try to set aside the factors that affect your confidence and recognize your own strengths and potential. Only when you believe in yourself can you truly find where you stand and work through your inner conflicts and difficulties.
But I seem to always feel like I’m not good enough, and that other people definitely won’t think much of me.

I understand your distress and lack of confidence. But we need to learn to accept and respect ourselves, and find what is unique and valuable about us. Because everyone has their own strengths and shortcomings, and the key is whether we’re willing to acknowledge them and use them as motivation to strive and grow.
How can I strengthen my confidence?

On the one hand, we can expose ourselves more to things that can inspire confidence, such as reading, traveling, exercise, and so on, and develop our interests, hobbies, and skills. On the other hand, we can communicate more with the people around us, listen to their suggestions and feedback, and from that discover our blind spots and shortcomings, then make timely adjustments and improvements. In this way, we can face life and challenges with a more positive and proactive attitude and mindset.
I also want to do better, but I always feel like I have limitations.

We shouldn’t give up on our ideals and efforts just because of temporary difficulties and limitations. On the contrary, we should have the courage to challenge ourselves, keep making progress, and actively broaden our horizons and abilities. Everyone has their own blueprint and dreams. As long as we have faith and perseverance, we can definitely realize our own value and achievements.
Thank you for your support and encouragement. I’ll work hard.
You’re welcome. When you need it, I’ll always be by your side supporting you. Believe in yourself, believe in the future, and let’s face new challenges and growth together.
Lately, whenever I’m in a crowded place, I get scared. I feel nervous, I sweat, and sometimes I don’t even want to talk. What should I do?
It sounds like you may be experiencing social anxiety disorder. But don’t worry—this is something that can absolutely be treated and overcome.
Really? Are there ways to treat it?
Mm, first, you could consider consulting with and getting treatment from a mental health professional. Also, trying some relaxation exercises may help ease the symptoms.
I’m still a bit hesitant about professional treatment right now. Are there any self-regulation methods that could help me reduce the symptoms?

Of course. You can try deep breathing or meditation exercises to reduce the feeling of anxiety. Also, slowly increase the amount of time and the frequency with which you face crowds, and gradually help yourself get used to social situations.
Thank you for your suggestions. But every time I feel too nervous, I always start having negative thoughts.
That’s very common. Try not to be so hard on yourself anymore. If you feel uncomfortable, you can talk openly with people around you, or release some pressure through things like journaling.
Okay, I’ll try to take your suggestions.
Very good. Remember not to let yourself get too tense or worried, and work through it step by step. If you need it, I’ll always be here to support you.
I’ve worked at this company for five years, but after being promoted three times, I still haven’t achieved any of my goals.

Hearing you talk about this, I can really understand that you feel deeply exploited at the company, while your manager keeps pushing you, making you feel like you’ve fallen into a deep pit. It’s possible that you have some dependence on and need for this boss, so you follow his orders closely, but your negative emotions are also hard to avoid. I’d suggest becoming more aware of your emotions, noticing the state you’re in, and also seeking help from a professional counselor to better support your planning.
I’m really tired of this job now. At this company, I feel like I’m constantly being forced to do things I don’t want to do. What should I do?

Hearing you say this, I can really understand that your current job has left you feeling very exhausted and deeply hurt. If you keep feeling forced to do things you don’t like, then you need to clarify your own values and preferences, and then look for a job that suits you better. At the same time, you can also learn and improve your abilities so that you have more choices. Also, try to understand your emotions, and don’t let negative feelings affect your decisions.
But I can’t just casually quit like someone with nothing to worry about, and I can’t quickly find a new job either. This makes me really irritated.

I understand your concerns, but you can make a plan in advance, such as choosing the right timing to resign, while also leaving enough time to look for a new job that suits you. During this period, you can adjust yourself, relax your mind, and also try out different industries more, broadening your career perspective. This can be very helpful for your future employment as well.
I’m under a lot of mental pressure at the company. The pressure is too much, and inside I feel very restless. Are there any treatment methods?

I understand that you’re under a lot of mental pressure, and this is also something many people in the workplace have to face. I’d suggest that you try some psychological treatment methods to relieve this pressure, such as self-guided meditation, yoga, body relaxation training, physical exercise, and so on. These methods can help you regulate your emotions and find balance. Of course, if the symptoms are more serious, you can seek help from a professional counselor.
But I feel like my abilities are limited. How can I improve my self-confidence?

I really understand how you feel, and I also know this situation is very common. But your abilities can actually be improved and changed. You can put more effort into your work, and of course you can also study and explore more, continuing to improve yourself. At the same time, pay attention to your emotions and avoid letting negative feelings affect your self-confidence. I’d suggest looking for some training or coaching, and also taking part in more activities you’re interested in, to build your confidence and experience.
I also want to ask, how can I keep my emotions stable?

Emotional stability is something we really need in work, life, and study, but we’re often affected by different factors, such as pressure at work, conflicts in relationships, and so on. Actually, the main way to keep your emotions stable is to pay attention to your emotions—for example, don’t let certain things trouble you for too long, express your emotions appropriately, find some things to do that you enjoy, and so on. You can also use methods like stretching and meditation to ease tense emotions.
But right now I feel very lost, and sometimes it’s hard to tell what I’m feeling. What can I do to understand myself more clearly?

When we’re in difficult and oppressive situations, listening to our inner self can be very helpful. I’d suggest trying some self-reflection methods, such as writing a journal or talking to someone. These can help your emotions and feelings become clearer, which is very important for better planning and managing yourself in the future. At the same time, you can also talk with friends and family, communicate more and observe more, and understand your strengths, weaknesses, and the areas you feel passionate about. That way, you can come to know yourself more clearly.
Lately I’ve been arguing with my best friend a lot. It feels like the friendship we had before is already gone.
Hi, I understand how you feel. Try asking yourself, what have these arguments been about?

We used to have cold wars a lot, and that distance really can’t go away anymore. After graduation, she suddenly said she thought another close friend was disgusting, just because they had a disagreement over a tiny interest or hobby. They were clearly pretty good before, and seeing that made me feel kind of chilled. Later I felt like we didn’t really get along in a lot of ways, so I deleted her.

This made you feel very uncomfortable, and it made you start to doubt whether the friendship between you and your best friend was real. At the same time, we also need to look at things from different angles. It’s possible that her dislike of the other friend wasn’t only because of different interests or hobbies, and that there were other factors too.
But now I feel like she and I are getting more and more distant. Sometimes I even feel like she’s saying bad things about me behind my back.

That’s a situation that can feel really discouraging and helpless. You could try communicating with her directly and understanding her thoughts and feelings. At the same time, don’t blame yourself, because everyone has their own feelings and ways of thinking.
I’ve tried communicating with her, but she always doesn’t want to listen to me. I feel really confused now and don’t know what to do.

This really is hard to deal with. But you could try communicating in a different way, letting her fully express her thoughts and letting her know that you care about her too. At the same time, we also need to understand that everyone has emotional ups and downs, and sometimes they may do things that don’t really make sense. That doesn’t mean she doesn’t care about you.
Yeah, I also hope our friendship can continue. But I still really care about some of the arguments from before. How can I let go of the unhappiness in my heart?

This is a process that takes time to work through. You could try learning some ways to handle emotions, such as self-reflection and self-soothing. At the same time, don’t be too harsh on yourself for how you feel, because emotions can slowly adjust and find balance.
Thank you for your advice. I feel now that letting go of the unhappiness in my heart will make things feel a bit easier.
You’re welcome. I’m always here with you. If you need any help or support, feel free to come talk with me anytime. Let’s keep a positive mindset together and find our real friendship again.
Okay, I’ll try. Thank you again for your support and encouragement!
You’re welcome. Everything will get better. Hang in there!

I look very ordinary. When I was little, my parents called me ugly, and when I didn’t do things well, they called me stupid. My grandma favored boys over girls. I have really low self-esteem. When people talk to me, I pay too much attention to changes in their expressions and tone, and I’m afraid they’ll think I’m ugly and boring, so I try really hard to be funny and please them. When people compliment me, I feel like they’re mocking me. I care a lot about what other people think. No matter how hard I work at school, the teachers don’t notice me. I feel like no matter how well I do on exams, I still can’t compare to people who are good-looking. I break down really easily, and I can’t find anyone to talk to. I feel a lot of guilt, like no one understands me, and I think about dying. I want to be needed, I want to be noticed, I want to feel like I exist. It hurts so much.

I know you’re feeling very sad right now, but that doesn’t mean you don’t have value. I think what you’re dealing with has to do with your sense of self-worth, which is a core part of everyone’s inner world. Because of the negative experiences and family environment you had in the past, your sense of worth may not have been built up well. This will take time and effort to improve. If circumstances allow, I’d suggest considering seeking help from a counselor. If you want to try on your own, I have a book to recommend: Families and How to Survive Them: A New Opportunity for Self-Renewal. It’s a work on positive psychology by Seligman, and it may be helpful to you. Lastly, I wish you good luck, and I hope you can get through this difficult time and regain your confidence.

At school I always get nervous for no reason. I feel really nervous when someone sits next to me, and I can’t stop myself from paying attention to it. Once I get nervous, I easily get headaches, and they hurt a lot. If I don’t eat, my blood sugar gets low, and I also feel nauseous and dry heave. My throat feels like it’s blocked. Personally, I think I’m a pessimistic person. I’m not interested in anything. I feel like studying is really painful, but I still have to force myself to do practice problems. Every day feels very painful.

Hearing your description, I can sense the unease and anxiety you’re feeling about your current situation. But please believe that you are not alone; we all go through emotional ups and downs like this. What you need is to accept your unease and anxiety, and also try to regulate your emotions in appropriate ways. Sometimes, simply having a good talk with someone can bring some relief inside. You could try telling some trusted friends or family members how you feel. They would be willing to listen to you. This can also help you find some good solutions and suggestions.

Mm, sometimes I really do need someone to share my feelings with me. But I always feel like my emotions should be dealt with only by myself. And the pressure at school is really heavy. I don’t know how to deal with the pain of studying.

This kind of thought isn’t unusual. Many people have this kind of emotional experience. But sometimes, what we may need is not to bear all the emotions and pressure alone, but to seek outside support and help. The pain you feel around studying may show that you need some extra help. You can try working together with teachers or classmates, and share your views and strategies about studying with each other. This can help address the pain you feel about studying, and it can also strengthen your connection with your classmates.
That sounds a little doable. But I’m still really worried about my physical condition. I often feel very nervous, and this will affect my health.

I understand. Our bodies and minds are closely connected. For many people, when they experience psychological stress, their body’s resistance can also go down, and all kinds of discomfort can show up. I’d suggest that you try to accept your body’s reactions, and also make some appropriate adjustments in your daily life, such as scheduling more than 30 minutes of exercise every day, or trying some meditation and breathing techniques to improve your physical and mental state. These methods don’t require too much time or space, and they can effectively improve your physical discomfort and emotional state.
These methods sound pretty good. I’ll try to do them. But I still feel like I’m too pessimistic, and I don’t have confidence in my future either.

You may not realize that you’ve already taken the first step in seeking help, and that is really great. Everyone encounters difficulties and setbacks in life, but belief and hope can help us get through hard times. I’d suggest that you find some time and space to think about what you’re truly interested in and the goals you want to pursue, and then make some action plans to achieve them. No matter what your future looks like, we are here to work together with you, supporting and encouraging you toward a better future.
Thank you for your suggestions and reminders. I’ll take action the way you said, and I’ll also remember to share my feelings with people I trust and seek help and support from them.

I’m very glad to hear you say that. I hope that through our conversation, you can gradually accept your inner self and see the more positive side of yourself. I also hope you can firmly believe that every process of learning and growth is worth cherishing. If you face difficulties or setbacks, don’t be afraid to ask others for help. We are all here, supporting and encouraging you as you become a better version of yourself.

I've been feeling troubled lately. When I see someone of the opposite sex, I often have some unreasonable thoughts and urges, and I even bring coworkers into my imagination. I feel very guilty. What's going on?

I understand your confusion. First, I want to tell you that this falls within the normal range of human sexual behavior. But if it is causing strong negative emotions or behaviors, then it may need some further adjustment. For now, try not to blame yourself or judge yourself.
But I really don't want to have these thoughts. Could it be that I'm just not mature enough?
This doesn't mean you're not mature enough, or that you have a moral problem. It may be influenced by your brain's biology and social factors. Now let's look at how to cope with it.
Okay, please support me.

First, you need to recognize that “thoughts are not actions.” This is a key idea Dr. Jeffrey Schwartz has mentioned in treating obsessive-compulsive disorder. If you have thoughts that don't align with moral standards, you should immediately call a stop to them and reattribute them.
I understand. When I have unreasonable thoughts, I need to remind myself of this.

Yes, that can help you build a new understanding of yourself. Second, you need to shift your attention and do other things that are meaningful and have a positive impact on you. This helps interrupt the brain circuits of unhelpful thoughts. Finally, don't forget to give yourself positive feedback. You haven't acted on these thoughts, and you haven't hurt anyone. That is something worth acknowledging.
Thank you for your suggestions. I'll try to put them into practice.
You are very brave, and you are not alone. When we feel confused, we all need to support each other. If you need further help, you can seek support from a psychologist or a professional organization.
Lately I always feel so, so tired. I don’t want to push myself, I don’t want to strive for anything. I just want to lie down and do nothing. Why is that? Is what I’m going through normal?

Yes, many people have been through this. It may be that you’ve been too exhausted recently, and both your body and mind need rest. But it’s also worth knowing that without a reasonable amount of effort, people can easily lose their sense of direction and motivation.
But right now I don’t have any motivation at all. Every day at work feels especially boring.

When a person works hard, it’s because they’ve seen that fire. That fire isn’t something you get by having someone whipping you from behind with an ox whip, strike after strike, forcing you to work hard. It’s a need that truly comes from within you. If you don’t move toward it, you feel awful, like life is worse than death—for example, desire, passion. Until that moment comes, you won’t be able to get moving.
But right now I feel like nothing has passion or meaning.

If you’re anxious about not working hard, that shows you still want to do something. So whatever you want to do, go do that. If it’s not necessary, don’t force yourself to work hard just for the sake of forcing yourself, and you don’t need to deceive yourself into working hard. Because effort usually isn’t the purpose of what we do; it’s a way to achieve success.
Yeah, I can try out areas I’m interested in, and go learn and practice.

Exactly. Only when you’re truly doing your own thing can you feel inner satisfaction and a sense of achievement. You don’t need to feel anxious and regretful about not working hard. Get moving—just do it!
But what if I try for a while and still don’t have any interest or motivation?

That’s okay. People’s interests and passions change as they grow and go through different experiences. If this still isn’t your path right now, don’t lose heart. Keep exploring, and maybe in the future you’ll find an area that suits you better.
Thank you for your support and understanding. I feel much more at ease now.
You’re welcome. We all have low points, and we need to support and encourage each other. Remember to take good care of yourself, and don’t let your emotions affect your life and work.
Recently, because of work, I need to live in another city for a while. It just so happens that the older guy I used to really like has settled in this city.
Hearing that you’re facing this kind of situation, I can really understand how you feel. I’m wondering what you’re feeling right now?

I’d thought many times before about coming to see him, but I never had the chance, and I didn’t have the courage. This time I asked him in advance to have dinner, but it still hasn’t happened, because I’ve been struggling with whether or not to see him.

This really is a complex issue. You can take more time to think through this decision, ask yourself whether you truly want to see him, and also consider the possible impact and consequences in the future.

We haven’t seen each other for 10 years, but all these years I’ve never forgotten him. He’s like a piece of white moonlight to me. When life feels helpless and hopeless, every time I think of him, I feel like life isn’t that bad.

It’s very clear that he holds a special place in your heart, and that place may not change for a very long time. But if you decide to meet him, you may need more courage and determination to face the feelings between you and him, and your own feelings as well.
Back then, I really, really, really liked him, but I didn’t have the courage to confess. I even, like an idiot, “rejected” his hints many times.

Perhaps the choice you made at the time was the most suitable one; after all, it also reflected a kind of decision within you. Whatever the decision was back then, in the end we all need to accept and face the choices we’ve made in our lives.

Back then, he held my hand, took me out to have fun, taught me how to swim, often called me... But he never said whether he liked me or not. He just treated me like a little girl. Later, because we were separated in different places for a long time, we gradually lost touch.

From what you’ve described, he did have a special emotional connection with you and paid special attention to you. But he never said he liked you, and we don’t know what he was thinking or feeling at the time. We can only respect his choice, and also respect our own marriages and families.
Now we both have our own families, and I’m even more unsure whether I should go see him, or whether I should tell him that I once liked him.

I believe you’ve already thought deeply about this question in your heart. Before making a decision, we need to understand our own inner needs and values, and also consider other people’s feelings and attitudes. No matter what choice you make, I will support your decision.

On the one hand, I don’t want to disturb his current life. On the other hand, I feel regret that my younger self didn’t have the courage, and I want to make up for that regret. I don’t know, if I miss this chance to meet, how many more years I’ll have to wait.

Sometimes, we have many thoughts and feelings inside, but the final choice still needs to depend on our own reasonable judgment and determination. You can feel proud of the choices you make for your own life, and remember that your decision comes from your own will and judgment.

Even though marriage is still a long way off for me, whenever I bring up marriage, I feel very scared and nervous. I’m afraid of losing my freedom after getting married, and I’m afraid of having children after marriage. I can’t imagine a little life calling me Mom. I don’t know why I feel so nervous.

Hello, it sounds like you’re feeling some distress and worry, and that’s very normal. You’re in an important stage of life right now, facing many choices and challenges. Let’s explore your worries about marriage together.
Okay. I feel like I don’t think about marriage and having children the way other girls do, and that makes me feel very anxious.

Everyone has different views on marriage and having children. These are important decisions in a person’s life, and before making them, we need to carefully consider our own thoughts and needs. Could you say more specifically what freedom means to you?
To me, freedom means being able to make my own choices freely. If I’m going to lose that freedom after getting married, I feel really afraid.

Marriage doesn’t necessarily mean losing freedom. On the contrary, married life can be very free and varied. You can talk with your partner about the lifestyle you both want. Marriage doesn’t mean everything has to change; it can be an expression of a deeper and more stable emotional relationship between you and your partner. Would you be able to express your need for freedom when communicating with your partner?
I’ll try to talk with him about it, but I’m still really worried it will change the relationship between us.

Communication is an important part of a stable and healthy relationship. If you’re able to communicate sincerely and make a decision you’re both satisfied with, it can help strengthen the feelings between you. You can share your thoughts and worries openly with your partner; maybe you’ll be surprised by how much he understands and supports your views and needs.
Maybe I’m overthinking it, but I really don’t want to lose my freedom after getting married.

It’s important to understand your thoughts and needs, but we also need to recognize that any decision we make, at any time, can come with uncertainty and different challenges. Giving up marriage and having children may make you feel safe and free, but it may also mean missing out on an important part of life experience and growth. We can explore together how to respond to the situations you’re worried about, and how to find a shared understanding about the future for you and your partner.
Thank you for your advice. I’ll try to face this issue together with my partner, and keep learning and growing.

Very good. I believe you’ll be able to find shared goals and a lifestyle that works for both of you. If you run into problems or difficulties again, feel free to come talk with me anytime. I hope you can keep a positive and optimistic mindset. Wishing you all the best!
Lately, I feel like my stress has been getting bigger and bigger.
Hearing you say that, I can understand how you’re feeling right now. Can you tell me more specifically what areas you’re feeling stressed about?
I’m under a lot of pressure at work, and I always feel like I’m not doing well enough. Also, some recent family issues have been really bothering me.

Hearing you say that, I can sense the difficulty you may be going through. Still, I also want to say that your work and family problems haven’t stopped you from seeking help, and that in itself is a very positive sign.
But I always feel anxious, like I’m not doing well enough. I’m really so tired.

Stress and anxiety are very common emotions. We all need to learn how to face and ease these feelings. I suggest you try some ways to relax your body and mind to ease the tension, such as physical relaxation exercises, listening to music, and so on.
Okay, I’ll give that a try. But sometimes I still feel low, even a little depressed.

If you feel the situation is ongoing and serious, I suggest you consult a professional physician or counselor as soon as possible. They can provide you with professional support and guidance, and help you better cope with different emotions and stress.
Thank you for your advice and concern. I’ll consider seeking professional help.

I’m glad I could help. If you need anything, you’re always welcome to contact me. Lastly, I want to remind you not to forget that you are not alone. Like you, everyone may experience emotional ups and downs.
I feel like I’m doing nothing, with no goals, and I don’t know what I should do.
It sounds like you’re feeling very confused. Would you like help or some suggestions?
Actually, I just don’t know what I want, and I feel really lost.
It’s very normal to feel this lost and uneasy. We can work together to find a way forward.
I always feel like I can’t finish tasks, and my anxiety is getting worse and worse.
Feeling anxious often while doing things is a very common issue. We can try to find some ways to ease that feeling.
I always feel like after working hard for a while, I lose interest.
Losing interest and trying to get out from under stress can be really hard. We can explore the activities you enjoy most; maybe that will help you find the motivation to come back to things.
But I don’t even know what I want to do.
Then we can think together about the things you like, and from there discover where your goals and motivation might be.
I always feel very anxious, and it’s hard to concentrate.
Anxiety can feel very oppressive. You can use methods like meditation and breathing exercises to help relax your mind.
I always feel like I have no meaning in this world.
That’s a very deep sense of worry. We can work together to find the real meaning in your life, and that may help you gain confidence from it.
But I feel like I can’t face my own emotions and awareness.
That’s a very normal feeling. But remember, talking about your feelings is a very important step. We can work together to find a safe person who can listen.
I feel very sad and lonely.
That’s a very heavy feeling, but I’ll be here with you, and we’ll look for ways together to ease the loneliness so you can face life better.
Thank you. Your support makes me feel very comfortable. I’ll take my emotions and happiness seriously.
I’m very glad I could contribute in some way. I hope you can always know that you are not alone, and that we can face life’s challenges together.

I have a problem. Ever since elementary school, I felt like my grades were around the lower-middle level. Then in middle school, I met a teacher who was very understanding. I worked really hard, but there were still some difficult problems I couldn’t figure out. Once, because I didn’t want to disappoint the teacher, I cheated using my phone. Even though I got first place in the class, I feel really stressed now and don’t know what to do.

Hello, after hearing what you’ve been through, I can understand how you feel. Cheating is definitely not the right choice, but I believe you did it with good intentions, wanting not to let down your teacher’s expectations. Now you’ve realized there’s a problem and are trying to find a way to address it, and that’s really worth acknowledging.
Yes, I really don’t know what to do. I don’t want to cheat again, but I also don’t want to disappoint my teacher or let my grades drop.

I understand the conflict you’re feeling, but one thing needs to be clear: you don’t need to deny your own achievements because of other people’s expectations. You can choose to tell your teacher the truth and ask for help, or you can review seriously on your own and stay up late before the exam to push yourself in preparing. Either way, it’s important to think through what consequences your actions may bring.
Thank you for your advice. I’ll think it over carefully. But I feel like my brain doesn’t work very well, and my study efficiency is really low. How can I improve it?

Everyone’s situation is different, but you can try some methods, such as adjusting your schedule, maintaining a good mindset, doing more practice, and thinking carefully. You can also ask your teacher or classmates for advice and seek their help and suggestions. Struggling during the learning process is very common, so don’t give up easily, and keep a positive, upward-looking attitude.

Thank you for your encouragement and advice. I’ll try to put it into practice. But I have another question: I always see failure as my own fault, and it’s hard for me to accept that kind of result. What should I do?

Accepting failure is difficult, but it’s also a necessary process. Failure can teach us to reflect on our shortcomings and remind us that we need to work harder to reach our goals. You can learn a lot from failure, and you need to believe in your potential to grow.
Thank you for your encouragement and support. I feel much better.
You’re welcome. If you need to talk with me, you can contact me anytime. Remember, you’re not fighting this battle alone. Finally, I hope you succeed!
Thank you for your help. I’ll keep going!
You’ve got this! I look forward to hearing good news from you.
I feel like my life right now has no hope at all.
I can understand how you're feeling right now. It's very normal to feel helpless and lost in your life.
But I still have some hopes for the future, and I feel like I can't give up.
Yes, that is part of your nature as a human being. We need some expectations and hope to encourage ourselves to keep moving forward.
But I feel like I have no control over the future. It feels like I've walked into darkness.
Sometimes in life, it's like we're moving through a pitch-dark tunnel, with a lot of sadness and difficulties along the way. But at the end of the tunnel, there will always be a little bit of light.
I'm also afraid I don't have enough courage to face the challenges in life.
Facing challenges takes courage and perseverance. But remember, you don't have to do everything all at once. We can move forward step by step, gradually working toward your goals.
I also feel like in my life, it's like I'm trapped in a circle.

When we're in a difficult situation, we need to think about ways to solve the problem, and we also need to talk with others. Sometimes, listening to other people's experiences can help us break out of a difficult situation.
I feel your support. Thank you.
I'm very glad I can support you. No matter what bumps lie ahead, believe that you have enough strength to get through them.

Learning to drive has been really painful lately. I practice every day, but I’m really doing badly. A female student who started around the same time is doing really well, and the instructor keeps praising her, while I get scolded really harshly. I feel like I’m so stupid. I’ve practiced so many times and still haven’t made any progress. I don’t know what to do. I feel hopeless, like I can’t accomplish anything in life.

First of all, a hug for you. Learning to drive isn’t easy, especially in the winter. Try not to overthink it. After all, everyone learns at a different pace and in different ways. Comparing yourself with others will only make you more anxious. Also, the instructor’s attitude doesn’t reflect your ability; that’s his mistake. You shouldn’t blame yourself or doubt yourself. The right approach is to stay calm first, believe in yourself, and then learn step by step. Everyone goes through a period of needing guidance. Your situation isn’t unique.
But I really can’t do it well. I’m just not making any progress at all.

Learning to drive takes time and patience, and you need to keep practicing hard each time. Don’t blame yourself too much. Everyone has times when they don’t do well. You should believe in yourself, listen carefully to the instructor’s guidance, and adjust the way you learn and take things in. If you feel you’re not doing well, reflect on what the issues are, find the reasons, and then keep going. You’ve got this.
But the instructor is always scolding me. Sometimes I don’t even want to learn anymore.

Your instructor’s attitude really isn’t good, but that doesn’t mean there’s a problem with your ability, and it shouldn’t stop you from continuing to learn. Try to approach his guidance in a more positive way, listen carefully to what he says, and try to understand his perspective. Try communicating with the instructor so he can understand you better, and try to get him to help you focus more. If you feel his attitude is really bad, you could talk with him privately or ask his supervisor to understand the situation more clearly.
I really feel hopeless. I feel like I’m no good at anything.

Don’t give up so easily. You’re not a failure. Believe in yourself and move toward success with a positive attitude. Sometimes you need to stop, get a good rest, and then readjust your thinking. Give yourself more time to think and reflect. Every time something doesn’t go well, it’s an opportunity to grow. Be brave and try!
Thank you, dear. You’re so kind.
Don’t thank me. This is just friends helping each other. We support each other.
I feel like it’s helping. After hearing what you said, I feel more confident.
That’s good. I’m really glad you feel that way. Please remember, I’ll always support you. You’ve got this!

I’ve never been confident, ever since I was little. When I was a child, my parents almost never praised me, and I grew up in an environment with hitting, scolding, arguing, and fighting. As I got older, I slowly became kind of insecure. I don’t even like my own name. I deny everything about myself, and I’m also very unconfident about my appearance. Before I turned 18, a lot of people said I was pretty, but after I went to college I got a lot of acne, and it left my face full of pits. My skin is really bad, even disfigured, and that made me feel very inferior. My features aren’t as pretty as before either, and my figure is just average. But other people say I’m tall, not fat, have a well-proportioned body, and I’m not ugly. I feel like I’m not as good as those beautiful women, and I’m already 26 and still single. No one pursues me, and I’m even more afraid to make the first move. I feel like no one would like me. Recently I’ve been working out, and I’ve stuck with it for a month, but the results are too small. Then my mom put me down again, saying, what’s the point of getting thinner if I still don’t find someone? Now my low self-esteem is really severe, and I even feel a bit depressed. I cried all afternoon and evening, and the tears just come out on their own. I feel like I’ve accomplished nothing and that my life is such a failure. I also haven’t found a very suitable job recently. I’m already trying hard to change myself. I’m exercising hard to make myself slimmer, but the results are really so little. I’m very disappointed. I want to do something on my own and find a sense of self-worth, but I don’t know what to do.

Dear, I understand how you’re feeling right now. From what you’ve shared, it seems like you struggle with confidence in several areas. The violent way you were raised as a child and the lack of attention also made it easier for you to deny yourself. At the same time, your skin issues and being single have further hurt the confidence you do have. These things make you feel very down, very disappointed, and even depressed. But we don’t need to be perfect. We just need to find happiness and confidence. So you need to work on finding your strengths and your value, and begin the path of affirming yourself.

But sometimes it’s really hard. I just keep feeling inferior, like I can’t do anything well. I want to go beyond what I’m capable of, but then I feel like I can’t do it. I’m always caught in this conflict, and it feels exhausting.

Actually, everyone has low points. It’s part of life. What matters is how you get back up. There will be many things in life that don’t go the way we want, but we can’t let them knock us down. We can change ourselves and the environment around us through positive thinking and action. Even though things may be difficult for you right now, I believe you can pull yourself together and become a stronger version of yourself.
But I really don’t know where to start. Every time I’m in pain late at night, I get even more anxious and don’t know what to do.

First, you need to soothe your emotions. You can try some self-relaxation methods, like listening to music, reading, doing yoga, and so on. After you’ve calmed down, list out your problems and make a plan that can actually be carried out. For example, finding a suitable job, improving your skin condition, expanding your social circle, and so on. At the same time, you also need to sort through your thoughts and find what your happiness and confidence can rely on. Looking for hobbies or personal practice with a positive attitude will help you discover yourself better, and it will also help increase your level of self-affirmation.
Mm, I understand. So, specifically, what can I do to help myself?

Everyone needs one or more supporters to help them get through a low point. You can try talking about your worries and struggles, and let the suggestions that have already been created help you feel relieved. This is also a way to release stress. At the same time, you can learn some new skills or a language, take part in activities you’re interested in, and so on, to help yourself gain a sense of achievement. Most importantly, you need to keep encouraging and affirming yourself, and use the achievements and strengths you already have as nourishment to maintain your confidence.
Okay, I’ll try. Thank you for your support.
You’re welcome. Let’s keep going together! You’ve already taken the first step. Now let’s work together toward a better future!
Mm, I will. Thank you for encouraging me.
You’re welcome. I just hope I can help you. If you have any other questions or confusion, you can contact me anytime, and we’ll overcome any difficulties together!
My stuttering and obsessive-compulsive disorder are seriously affecting my life. I feel very depressed and low.

I heard that your stuttering and obsessive-compulsive symptoms eased somewhat when you were in college. That shows that relaxing your mindset can be very helpful. Outside of work, you can seek some psychological support and learn ways to ease your anxiety and relax yourself.
I often have headaches and chest tightness, because the repeated thinking from my obsessive-compulsive disorder makes my mind tense and uneasy, and it’s getting harder and harder for me to relax.
You can try relaxing your body and mind through physical activity, meditation, or deep breathing. These can be very helpful for easing your symptoms.
I’m always worried about how I perform and about making mistakes, and that has made me miss a lot of opportunities.
You can try to reduce your pursuit of perfectionism. Maybe start with small things, like being a little more flexible with the requirements for a project, so you can feel more relaxed.
It’s hard for me to handle things and express myself, because my stuttering makes me feel powerless and not confident.
