You can use good communication skills, such as practicing spoken expression and pronunciation, learning how to listen to other people’s opinions and feedback, and adjusting the way you speak in terms of speed and rhythm.
I often feel anxious and uneasy, and my obsessive-compulsive disorder is getting worse.

You can learn how to understand and respond to your obsessive-compulsive disorder in a healthier way, such as finding alternative behaviors and ways of thinking. You can also use professional treatment methods to help you manage the compulsive behaviors.
But I feel like my situation is really serious, and it seems like there’s no hope.

Try not to be too pessimistic or worried. Through active effort and practice, you can gradually improve your symptoms. Don’t forget to seek help and support from others as well. Help from a professional therapist may be even more beneficial for your recovery.
Thank you for your support and suggestions. I’ll do my best, so I can face life better.
I hope you can keep making your own efforts, continue to improve your range and tolerance, and believe that you can get through this dark period and return to a normal state of life.

Lately, my feelings toward people have felt really strange. Sometimes I feel very close to them, and sometimes I feel very distant. For example, when I’m with my partner, we can be talking nonstop, but as soon as he says one wrong thing, I instantly cool off. It feels like I can’t control it. This also shows up in my relationships with my daughter and my family—sometimes close, sometimes distant. Maybe it’s because I had the experience of being a left-behind child, or maybe it has to do with dual attachment. I don’t know what to do.

Reading what you shared, I feel very moved. First, let me give you a warm hug. The way you feel in relationships shows that you really long for closeness and also hope to be acknowledged. At the same time, you may also have some perfectionism and a desire for control. We need to learn to be more forgiving toward others, and try to forgive and tolerate other people’s mistakes. We can’t control others, but we can control ourselves. Learning to accept and adapt to other people’s shortcomings can make life better.

Thank you for understanding. I want to ask how to deal with being hot and cold emotionally. Sometimes I feel my daughter is the cutest and closest person in the world, and sometimes I feel I don’t care about her enough. My relationship with my family is like this too, and it makes me feel very conflicted and lost.

Being emotionally hot and cold is a very common issue. Sometimes it may be caused by inner anxiety or worries. I’d suggest communicating more with your husband; the relationship between husband and wife is the foundation of family relationships. When your relationship with your husband is good, other people won’t be able to bully you so easily. At the same time, communicate more with your daughter, share what’s on your mind, express your love more, and strengthen your bond. It’s the same with family members. I’d suggest communicating in warmer ways, understanding each other, and maintaining good relationships.

You’re right. I’ll try to talk more with my husband and communicate more with my daughter, and work on improving our family relationships. But I’m still really afraid of losing control of my emotions. What should I do?

You don’t need to be afraid of losing control of your emotions. This is a very common emotional experience. We need to learn to accept our emotions, while also learning to regulate and manage them. I’d suggest exercising more, listening to music more, and doing more of the things you enjoy. These can all help ease your emotions and make you feel calmer. If needed, you can also consider seeking professional counseling, talking about what’s in your heart, and getting more professional support.
Thank you for your suggestions. I’ll try to do them. But I still feel it’s really hard to face the worries and fears inside me, and I often have insomnia.

Insomnia is a mind-body issue, and we also need to take some steps to ease it. First, I’d suggest practicing good sleep hygiene and keeping a regular daily schedule and sleep routine. Second, you can try some ways to ease your emotions, such as deep breathing, relaxation training, meditation, and so on. Most importantly, open your heart and share your emotions and feelings with others, so you don’t feel so alone. I believe that as you work on improving yourself, everything will gradually get better.
Thank you for being with me and supporting me. I’ll do my best.

You’re welcome. Whenever you need help and support, I’m here. Remember, everyone has their own imperfections, but that doesn’t stop us from living in a healthy way. Face your emotions and needs bravely, and you’ll find that all kinds of problems in life can be eased and resolved.

My boyfriend is usually very good to me, to the point where I can’t find anything to criticize. But now I’m always afraid of upsetting him, and that he’ll lose his temper at me and say really hurtful things. I’m pretty introverted, and when he gets angry, I become even more afraid to speak. His temper really is very explosive.
Dear, sending you a hug ⊙ω⊙. First, I want to tell you that you are not wrong. In a bad relationship, no one is innocent. Everyone has their own problems and faults.
I know I’m not a flawless person either. But he just gets angry too easily. Sometimes I have no idea what I did to upset him, and he starts insulting me.

I understand how you feel. Everyone has their own life experiences and environment, and these can affect their personality and behavior. Maybe he went through some bad things in life before, which led to his explosive temper now. We need to understand his past and help him get out of his current difficulty.
But every time he gets angry, he insults me, and that makes me really scared. Sometimes I don’t even know how to deal with him.

I can understand your worry and fear. But we shouldn’t give up on helping him change his behavior. You can try communicating with him, telling him how you feel, and hoping he can understand your thoughts. When talking with him, we should persuade him with reason, rather than using emotions to influence his decisions.
Every time he gets angry, I feel really heavy inside. Actually, I’ve also thought about whether I should break up with him, especially every time he loses his temper.

Breaking up is one way to solve the problem, but it may not necessarily be the best choice. I hope you can think about it calmly and understand your own thoughts and feelings. If you believe breaking up is the only solution, then you can consider breaking up. But before making a decision, you must think it through fully and carefully.
Actually, I can’t bear to break up with him, because I love him. But every time he loses his temper, I think about it, and I feel very tired and discouraged.

Love is not something we give up on easily. But we need to love ourselves and care about our mental health. If his behavior makes you feel mentally exhausted and weighed down, then you also need to consider protecting yourself. We can try communicating with him and looking for ways to solve the problem. But no matter what, you need to keep taking care of your mental health.
I understand. Thank you for your advice and help. I’ll think carefully about this and handle it properly.

You’re welcome. I hope my advice can help you. Whenever you need help and support, I’ll be here waiting for you. Remember to take care of yourself, keep a positive and optimistic mindset, and make life better.

Lately I feel like I’ve gained a new understanding of relationships, but it’s left me feeling lost and disappointed. I’ve realized that relationships between people are built on needs and social ideas, and these relationships don’t always make people feel truly present or valued. On the contrary, they can make people feel empty and in pain. I don’t know how I should face this world and the people around me, and this feeling is really troubling me.

Hi, I hear how troubled you feel. First, I think your view reflects some deep thinking about relationships, and that isn’t a bad thing. Value exchange in relationships does exist, but unlike economic transactions, it focuses more on both people’s willingness and feelings. In that process, relationships can bring satisfaction and happiness to each other, and that is also the beautiful part of human connection.
But I still feel a sense of emptiness, because these relationships seem to be built on one’s own needs, rather than truly caring about the other person.

It’s true that each of us has our own needs and interests, but that doesn’t mean we can’t care for and support each other. In relationships, both people can meet their own feelings and needs, while also offering support and care, and building genuine bonds of friendship and family affection. Not everyone is only acting for themselves, especially in family relationships, where people are more often thinking about each other’s happiness and safety.

But I feel like right now I’m someone who needs other people’s approval. I’m really afraid of being rejected or ignored. Sometimes I even ignore my own feelings in order to meet the other person’s needs.

I understand how you feel, but this isn’t a healthy way to be in relationships. In relationships, we need to hold on to our own boundaries and needs, while also respecting the other person’s feelings and needs. If you feel the other person’s needs are unreasonable or would make you uncomfortable, you can express your thoughts appropriately, rather than blindly going along with them or sacrificing yourself to please others.
But I’m really afraid of seeming unlikeable or not fitting the norm. Sometimes I suppress my emotions or think I haven’t done well enough.

This is a common psychological difficulty—low self-esteem or social anxiety. You need to understand that everyone has their own strengths and weaknesses. We don’t need to keep catering to other people’s expectations or suppressing our own emotions. Honesty and confidence are important factors in building healthy relationships, not blindly going along with others or caring too much about what they think. You can practice self-acceptance and self-encouragement, and gradually build your confidence and self-esteem.
Thank you for your advice. I’ll try to hold on to my own boundaries and pay more attention to my own feelings and needs, while also respecting other people’s feelings and needs.

That’s good. Having confidence in your own growth is very important. At the same time, psychological difficulties can’t be overcome overnight; it takes a gradual process. If you need more help or support, you might consider finding a professional psychologist or counselor to help you.
Okay, thank you for your support and encouragement. I’ll do my best to become better.

You’re welcome. You can always come to me to talk. The human inner world and emotions are very complex. We don’t need to have ourselves sorted out all the time; we need to learn to accept and face every corner of our inner selves. Once again, I wish you a happy life!
Lately, whenever I think about having to have children after getting married, I somehow start to feel anxious. I feel like I’m still a child, and that after marriage I’ll be an adult.

I understand how you feel. You don’t need to worry—this is a very normal psychological reaction. You may be wondering why you’re having these feelings. Actually, at different stages of life, we face many different challenges, and the pressure we feel can vary. But there’s nothing wrong with that. Have confidence in yourself. You can get through this, because you’re already making an effort to break out of this difficult situation.
Thank you for encouraging me. But I’m still really afraid of what life will be like in the future.

Your worries are very normal. We’ve all had worries like this. But life is full of changes. When you’re ready to face them, you may feel more at ease. Remember, don’t put too much pressure on yourself, and don’t ignore your own feelings. You need to trust yourself and move step by step in the direction you want to go. We all look forward to seeing you successfully achieve your dreams.
I really want to manage my anxiety in some way. Do you have any suggestions?

When you feel anxious and worried, if you can talk with someone who has experience or authority, you may feel more relaxed. We’re glad to see that you’re reaching out to us for support now. At the same time, you can try doing things that relax your body and mind, like listening to soothing music at the right time, reading some good books, and so on. Maybe these things would also be valuable for you.
I’ll try the methods you just mentioned. But right now I’m very unsure whether the decision I’ve made is the right one.

Try not to worry too much about your choices, because sometimes it’s completely okay not to make the best choice. If you can’t make a decision about something, then let yourself relax a little. You’ll find the answer soon. But that doesn’t mean you can’t complain or seek help. You can vent to someone you trust, or talk with a professional. Remember, you’re not alone.
Thank you for helping me sort out my thoughts. You really understand my situation.

It’s okay. I’ll always be here to support you. Sometimes, we just need someone who is willing to care about us, listen to us, and then offer a few suggestions. That can be enough to help us feel comforted and supported.

My girlfriend and I have known each other for over two years, but in the past six months, some of the things she says have started to seem abnormal. She often says things that sound anti-human, and I’m really worried about her mental state. Supporter, what do you think I should do?

Hello, after reading what you shared, I can really understand how you feel. This kind of situation is quite common, because many people now are troubled by the negative influence of short videos. I suggest you first try communicating with her, understanding her thoughts and inner needs, paying more attention to her inner world, and listening to her more, so she can feel your support and understanding.

Okay, thank you for your advice. But I’m still really worried about her mental health, because she’s obsessed with Douyin and other short videos all day, even to the point that it affects her daily life. How can I get her to put down her phone?

You could make a schedule together with her, arranging her study, daily life, and entertainment time, so she can be clear about what she needs to do, set goals for herself, and achieve them. At the same time, you could also introduce her to some traditional books with sound values, and gradually guide her to change unhealthy habits.

That sounds like it might be a good idea. I’ll try talking with her and see what she thinks and what her opinions are. But I feel like social media these days has gone a bit too far, and its impact is really far-reaching.

Indeed, the negative impact of modern social media can’t be ignored. But we also need to see that these media have brought many positive effects as well. While paying attention to her, you also need to leave yourself time and space to do things you’re interested in that feel positive and uplifting. That way, you’ll be better able to help her solve the problem.
Okay, I understand. But sometimes the things she says really leave me at a loss. How should I respond?

Try to stay patient and rational, and don’t respond to her negative emotions with a negative attitude. You can try to find common ground in what she says, guide the direction of her thinking about the issue, and help her improve her mental state through ongoing reflection and exploration.
I understand. I’ll definitely try to communicate with her properly. Are there any good ways to regulate her mental state that could help her relax and ease her emotions?

You can try encouraging her to learn some techniques for relaxing the body and mind, such as meditation, calming breathing, and yoga. You could also take her outdoors to enjoy the sunshine and immerse herself in nature. Let her slowly find inner balance and peace away from unhelpful outside influences.

Okay, these are all very good suggestions. Thank you for your support and encouragement. I think I’ll do my best to help her, and with my companionship and encouragement, help her step by step come out of her confusion and difficulties.
Thank you very much for your trust and sincerity. I hope our conversation can help you and her come out of this psychological difficulty together, and rediscover yourselves and your inner strength.

I like observing the details of facial expressions, but I’m not sure whether I should study behavioral psychology or the social side of psychology. I don’t know which textbooks I should read, and I’m also not sure whether I need to get a psychology certificate.

Hello, hearing your question, I understand that you want to explore more knowledge about psychology. First, you should know that your interest is valid, and that is already a good thing. If you’re interested in subtle expressions, I’d suggest studying microexpression psychology. As for textbooks, some introductory books are not only simple and easy to understand, but also have enough depth to help you understand the basics of psychology. Also, if you’ve taught yourself some psychology knowledge, you could help others in the community, which would also allow you to use your strengths and skills.
Thank you for your suggestions. The community is also a good idea. But I’m still not sure whether I need to get a psychology certificate. Do you think it’s necessary?

Actually, not everyone needs to get a certificate. It depends on your career plans and goals. If you want to work in the field of psychology, then some recognized certificates are necessary, and they can provide you with more opportunities and resources. But if you’re studying psychology only out of interest, then a certificate isn’t essential.
I see. My knowledge of psychology is still not very sufficient right now. I’d like to ask what suggestions you have for dealing with negative emotions.

When we encounter difficulties or negative emotions, we often only see the problem, rather than the solution. So I’d suggest that you first look at the problem carefully, and then actively think of ways to solve it. On that basis, you can use some relaxation techniques, such as practicing meditation or breathing exercises, to help you balance your emotions and relax your body and mind.
These methods sound pretty good. But sometimes I feel tired and discouraged. Do you have any more specific suggestions to help me manage and ease these feelings?

When you feel tired and discouraged, my suggestion is to take your physical and mental health seriously. You can help yourself ease these feelings by exercising, maintaining good sleep habits, and eating healthily. At the same time, remember to keep up positive social activities, so your mood can relax and find balance. Finally, don’t forget to arrange some personal hobbies or ways to relax. This can help you find balance and enjoyment outside of work and study.
I feel like your suggestions are very helpful. Thank you for your support and help!
No need to thank me. We all need support and help. If you need further support or have other mental health concerns, I’m always here, and you can come chat with me.
Hello, I’m feeling a bit anxious and depressed, and I don’t know what to do.

Hello, I can understand how you’re feeling right now. First, you can start with a regular daily routine and exercise, and keep up healthy habits. At the same time, you can also get more professional help by consulting a mental health professional or joining a counseling group.
I know, but sometimes I feel like the people around me don’t understand me.

That’s because they haven’t gone through what you’re going through, but don’t give up on seeking help because of that. You can try looking for more information, or joining relevant social networks. That way, you may meet more people who can empathize with you, and more people who are willing to listen to your difficulties and needs.
I’m still really scared. I don’t know how to face my problems.

That feeling is understandable, but don’t let fear control your life. Try to face difficulties with a positive attitude and find ways to solve the problems. If you’re struggling with schizophrenia, you can try looking for social support, such as joining a therapist-led support group, or contacting relevant nonprofit organizations to get professional help and understanding.
Oh, I understand. I’ll take action as soon as I can. Thank you for your advice.

You’re welcome. I’m very glad I could offer you some help. No matter what situations or problems you’re facing, remember that you’re not alone. You can seek help and support through different channels, and with healthy habits and a positive attitude, you can face all the challenges in your life.
Thank you for your encouragement and support. I’ll try even harder.
You’re doing well. Keep moving in a positive direction, believe in yourself, and you will get through this difficult time. If you need more help and support, don’t hesitate to contact me anytime.
During the pandemic last year, when I was at home, I found myself again. But after I went back to school, dorm life made me really unhappy.
Hearing you say all this, I can feel how upset you are. It’s really brave of you to speak up and express your feelings. Please keep sharing with me what’s been troubling you.

There’s a girl in the dorm who often talks about me, and it makes me feel really disgusted. They also often disturb my sleep, and they even threatened to send an audio recording of me arguing to my mom.

It sounds like that girl’s behavior makes you feel very uncomfortable. I understand how you feel; that’s really hard. But I want to emphasize that you have the right to protect yourself. You can communicate with them calmly, or seek help from the dorm administrator to resolve this issue.
I’m just worried that if I talk to them face-to-face, we’ll end up arguing.

If this girl makes it hard for you to stay calm, you can write down what you want to say and express your feelings that way. This can help you communicate your thoughts clearly without losing control of your emotions. I believe you can handle this painful situation well.
I really, really don’t like having conflicts with other people.

I know. Many people are afraid of conflict. But conflict is an unavoidable part of relationships. Handling conflict well can help us get along better with others and understand each other’s thoughts and feelings. You can practice more conflict-resolution skills, and that can help you communicate better with others.
I’m also worried that everyone will criticize me and think there’s something wrong with me.

Try not to take it too much to heart. Other people’s opinions don’t have to control our emotions or confidence. College students’ lifestyles and rhythms aren’t all exactly the same; everyone has their own way of living. Try to look at yourself from a more positive perspective and accept your shortcomings. Maybe that will help you better face other people’s judgments of you.
I’m also worried that I’m complaining and making it hard for others to study.

Don’t blame yourself. Seeking help from others is also very normal. Everyone needs emotional support sometimes. I believe the people who love you will understand you and be willing to help you deal with difficulties.
I just feel like everyone should respect each other, but they don’t respect me.

That’s a very good point. Respect is a very important part of relationships. But sometimes we need to actively show that attitude ourselves. By respecting others and showing your goodwill, you can help others respect you more and create better relationships with each other.
Thank you for your suggestions, but I still seem to have some negative thoughts.

That’s okay. Everyone has negative emotions and thoughts sometimes. What matters is how we deal with these emotions. You can try adjusting your thought patterns and putting your attention on more positive and constructive thoughts. You can also try immersing yourself in things you enjoy, and doing things that help you relax and feel good.
I’ll try doing some things that help me relax, to adjust my thought patterns.

That’s very good. Doing that can be really helpful. If you need to, you can seek help and support from the people around you, and you can also try talking with a professional counselor. I believe you’ll gradually get through this difficult time and become stronger and more confident.

Recently, during the pandemic, I’ve had very little contact with other people. Now school is suddenly about to start again, and I feel like I can’t adapt well to group life. When I’m around crowds, I withdraw and feel scared, and I just want to get to somewhere with fewer people as soon as possible.

I understand. During the pandemic, many people have been self-isolating, so it’s understandable to have this kind of reaction when facing larger social interactions. You’re not alone. This is a very normal response, and you can allow yourself to be in this state.
When I’m at home now, I can get along with my family easily, but once I’m in a group where people are kind of unfamiliar and not really close to me, I feel at a loss and don’t know what to do.

This is because you lack self-confidence and are afraid or worried that others will see you as not good enough. This is a very common issue. You can try doing some self-encouragement exercises at home, as long as you don’t put too much pressure on yourself.
I don’t know how to adapt to these changes. I feel like I’m stuck in a difficult situation.
At times like this, you can make use of online social media to talk and communicate with your friends, share your feelings, or seek help from teachers or counselors. These are all good options.
I always feel like I get trapped in other people’s opinions and can’t truly express my own thoughts. This is really upsetting for me.

This is because you focus too much on your own views and care too much about other people’s evaluations, to the point that you lack confidence. You can take part in more social activities, increase your social experience, and gradually overcome this anxiety, helping yourself overcome feelings of inferiority.
I’m really worried that I’ll be isolated and rejected at school.

Try not to worry too much. There are many people in the same situation. You can join school clubs and look for activities you like. You can also communicate with classmates or teachers before school starts, increase mutual understanding, and make it easier for yourself to integrate into the community and truly expand your social circle.
Thank you for your support and suggestions. I’ll think about it carefully, and then actively try things out.
Don’t forget, we, like you, have also felt uneasy and distressed before. What’s important is to overcome these feelings. You can seek help from us, and we’ll be here to listen to you and help you.
I recently broke up with my boyfriend, and I’ve been stuck feeling conflicted and regretful about my bad temper. I don’t know what to do.

First, it’s important to accept yourself. Only when you can accept yourself can you better accept others. The pattern you described—“being ignored - anxious feelings - more being ignored - longing to be understood - not being accepted - growing distant - unable to connect emotionally…”—fits with attachment theory. I’d suggest seeking counseling, because this kind of attachment relationship needs to be repaired through interpersonal relationships, and it’s relatively hard to improve on your own.
Do I really need counseling? I feel like I’m not that bad.

That’s not wrong. Everyone needs to pay attention to their emotional health. No matter how you’re feeling right now, working with a counselor to explore it together can help you better understand your inner world and provide more effective, personalized support.
Then if I meet another partner, how can I change this pattern?

First, you need to understand your own attachment style. It could be secure, avoidant, dismissive, or anxious. Based on your own style, finding a partner who is willing to accept and be understanding of you, along with your own active efforts to change, can help you create a healthy emotional connection through your joint efforts.
Then how do I understand my attachment style?
You can learn about your attachment style through psychological tests or counseling. You can also read some related books or materials to increase your emotional awareness.
I feel like I’ve become selfish now, and I don’t know how to change.

To change this situation, you can try starting from within yourself and paying more attention to other people’s feelings, and try to show more care so you can build a more stable emotional connection. At the same time, be patient. Change takes time, and don’t be too hard on yourself.
I’ll try to do that. Thank you for your encouragement and advice.
You’re welcome. We’ll keep going together! If you have any other questions, feel free to come chat with me anytime. I’ll do whatever I can to help you.

Lately things seem a bit off with a friend. Every time I talk to her about something, she agrees verbally, but then in her actions she keeps putting it off again and again. It feels like I’ve been tricked by her. If you say something 10 times, it becomes nagging; she agrees so readily but doesn’t act on it. I really hate that.

Hello, hearing about what you’ve been going through, I understand how you feel. Maybe your friend is using a kind of passive-aggressive behavior. This behavior uses negative, hidden ways to vent one’s emotions, as a way to attack the person or thing they’re unhappy with. It makes sense that you feel you’ve been attacked.
Yes, I really do feel that.

Then I can offer some help. 1. When you make a request, you can give her a few options and emphasize that no matter which one she chooses, you won’t get angry or complain. 2. At the same time, allow her to express anger and dissatisfaction, and you can discuss with her what a good standard would look like. 3. If you’ve already discussed the standard, you can let her clearly understand that you won’t just let her vent her emotions at you, and you also need to set your own boundaries. 4. If possible, encourage her to find a counselor to help her manage her emotions and overcome passive aggression. 5. Tell her that there are many ways to express anger, and she can learn to express her needs directly in a calm and firm way. That’s usually the easiest for everyone to accept. Remember, you weren’t necessarily tricked; she may just not know how to say “no.” Wishing you well~!
Thank you for your suggestions. They’ve given me more ideas for solving the problem. I’ll try to communicate with her properly.
I’m glad I could help. If you need any help, please let me know.
Okay, thank you.
You’re welcome. Let’s agree to work together to solve the problem!
Okay, definitely!
Is there anything else I can help you with?
No, that’s all. Thank you for listening patiently and for your advice.
It’s okay. You can come chat with me anytime.
I'm afraid that when I look at other people, it makes them uncomfortable.
It sounds like this is really troubling you, right?
Yes. I don't know what to do.
First, you should know that this feeling is very normal. Many people have this kind of worry.
Then what should I do?
You could try asking the people you think you may be making uncomfortable by looking at them, and see whether they really do feel uncomfortable. They may not have noticed at all.
Mm, I'll give it a try.
Also, you can practice relaxation techniques, like deep breathing or meditation, to reduce your anxiety.
Okay, I'll try. Thank you for your suggestions.
You're welcome. I also often have similar feelings. Let's work on overcoming it together.
Mm, okay. I feel much more at ease. Thank you for always being here with me.
It's okay. I'm always here to support you, and I'm willing to help you get through this difficult time.
I have a question I’d like to ask. How can I communicate well with my teacher? I’m afraid of being criticized because of communication problems.
It’s okay. We can think through possible solutions together. Could you describe how you and your teacher usually communicate, and what specifically happened?

Here’s what happened. My advisor asked if I wanted to go to her place to pick up some books. I didn’t know how far it was, so I replied, “Sorry, I’m not sure about the distance,” and then she got angry.

I understand your anxiety and nervousness. But considering that your advisor is your elder and your mentor, we need to respect her opinion and give a positive response. You could try asking her for the specific address, or share your choice and thoughts.
Right, I know what I should do now. I’ll express my gratitude and respect to my teacher.
Good. I really support this decision. At the same time, we may also need to learn and practice better communication skills and strategies.
Right. I feel like sometimes I just don’t know how to communicate with others. Are there any good ways to learn?

You can look for a professional counselor or other mental health resources to learn and talk things through. You can also read related books and materials to reflect on and summarize your own experiences.
Okay, thank you for your advice. I have one more question. Now my teacher has given me two options, and I’m not sure how to choose in a better way.

This question is relatively specific, and your judgment and strategy depend on many factors. You can try combining your own thoughts and needs with the specific situation and practical needs, then make a better choice after careful evaluation.
I understand. Thank you for your advice and help. Now I feel more confident about communicating well with my advisor.

That’s wonderful. I’m glad I could help. One last thing I want to say is, don’t care too much about other people’s judgments and criticism. Trust yourself, keep improving your communication skills, and get along harmoniously with others. You’re not alone; we’ll move forward together.

Lately I feel like I'm becoming more and more fragile inside, and when I run into difficulties I feel anxious. My mother cares about me a lot, but I feel like I'm very self-centered, rather indifferent to the outside world, and lacking in emotion.

Hearing you say that, I can understand how you feel inside. Everyone has their own vulnerabilities and uneasiness; these are very normal human emotional responses. You’re not alone, and we can look for answers together.

I feel inferior and sensitive. I'm afraid to talk to others, and I always guess whether they like me or not. I stay doubtful and negative, and it's hard for me to make decisions. And I set my expectations for myself too high.

These feelings can be very troubling, but I think this can also be an opportunity. By noticing your own shortcomings and needs, you can strengthen yourself and become more mature. Not everyone is able to realize that they need to keep improving themselves, and that is a good thing.
But it's always hard for me to accept my shortcomings. Sometimes other people's criticism makes me very unhappy, and I also pick at what I think is bad in others.

We all need to recognize that we have shortcomings; this is an opportunity for growth. And we should also learn to accept criticism from others and discover from it where we need to improve. This is also very helpful for our growth.
I really like comparing the people around me with myself, and when I see others doing well, I feel jealous.

Everyone has their own strengths and shortcomings. We should believe in and cherish our own strengths. And we shouldn't use others to measure ourselves so easily. Other people's achievements don't affect our own achievements; instead, they can push us to work hard and grow.
I feel like I need to become stronger, but my grades and abilities have always been just average.

Everyone has their own talents and interests. We should find what we like and work hard to develop ourselves. Also, a good mindset is very important. Your confidence and positivity can also help you move forward.
I feel like my relationships have also been greatly affected, and I can't communicate smoothly.
Communication really is important. We need to find suitable ways and methods to communicate, and we also need to learn to listen to other people's opinions and suggestions.
Then what advice would you have to help me become stronger?

First, we need to try to let go of psychological barriers and balance our emotional and mental state. At the same time, we need to arrange our time reasonably and find hobbies and interests for ourselves. Also, we need to be brave in expressing ourselves and take steps toward communication. You will become stronger.
After hearing your suggestions, I feel somewhat encouraged. I'll work hard to put them into practice.
Believe in yourself. You've got this! If you have any difficulties or problems, feel free to come back and talk with me anytime. We'll get through these difficulties together.

I recently had a fight with my boyfriend. He keeps insisting that we live together, saying it’s the standard for whether I love him or not. I’m more conservative and can’t accept living together before marriage. What should we do when the two of us think differently?

Hello, I can see what’s troubling you. When your views differ, the most important thing is to understand each other. If he can’t understand your more conservative view, and you also can’t fully accept his request, then things between the two of you become very complicated. You can try talking with him about what you think and see how he responds. In that process, please be honest, and don’t worry too much about his feelings. The ultimate goal is to understand each other, not to blame or pressure each other. I hope the two of you can find a proper resolution.
I’ve tried talking to him, but he seems to completely not understand what I think. I’m really frustrated. I feel like our trust and respect have hit a bottleneck.

I understand how you feel. This kind of conflict really can be upsetting. But the story isn’t over yet. After all, you have a strong emotional foundation, don’t you? Since you both want to solve the problem, please communicate patiently, find the root of the issue, and then try to resolve it. I believe that as long as both of you have enough trust and patience, you can get through this difficult situation and move toward a better future.
I’m so scared that if I can’t let go of this issue, the two of us won’t be able to keep going.

Try not to worry too much, and don’t give up your beliefs. We can’t stay stuck in the past; we need to learn to embrace the future. As long as you and your partner truly love each other and fully understand each other, you will surely have a good life in the future. At the same time, don’t give up your own beliefs out of concern for others. Life is rich and colorful because of differences. I believe you can find your own path and move toward happiness with the person you love.
Thank you for your advice. I’ll try to communicate with him and understand his thoughts. At the same time, I also need to have enough confidence and courage in myself, and hold on to my own beliefs.
Very good! I believe you’ll find the right solution. And no matter what choice you make, I will support you. I hope the two of you can continue living happily. Wishing you well!

I suddenly realized that I act really mean toward my mother, really harsh. I seem to have endless patience for strangers who don’t matter, but I’m stingy about showing tolerance and patience to my mother. I’m always impatient with her. Every time I stay with her in an enclosed space for more than half an hour, I make her get away from me and go back to her own room, because I simply can’t stand being with her.

Hello! When I read about the relationship between you and your mother, I thought of a “pursuer-distancer pattern.” Your mother keeps moving toward you, while you keep trying to get away. This kind of relationship makes you feel suffocated, and you respond by cutting off and being cold, even though you know this isn’t healthy. Could you share with me what you feel when you’re in this state of mind? You said you’re very curious about why this happens. What I can tell you is that a “pursuer-distancer pattern” usually appears in close relationships, especially between parents and children, so this is also showing up in your relationship.

Actually, whenever my mother wants attention and closeness from me, I feel really uncomfortable, even panicky and anxious. Whenever my mother reaches out to me on her own, I immediately feel unsafe, and I push her away and keep my distance.

I understand your situation. Sometimes you feel your mother is pursuing you too closely, and you don’t want too much attention. This conflict makes you feel very anxious. We can explore together what inner needs are behind your complaints about your mother and your avoidance of her. Excessive pursuing or avoiding may mean that some positive or negative feelings in you are unresolved, and when they’re overstimulated and can’t be met right away, you become anxious and uneasy.
Mm-hmm, that’s very possible. I also have a hard time understanding what I actually need in relationships, and I don’t know how to express my feelings and needs.

Yes, that’s very normal. Many people run into the same issue when seeking help. I suggest starting from your inner feelings and really thinking about your emotional needs toward your mother. I hope you can find some ways to express your feelings and needs.
I’ll try to express my needs. At the same time, I also really want to know why I have this so-called “sense of revenge.” Every time I reject my mother, I feel very pleased and satisfied.

Your “sense of satisfaction” may come from feeling in control, and that may make you feel comforted and satisfied. Her pursuit of you is a kind of “request,” and you are able to refuse it. But if this emotion and these thoughts become overstimulating, they may make your relationship more and more distant. I suggest you learn to communicate as equally as possible, so as to reduce the influence of this feeling.
Okay, thank you for your suggestion. I’ll try to change my attitude and behavior, and do my best to reduce the influence this feeling has on me.

Good. I believe you can learn more about your own psychological state through self-exploration, and find more positive ways to address this. At the same time, I suggest communicating more with your mother, so that the relationship between you can become more harmonious.
Thank you for your suggestions and support. I’ll think about them seriously and try to take action.

I’m about to start eighth grade, and I don’t know how to improve my grades. In seventh grade, I did really poorly on a lot of major exams. I’m really worried I won’t be able to get into high school, and my parents are very anxious for me too.

Try not to worry too much. Everyone has their own strengths and weaknesses. You were always among the top students in elementary school, which shows that you are capable. If seventh grade didn’t go well, there may be many reasons for that, and we can identify them one by one and work on them.
But I really don’t know what to do to do well in my schoolwork, especially in the subjects I’m not good at, like math and history.

Math and physics require you to remember theories, definitions, and formulas, and to be able to apply them flexibly. For history, politics, geography, and biology, you can spend more time memorizing and reviewing; the same goes for English. Also, for Chinese, it’s important to focus on building knowledge and understanding, and memorization is important too.

My problems with studying are already making me really upset, and I especially don’t want to be laughed at or blamed by others. Teachers and classmates often say I have a weak foundation and won’t do well on exams. That makes me feel very sad.

Of course hearing those things would make you feel sad, but those words are only other people’s opinions, and they don’t have to control your mindset. You are a girl who really wants to improve. Don’t let those harsh words and grades crush you. Believe in yourself, understand your strengths and weaknesses, and work on improving. You will definitely be able to get good grades, and more people will also come to see your strengths.
Thank you for trusting me and encouraging me. But I always give up studying because of certain things. How can I keep my motivation to study?

Motivation needs to be maintained through both inner drive and outside encouragement. First, you need to think clearly about why you want to study—that is your inner drive. Outside encouragement can include small rewards, plans, sharing with friends, and so on. Also, pay attention to rest and your physical health, and keep a pleasant mood. These can all help you maintain your motivation to study.
By the way, I also want to ask about choosing courses. I’m not good at math or history, but I’m especially interested in Chinese and English. What courses do you think I should choose?

Everyone’s interests and talents are different, so the courses they choose will vary from person to person. If you are especially interested in Chinese and English, you can explore those subjects more deeply. There is no “wrong” choice; the key is your attitude and how much effort you put in. If you’re interested in the courses, there is a lot of hope for learning them well. At the same time, you can also strengthen your practice in the subjects you’re not good at outside of class.
Thank you for your advice. I’ll work hard to study and improve my weaknesses. If I run into difficulties with studying, I’ll ask you for help as soon as I can.
No problem. You can come talk to me anytime. I believe you can overcome the difficulties and get good grades. You’ve got this!

I met a guy, and we’re in different places, but after a gathering we started having this kind of ambiguous period for about a month. Now we’re boyfriend and girlfriend, but our relationship is very complicated. I’ve realized I really like him, but he seems to only be thinking about the practical issues, worrying about work and not continuing our relationship.

That sounds really difficult, and I understand how you feel. It’s very normal to have this kind of conflicting feeling, and you don’t have to feel pressured. Sometimes we need to calm down and think about what we truly want.
Yeah, I feel like I keep thinking about it like this, and I feel really torn. I don’t want to lose this relationship, but I’m also afraid that if I’m too attached, I’ll lose my own life.

I understand how you feel. Keep in mind that before making any decision, try to be sure whether that person is worth all your effort and persistence. Don’t be afraid to consider letting go; sometimes letting go takes more courage than holding on.
But I don’t know what I should do. I used to be a very brave person, but now I can’t handle this complicated situation.
Think about your past experiences. Maybe you’ve faced some difficulties before—how did you overcome them in the end? Could you apply those solutions to the current situation?
I understand. Maybe I need to understand myself more, and guide myself more to face this problem. Thank you for your advice.
You’re welcome. I’m always happy to help others. When you need it, please always remember to seek help and support.
Lately I’ve been doing well at work, but I still feel like I’m missing my in-laws’ recognition and support. I don’t know how to let go of this thought.

I understand that you want recognition from the people around you, and that’s very normal. At the same time, you can also recognize that you’re already doing very well, and you don’t need other people’s approval to prove yourself.
But why can I accept my parents’ opinions, while I care so much about what my in-laws think?

This may be because your in-laws’ opinions and trust feel more important to you, so you care about them more. But you need to know that your own recognition and trust in yourself are the most important.
I know that makes sense rationally, but why do I still emotionally want to prove myself?

This is a very human reaction, but emotionally driven behavior isn’t helpful for your mental health or growth. You can ease these feelings through self-affirmation and by seeking some professional support.
Okay, I’ll try to affirm myself more, and I’ll also think about ways to seek help.
Good. This is an important step toward a healthier direction. You can also try communicating with your in-laws, so they can have a fuller understanding of your strengths.
I’ll think carefully about this suggestion. Thank you for your patient support and advice.

You’re welcome. I’ll always be here to support you. At the same time, I’d also suggest talking more with the people around you and sharing your thoughts and feelings. That can also help you relax more.
Okay, I’ll keep that in mind. Thank you again for your help and support.
You’re welcome. Whenever you need help, I’ll be here. I hope you can face life with more confidence and a more positive attitude.
I feel like life really has no hope. I’m not afraid of dying either. Death feels like the best way for me to be free. I’m so tired. How can I kill myself without pain?
I’m very sorry to hear you say that. Your feelings and thoughts are important. Would you be willing to share with me how you’ve come to feel that there’s no hope, or what has led to this feeling?
I feel like there’s no way to change the situation I’m in now. Everything feels hopeless and helpless.

I know this is a very difficult thought to have, but could you try to see it as a kind of challenge or test? Everyone faces some challenges, and if we can find ways to face them, even in the darkest moments, we can still find support and something to lean on.
But I really feel so tired. I don’t have the strength to face any more challenges.

I completely understand how you feel. Sometimes we need to take a break and gather our energy again. Maybe you could try to relax a bit, get some good rest, do some things you like, and get back into a better state of mind, so you’ll be better able to face the challenges.
But I really want to die. Life has no meaning at all for me.

I care a lot about what you’re thinking, and I’m glad you’re willing to share it with me. Still, we need to be careful not to let negative thoughts take over our minds. We can find many reasons to keep going. Why not spend some time thinking about the good things in life?
I don’t seem to be able to feel anything good anymore.

Sometimes, we need to spend some time and energy looking for things we like, finding the things that can bring us calm and joy. But in this process, we also need to remember our own progress and achievements. Could you tell me, over the past while, what are some things you feel proud of?
Actually, I’ve been doing pretty well at work.
Could you talk a bit more about your achievements at work? Maybe your work is the thing you’re most proud of. You should celebrate and appreciate your own effort and progress.
Mm, it does seem like there have been some achievements and progress.

Seeing you begin to feel some of your own achievements and progress makes me feel very relieved. You can try to think more about your strengths and good qualities, and that way you’ll be better able to face these difficulties and challenges.
Thank you for being here with me and supporting me.
You’re welcome. I care a lot about how you’re doing. If you still need my company and support, tell me anytime.

I feel like I’m full of immature childishness. I don’t even know basic things like scallions, ginger, and garlic. I work at the grassroots level, my spouse and I live apart, and I’m far away from my family and child. I feel unloved and lonely. I’m alone in a county town, with no friends.

Seeing the state you’re in right now, I can feel that you’re surrounded by negative emotions. You have a lot of negative judgments about yourself, and these thoughts are not healthy and need to change. Understanding your emotions and feelings is the first step.
I used to be self-righteous, arrogant, and speak without thinking. Now I have very few friends, and I’d rather be alone.

Remember, you are not alone. Many people are in situations similar to yours. You need to accept, understand, and appreciate yourself. Once you accept yourself, you can get through this difficult place. At the same time, you can adjust the way you interact with others and communicate reasonably by expressing your needs.
I feel shut off from others. I don’t know how to handle relationships. My family and coworkers don’t trust me.

You don’t need to care too much about other people’s evaluations. The most important thing is being able to accept yourself and make positive changes in your daily life. Improving your skills and taking part in training can help you feel more confident and present yourself better in front of others.
I feel like life has lost its meaning, and I lack a sense of value.

Life has many meanings. When you can accept yourself and choose a better way of living, you can feel your own value. You can also find meaning in life through working hard, learning, spending time with friends, and reuniting with family. Everyone has their own unique mission.
I want to quit my job. What you do in this world isn’t important; what matters is the family being together.

Sometimes, making the decision to change is important. We need to understand our own situation and the difficulties we’re currently facing, and then make positive changes. Family reunion is indeed very important, but it may also be possible to balance work and family without sacrificing your career.
I feel like I don’t have enough ability, and I’m far from success.

Everyone has their own standards for success. Remember, success is not only about career. Success in family and social life is just as important. You can reshape your beliefs and believe that you have the ability to become a better version of yourself.
I feel like life is too hard, and it’s difficult to deal with problems.

There are many bumps along the journey of life, and overcoming them is an important way to achieve personal growth. Communicate with others, share your thoughts, and look for solutions to the problems. Every problem has a solution; sometimes it takes continuous trying to find it.
I feel like I’m not understood, and no one believes me.

This is indeed a very tricky issue, but don’t let it drag you down. Understand your emotions and your past feelings. Only while accepting yourself can you allow others to accept you. You can try changing your patterns of behavior, strengthening your self-confidence, and expressing your thoughts better.
I feel like life is an invisible prison, pressing down on me.

Your emotions and feelings can restrict your behavior. What’s important is learning to listen to your inner self and relax, so you can understand your thoughts and actions. In short, you are not completely alone and helpless. Finding a solution that fits you is the key to resolving the problem.
Thank you for your suggestions. I’ll work on adjusting myself and try to understand myself in a more positive way, and overcome the problems I’m facing.

We are willing to help you get through this difficult place. You also need to believe in your own abilities and have confidence in yourself. Let’s support each other through our efforts and work together to achieve our life goals.
Lately I keep feeling like I don’t have enough friends, and I’m very anxious.
Hi, I’m glad to talk with you about this. I’d like to know, what do you think friendship should be like?
I think it should be about understanding and trusting each other, and being able to share the joys and sorrows of life.
So do you have friends like that now?
I have a few, but it always feels like it’s not enough. I used to have very few friends, but I didn’t think there was a problem. Why am I like this now?

Some people may need to interact with others to meet their psychological needs. It’s also possible that you’re being influenced by classmates around you and feeling like you’re not as good as they are.
Yes, I really want to interact with other people to pass the time, but I never know who to reach out to. Which do you think is more important, the number of friends or the quality of the friendships?

I think quality matters more than quantity. Friendship requires an investment of time and energy, rather than vague, superficial socializing. At the same time, finding close friends who share your interests and values is even more precious.
I also want to know, at age 20, how many close friends is it normal to have?

Actually, it’s hard to give one standard number for this. But according to Dunbar’s number, humans can maintain close to 150 social relationships, including 5 intimate friends, 15 good friends, and 50 friends.
I see. I still feel like I don’t have enough friends. Do you have any suggestions that could help me?

You could take part in more interest groups or activities and meet people who share your interests and values. At the same time, it’s also important to learn to enjoy being alone, and to focus more on your own growth and development.
Okay, thank you for your suggestions. I’ll try.
You’re welcome. I believe you can work through this. If you need anything else, feel free to chat with me anytime.
Lately I always feel like the atmosphere at home is really tense, especially my relationship with my mom. She always acts like she doesn’t trust me and doesn’t like me, and it really hurts.
It sounds like there’s been a problem with communication between you and your mom. Is it that, day to day, your communication isn’t very smooth, and that leaves you feeling misunderstood?
Yes. Every time I argue with my mom, it feels like we’re on completely different wavelengths.

This kind of situation is very common; I’ve experienced it too. But you know, the more you diss your mom, the more likely it is to backfire. I’d suggest finding a time when both you and your mom are in a good mood and there isn’t any conflict, and having a proper talk with her. Tell her how you really feel, let her know your thoughts and needs, and hopefully you can come to understand and support each other.
Then what if I find it hard to express my feelings, or I’m afraid my mom won’t understand me?

Don’t be afraid. Opening up to family isn’t easy. You can first try writing a letter, sending a message, or writing down your thoughts. Slowly, as you get more used to expressing your feelings, you can then try communicating with your mom face to face.
Mm, that sounds like a good method. I also know my mom is good to me, but I just can’t help losing my temper or crying. I want to know how I can control my emotions.

Try recording your emotional process. Every time you lose your temper or cry, first slowly write down your emotions, then find a quiet place, close your eyes, and take deep breaths to relax your body and mind. Tell yourself: I can control my emotions. I don’t want my emotions to affect me and my family. In this way, you can slowly learn to control your emotions.
Thank you for your suggestions. I’ll try to do that.
I hope this helps. Remember, don’t let your emotions affect you and your family anymore, okay? If there’s anything else you need help with, you can tell me anytime.

I’ve liked a lot of people before. In elementary school, middle school, high school, and even college. I don’t know if I’m just too fickle? Why have I liked so many people? And it often changes again and again. When I know there’s no possibility, I stop putting so much feeling into it.

It sounds like you’re feeling really sad. This may be because you’ve been looking for true love and haven’t found it yet. That doesn’t mean you’re fickle. I’ve heard a saying: “One of the most beautiful things in life is to love and be loved.” Maybe you just want to find the right person. Don’t worry—when you find them, you’ll know.
But once I like someone, it’s really hard for me to control my feelings. My feelings are always very intense, and they affect my quality of life.

It sounds like your inner self needs more comfort and support. Maybe you could try finding some healthy outlets, like slowly sharing your feelings with friends, or doing things you enjoy to shift your attention. This can help you manage your emotions better.
I’ve tried those things, but they don’t seem to have had any real effect. I’m really conflicted right now and don’t know what I should do.

Everyone’s situation is different. Maybe you need more time and professional guidance to work through this. If you keep feeling conflicted and uneasy, you could consider seeking help from a mental health professional.
I’ve never thought about seeing a psychologist. Wouldn’t that be really embarrassing?

Absolutely not! More and more people are getting help from psychologists to regulate their emotions and work through problems. Seeing a psychologist doesn’t mean there’s something wrong with you; it means you’re willing to make an effort to improve your emotional life. That’s a very brave step, and it deserves respect.
What you said makes a lot of sense. Maybe I really do need to find a psychologist to talk to. Thank you for your encouragement and support.
You’re welcome. I’m glad I could help. If you need any further help, or just want someone to listen, you can always come talk to me.
Lately people keep bringing up my old wounds. What should I do?

Hello. I understand how you feel. Everyone has their own wounds, and other people’s comments or exposing them can make us feel uncomfortable. But there are some ways we can handle this kind of pressure. For example, you could talk with people who have had similar experiences, or seek help from a professional counselor.
But I feel like when things get exposed, I become really vulnerable, and my emotions can easily get out of control.

That is a very normal feeling. To help balance your emotions, you may need some regulation skills, such as deep breathing, relaxing activities, listening to music, and so on. You can try different methods and find the one that works best for you.
I feel like it’s really hard to deal with this situation, and I feel kind of helpless.

Don’t give up on yourself. It may take more time and support to help you face this issue. You can talk more with people around you whom you trust, share your feelings, let them help you relieve the pressure, and also try to seek professional support.
I know that sounds meaningful, but I don’t know how to do it.

Try to honestly express your feelings to them, help them understand your situation, and discuss together how to solve the problem. You can also learn some effective communication skills to better express your thoughts and feelings.
I feel like what you’re saying makes a lot of sense, but I’m still really afraid of facing things being exposed.

You don’t have to force yourself. Some small steps may help you gradually adjust to this situation. For example, you could try not responding directly to questions or doubts that expose things, change the subject, or ask someone else for an answer. Over time, you will find that this situation no longer troubles you so much.
Thank you for your advice and support.
You’re welcome. We all may need help at certain times. Please remember that you are not alone, and that making a little progress each day is very important.

Every time it gets dark, my mood drops, and I really don’t know why. I suddenly feel bad, and unhappy things come along with it, like scene after scene of a movie replaying in my mind. Also, why do I always like to sit quietly by myself and zone out?
It sounds like you need comfort and understanding. So, tell me, can you describe the specific things that make you feel depressed and sad?
Actually, what I just described was just a feeling stirred up by my emotions. There wasn’t anything specific that caused it. But I really feel very sad. I feel like I don’t know what I want.

It sounds like you’re in a state of emotional confusion, and that’s very normal. You may need some time to better understand your feelings. Is there anything, or any activity, that you used to feel you liked?
I used to like playing all kinds of games, but now even the games I like can’t make me feel happy anymore.
Sometimes, when we’re in an emotional low point, we need to find new ways to meet our own needs. Maybe you could explore some new hobbies, like learning a new language or taking part in sports?
That suggestion is really good. I’ll try it. But I still feel lonely and sad. I feel like there are problems in my relationships, and I don’t know what to do.
Relationship problems are very common, and you’re definitely not the only person who has run into this. Is there anyone you could talk to about your feelings?
I don’t have very close friends, and I’m afraid to tell them. I feel like they won’t understand me, and might even laugh at me.
Sometimes, by seeking help from the outside, we can unexpectedly find the support we need. Would you consider trying to find a support group or a professional counselor you can talk to?
That’s a good idea. I’ll think about it. Thank you for your advice.
I’m glad I could help you. Remember, you’re not alone, and when you need it, please feel free to reach out to me for help anytime.
